  42class LowResGCMSExport:
  43    """A class to export low resolution GC-MS data.
  44
  45    This class provides methods to export low resolution GC-MS data to various formats such as Excel, CSV, Parquet, HDF5, and Pandas DataFrame.
  46
  47    Parameters:
  48    ----------
  49    out_file_path : str
  50        The output file path.
  51    gcms : object
  52        The low resolution GCMS object.
  53
  54    Attributes:
  55    ----------
  56    output_file : Path
  57        The output file path as a Path object.
  58    gcms : object
  59        The low resolution GCMS object.
  60
  61    Methods:
  62    -------
  63    * get_pandas_df(id_label="corems:"). Get the exported data as a Pandas DataFrame.
  64    * get_json(nan=False, id_label="corems:"). Get the exported data as a JSON string.
  65    * to_pandas(write_metadata=True, id_label="corems:"). Export the data to a Pandas DataFrame and save it as a pickle file.
  66    * to_excel(write_mode='a', write_metadata=True, id_label="corems:"),
  67        Export the data to an Excel file.
  68    * to_csv(separate_output=False, write_mode="w", write_metadata=True, id_label="corems:").
  69        Export the data to a CSV file.
  70    * to_parquet(write_metadata=True, id_label="corems:").
  71        Export the data to a Parquet file.
  72    * to_hdf(id_label="corems:").
  73        Export the data to an HDF5 file.
  74    * get_data_stats(gcms).
  75        Get statistics about the GCMS data.
  76
  77    """
  78

 141    def get_pandas_df(self, id_label="corems:"):
 142        """Get the exported data as a Pandas DataFrame.

 154

 209    def to_excel(self, write_mode="a", write_metadata=True, id_label="corems:"):
 210        """Export the data to an Excel file.
 211
 212        Parameters:
 213        ----------
 214        write_mode : str, optional
 215            The write mode for the Excel file. Default is 'a' (append).
 216        write_metadata : bool, optional
 217            Whether to write metadata to the output file. Default is True.
 218        id_label : str, optional
 219            The ID label for the data. Default is "corems:".
 220        """
 221
 222        out_put_path = self.output_file.with_suffix(".xlsx")
 223
 224        columns = self._init_columns()
 225
 226        dict_data_list = self.get_list_dict_data(self.gcms)
 227
 228        df = DataFrame(dict_data_list, columns=columns)
 229
 230        if write_mode == "a" and out_put_path.exists():
 231            writer = ExcelWriter(out_put_path, engine="openpyxl")
 232            # try to open an existing workbook
 233            writer.book = load_workbook(out_put_path)
 234            # copy existing sheets
 235            writer.sheets = dict((ws.title, ws) for ws in writer.book.worksheets)
 236            # read existing file
 237            reader = read_excel(out_put_path)
 238            # write out the new sheet
 239            df.to_excel(writer, index=False, header=False, startrow=len(reader) + 1)
 240
 241            writer.close()
 242        else:
 243            df.to_excel(
 244                self.output_file.with_suffix(".xlsx"), index=False, engine="openpyxl"
 245            )
 246
 247        if write_metadata:
 248            self.write_settings(out_put_path, self.gcms, id_label=id_label)
 249
 250    def to_csv(
 251        self,
 252        separate_output=False,
 253        write_mode="w",
 254        write_metadata=True,
 255        id_label="corems:",
 256    ):
 257        """Export the data to a CSV file.
 258
 259        Parameters:
 260        ----------
 261        separate_output : bool, optional
 262            Whether to separate the output into multiple files. Default is False.
 263        write_mode : str, optional
 264            The write mode for the CSV file. Default is 'w' (write).
 265        write_metadata : bool, optional
 266            Whether to write metadata to the output file. Default is True.
 267        id_label : str, optional
 268            The ID label for the data. Default is "corems:".
 269        """
 270
 271        if separate_output:
 272            # set write mode to write
 273            # this mode will overwrite the file without warning
 274            write_mode = "w"
 275        else:
 276            # set write mode to append
 277            write_mode = "a"
 278
 279        columns = self._init_columns()
 280
 281        dict_data_list = self.get_list_dict_data(self.gcms)
 282
 283        out_put_path = self.output_file.with_suffix(".csv")
 284
 285        write_header = not out_put_path.exists()
 286
 287        try:
 288            with open(out_put_path, write_mode, newline="") as csvfile:
 289                writer = csv.DictWriter(csvfile, fieldnames=columns)
 290                if write_header:
 291                    writer.writeheader()
 292                for data in dict_data_list:
 293                    writer.writerow(data)
 294
 295            if write_metadata:
 296                self.write_settings(out_put_path, self.gcms, id_label=id_label)
 297
 298        except IOError as ioerror:
 299            print(ioerror)
 300

 328    def to_hdf(self, id_label="corems:"):
 329        """Export the data to an HDF5 file.
 330
 331        Parameters:
 332        ----------
 333        id_label : str, optional
 334            The ID label for the data. Default is "corems:".
 335        """
 336
 337        # save sample at a time
 338        def add_compound(gc_peak, compound_obj):
 339            modifier = compound_obj.classify if compound_obj.classify else ""
 340            compound_group = compound_obj.name.replace("/", "") + " " + modifier
 341
 342            if compound_group not in peak_group:
 343                compound_group = peak_group.create_group(compound_group)
 344
 345                # compound_group.attrs["retention_time"] = compound_obj.retention_time
 346                compound_group.attrs["retention_index"] = compound_obj.ri
 347                compound_group.attrs["retention_index_score"] = compound_obj.ri_score
 348                compound_group.attrs["spectral_similarity_score"] = (
 349                    compound_obj.spectral_similarity_score
 350                )
 351                compound_group.attrs["similarity_score"] = compound_obj.similarity_score
 352
 353                compond_mz = compound_group.create_dataset(
 354                    "mz", data=np.array(compound_obj.mz), dtype="f8"
 355                )
 356                compond_abundance = compound_group.create_dataset(
 357                    "abundance", data=np.array(compound_obj.abundance), dtype="f8"
 358                )
 359
 360                if self.gcms.molecular_search_settings.exploratory_mode:
 361                    compound_group.attrs["Spectral Similarities"] = json.dumps(
 362                        compound_obj.spectral_similarity_scores,
 363                        sort_keys=False,
 364                        indent=4,
 365                        separators=(",", ":"),
 366                    )
 367            else:
 368                warnings.warn("Skipping duplicate reference compound.")
 369
 370        import json
 371        from datetime import datetime, timezone
 372
 373        import h5py
 374        import numpy as np
 375
 376        output_path = self.output_file.with_suffix(".hdf5")
 377
 378        with h5py.File(output_path, "w") as hdf_handle:
 379            timenow = str(datetime.now(timezone.utc).strftime("%d/%m/%Y %H:%M:%S %Z"))
 380            hdf_handle.attrs["time_stamp"] = timenow
 381            hdf_handle.attrs["data_structure"] = "gcms"
 382            hdf_handle.attrs["analyzer"] = self.gcms.analyzer
 383            hdf_handle.attrs["instrument_label"] = self.gcms.instrument_label
 384
 385            hdf_handle.attrs["sample_id"] = "self.gcms.id"
 386            hdf_handle.attrs["sample_name"] = self.gcms.sample_name
 387            hdf_handle.attrs["input_data"] = str(self.gcms.file_location)
 388            hdf_handle.attrs["output_data"] = str(output_path)
 389            hdf_handle.attrs["output_data_id"] = id_label + uuid.uuid4().hex
 390            hdf_handle.attrs["corems_version"] = __version__
 391
 392            hdf_handle.attrs["Stats"] = json.dumps(
 393                self.get_data_stats(self.gcms),
 394                sort_keys=False,
 395                indent=4,
 396                separators=(",", ": "),
 397            )
 398            hdf_handle.attrs["Calibration"] = json.dumps(
 399                self.get_calibration_stats(self.gcms, id_label),
 400                sort_keys=False,
 401                indent=4,
 402                separators=(",", ": "),
 403            )
 404            hdf_handle.attrs["Blank"] = json.dumps(
 405                self.get_blank_stats(self.gcms),
 406                sort_keys=False,
 407                indent=4,
 408                separators=(",", ": "),
 409            )
 410
 411            corems_dict_setting = parameter_to_dict.get_dict_data_gcms(self.gcms)
 412            hdf_handle.attrs["CoreMSParameters"] = json.dumps(
 413                corems_dict_setting, sort_keys=False, indent=4, separators=(",", ": ")
 414            )
 415
 416            scans_dataset = hdf_handle.create_dataset(
 417                "scans", data=np.array(self.gcms.scans_number), dtype="f8"
 418            )
 419            rt_dataset = hdf_handle.create_dataset(
 420                "rt", data=np.array(self.gcms.retention_time), dtype="f8"
 421            )
 422            tic_dataset = hdf_handle.create_dataset(
 423                "tic", data=np.array(self.gcms.tic), dtype="f8"
 424            )
 425            processed_tic_dataset = hdf_handle.create_dataset(
 426                "processed_tic", data=np.array(self.gcms.processed_tic), dtype="f8"
 427            )
 428
 429            output_score_method = (
 430                self.gcms.molecular_search_settings.output_score_method
 431            )
 432
 433            for gc_peak in self.gcms:
 434                # print(gc_peak.retention_time)
 435                # print(gc_peak.tic)
 436
 437                # check if there is a compound candidate
 438                peak_group = hdf_handle.create_group(str(gc_peak.retention_time))
 439                peak_group.attrs["deconvolution"] = int(
 440                    self.gcms.chromatogram_settings.use_deconvolution
 441                )
 442
 443                peak_group.attrs["start_scan"] = gc_peak.start_scan
 444                peak_group.attrs["apex_scan"] = gc_peak.apex_scan
 445                peak_group.attrs["final_scan"] = gc_peak.final_scan
 446
 447                peak_group.attrs["retention_index"] = gc_peak.ri
 448                peak_group.attrs["retention_time"] = gc_peak.retention_time
 449                peak_group.attrs["area"] = gc_peak.area
 450
 451                mz = peak_group.create_dataset(
 452                    "mz", data=np.array(gc_peak.mass_spectrum.mz_exp), dtype="f8"
 453                )
 454                abundance = peak_group.create_dataset(
 455                    "abundance",
 456                    data=np.array(gc_peak.mass_spectrum.abundance),
 457                    dtype="f8",
 458                )
 459
 460                if gc_peak:
 461                    if output_score_method == "highest_sim_score":
 462                        compound_obj = gc_peak.highest_score_compound
 463                        add_compound(gc_peak, compound_obj)
 464
 465                    elif output_score_method == "highest_ss":
 466                        compound_obj = gc_peak.highest_ss_compound
 467                        add_compound(gc_peak, compound_obj)
 468
 469                    else:
 470                        for compound_obj in gc_peak:
 471                            add_compound(gc_peak, compound_obj)

 473    def get_data_stats(self, gcms):
 474        """Get statistics about the GCMS data.
 475
 476        Parameters:
 477        ----------
 478        gcms : object
 479            The low resolution GCMS object.
 480
 481        Returns:
 482        -------
 483        dict
 484            A dictionary containing the data statistics.
 485        """
 486
 487        matched_peaks = gcms.matched_peaks
 488        no_matched_peaks = gcms.no_matched_peaks
 489        unique_metabolites = gcms.unique_metabolites
 490
 491        peak_matchs_above_0p85 = 0
 492        unique_peak_match_above_0p85 = 0
 493        for match_peak in matched_peaks:
 494            gc_peak_above_85 = 0
 495            matches_above_85 = list(
 496                filter(lambda m: m.similarity_score >= 0.85, match_peak)
 497            )
 498            if matches_above_85:
 499                peak_matchs_above_0p85 += 1
 500            if len(matches_above_85) == 1:
 501                unique_peak_match_above_0p85 += 1
 502
 503        data_stats = {}
 504        data_stats["average_signal_noise"] = "ni"
 505        data_stats["chromatogram_dynamic_range"] = gcms.dynamic_range
 506        data_stats["total_number_peaks"] = len(gcms)
 507        data_stats["total_peaks_matched"] = len(matched_peaks)
 508        data_stats["total_peaks_without_matches"] = len(no_matched_peaks)
 509        data_stats["total_matches_above_similarity_score_0.85"] = peak_matchs_above_0p85
 510        data_stats["single_matches_above_similarity_score_0.85"] = (
 511            unique_peak_match_above_0p85
 512        )
 513        data_stats["unique_metabolites"] = len(unique_metabolites)
 514
 515        return data_stats
 516

 555    def get_data_metadata(self, gcms, id_label, output_path):
 556        """Get metadata about the GC-MS data.
 557
 558        Parameters:
 559        ----------
 560        gcms : object
 561            The low resolution GCMS object.
 562        id_label : str
 563            The ID label for the data.
 564        output_path : str
 565            The output file path.
 566
 567        Returns:
 568        -------
 569        dict
 570            A dictionary containing the data metadata.
 571        """
 572        if isinstance(output_path, str):
 573            output_path = Path(output_path)
 574
 575        paramaters_path = output_path.with_suffix(".json")
 576
 577        if paramaters_path.exists():
 578            with paramaters_path.open() as current_param:
 579                metadata = json.load(current_param)
 580                data_metadata = metadata.get("Data")
 581        else:
 582            data_metadata = {}
 583            data_metadata["data_name"] = []
 584            data_metadata["input_data_url"] = []
 585            data_metadata["has_input"] = []
 586
 587        data_metadata["data_name"].append(gcms.sample_name)
 588        data_metadata["input_data_url"].append(str(gcms.file_location))
 589        data_metadata["has_input"].append(id_label + corems_md5(gcms.file_location))
 590
 591        data_metadata["output_data_name"] = str(output_path.stem)
 592        data_metadata["output_data_url"] = str(output_path)
 593        data_metadata["has_output"] = id_label + corems_md5(output_path)
 594
 595        return data_metadata
 596
 597    def get_parameters_json(self, gcms, id_label, output_path):
 598        """Get the parameters as a JSON string.
 599
 600        Parameters:
 601        ----------
 602        gcms : GCMS object
 603            The low resolution GCMS object.
 604        id_label : str
 605            The ID label for the data.
 606        output_path : str
 607            The output file path.
 608
 609        Returns:
 610        -------
 611        str
 612            The parameters as a JSON string.
 613        """
 614
 615        output_parameters_dict = {}
 616        output_parameters_dict["Data"] = self.get_data_metadata(
 617            gcms, id_label, output_path
 618        )
 619        output_parameters_dict["Stats"] = self.get_data_stats(gcms)
 620        output_parameters_dict["Calibration"] = self.get_calibration_stats(
 621            gcms, id_label
 622        )
 623        output_parameters_dict["Blank"] = self.get_blank_stats(gcms)
 624        output_parameters_dict["Instrument"] = self.get_instrument_metadata(gcms)
 625        corems_dict_setting = parameter_to_dict.get_dict_data_gcms(gcms)
 626        corems_dict_setting["corems_version"] = __version__
 627        output_parameters_dict["CoreMSParameters"] = corems_dict_setting
 628        output_parameters_dict["has_metabolite"] = gcms.metabolites_data
 629        output = json.dumps(
 630            output_parameters_dict, sort_keys=False, indent=4, separators=(",", ": ")
 631        )
 632
 633        return output
 634
 635    def write_settings(self, output_path, gcms, id_label="emsl:"):
 636        """Write the settings to a JSON file.
 637
 638        Parameters:
 639        ----------
 640        output_path : str
 641            The output file path.
 642        gcms : GCMS object
 643            The low resolution GCMS object.
 644        id_label : str
 645            The ID label for the data. Default is "emsl:".
 646
 647        """
 648
 649        output = self.get_parameters_json(gcms, id_label, output_path)
 650
 651        with open(
 652            output_path.with_suffix(".json"),
 653            "w",
 654            encoding="utf8",
 655        ) as outfile:
 656            outfile.write(output)
 657
 658    def get_list_dict_data(self, gcms, include_no_match=True, no_match_inline=False):
 659        """Get the exported data as a list of dictionaries.
 660
 661        Parameters:
 662        ----------
 663        gcms : object
 664            The low resolution GCMS object.
 665        include_no_match : bool, optional
 666            Whether to include no match data. Default is True.
 667        no_match_inline : bool, optional
 668            Whether to include no match data inline. Default is False.
 669
 670        Returns:
 671        -------
 672        list
 673            The exported data as a list of dictionaries.
 674        """
 675
 676        output_score_method = gcms.molecular_search_settings.output_score_method
 677
 678        dict_data_list = []
 679
 680        def add_match_dict_data():
 681            derivatization = "{}:{}:{}".format(
 682                compound_obj.classify,
 683                compound_obj.derivativenum,
 684                compound_obj.derivatization,
 685            )
 686            out_dict = {
 687                "Sample name": gcms.sample_name,
 688                "Peak Index": gcpeak_index,
 689                "Retention Time": gc_peak.retention_time,
 690                "Retention Time Ref": compound_obj.retention_time,
 691                "Peak Height": gc_peak.tic,
 692                "Peak Area": gc_peak.area,
 693                "Retention index": gc_peak.ri,
 694                "Retention index Ref": compound_obj.ri,
 695                "Retention Index Score": compound_obj.ri_score,
 696                "Spectral Similarity Score": compound_obj.spectral_similarity_score,
 697                "Similarity Score": compound_obj.similarity_score,
 698                "Compound Name": compound_obj.name,
 699                "Chebi ID": compound_obj.metadata.chebi,
 700                "Kegg Compound ID": compound_obj.metadata.kegg,
 701                "Inchi": compound_obj.metadata.inchi,
 702                "Inchi Key": compound_obj.metadata.inchikey,
 703                "Smiles": compound_obj.metadata.smiles,
 704                "Molecular Formula": compound_obj.formula,
 705                "IUPAC Name": compound_obj.metadata.iupac_name,
 706                "Traditional Name": compound_obj.metadata.traditional_name,
 707                "Common Name": compound_obj.metadata.common_name,
 708                "Derivatization": derivatization,
 709            }
 710
 711            if self.gcms.molecular_search_settings.exploratory_mode:
 712                out_dict.update(
 713                    {
 714                        "Weighted Cosine Correlation": compound_obj.spectral_similarity_scores.get(
 715                            "weighted_cosine_correlation"
 716                        ),
 717                        "Cosine Correlation": compound_obj.spectral_similarity_scores.get(
 718                            "cosine_correlation"
 719                        ),
 720                        "Stein Scott Similarity": compound_obj.spectral_similarity_scores.get(
 721                            "stein_scott_similarity"
 722                        ),
 723                        "Pearson Correlation": compound_obj.spectral_similarity_scores.get(
 724                            "pearson_correlation"
 725                        ),
 726                        "Spearman Correlation": compound_obj.spectral_similarity_scores.get(
 727                            "spearman_correlation"
 728                        ),
 729                        "Kendall Tau Correlation": compound_obj.spectral_similarity_scores.get(
 730                            "kendall_tau_correlation"
 731                        ),
 732                        "DFT Correlation": compound_obj.spectral_similarity_scores.get(
 733                            "dft_correlation"
 734                        ),
 735                        "DWT Correlation": compound_obj.spectral_similarity_scores.get(
 736                            "dwt_correlation"
 737                        ),
 738                        "Euclidean Distance": compound_obj.spectral_similarity_scores.get(
 739                            "euclidean_distance"
 740                        ),
 741                        "Manhattan Distance": compound_obj.spectral_similarity_scores.get(
 742                            "manhattan_distance"
 743                        ),
 744                        "Jaccard Distance": compound_obj.spectral_similarity_scores.get(
 745                            "jaccard_distance"
 746                        ),
 747                    }
 748                )
 749                for method in methods_name:
 750                    out_dict[methods_name.get(method)] = (
 751                        compound_obj.spectral_similarity_scores.get(method)
 752                    )
 753
 754            dict_data_list.append(out_dict)
 755
 756        def add_no_match_dict_data():
 757            dict_data_list.append(
 758                {
 759                    "Sample name": gcms.sample_name,
 760                    "Peak Index": gcpeak_index,
 761                    "Retention Time": gc_peak.retention_time,
 762                    "Peak Height": gc_peak.tic,
 763                    "Peak Area": gc_peak.area,
 764                    "Retention index": gc_peak.ri,
 765                }
 766            )
 767
 768        for gcpeak_index, gc_peak in enumerate(gcms.sorted_gcpeaks):
 769            # check if there is a compound candidate
 770            if gc_peak:
 771                if output_score_method == "highest_sim_score":
 772                    compound_obj = gc_peak.highest_score_compound
 773                    add_match_dict_data()
 774
 775                elif output_score_method == "highest_ss":
 776                    compound_obj = gc_peak.highest_ss_compound
 777                    add_match_dict_data()
 778
 779                else:
 780                    for compound_obj in gc_peak:
 781                        add_match_dict_data()  # add monoisotopic peak
 782
 783            else:
 784                # include not_match
 785                if include_no_match and no_match_inline:
 786                    add_no_match_dict_data()
 787
 788        if include_no_match and not no_match_inline:
 789            for gcpeak_index, gc_peak in enumerate(gcms.sorted_gcpeaks):
 790                if not gc_peak:
 791                    add_no_match_dict_data()
 792
 793        return dict_data_list
 794
 795
 796class HighResMassSpectraExport(HighResMassSpecExport):
 797    """A class to export high resolution mass spectra data.
 798
 799    This class provides methods to export high resolution mass spectra data to various formats
 800    such as Excel, CSV, Parquet, HDF5, and Pandas DataFrame.
 801
 802    Parameters
 803    ----------
 804    out_file_path : str | Path
 805        The output file path.
 806    mass_spectra : object
 807        The high resolution mass spectra object.
 808    output_type : str, optional
 809        The output type. Default is 'excel'.
 810
 811    Attributes
 812    ----------
 813    output_file : Path
 814        The output file path without suffix
 815    dir_loc : Path
 816        The directory location for the output file,
 817        by default this will be the output_file + ".corems" and all output files will be
 818        written into this location
 819    mass_spectra : MassSpectraBase
 820        The high resolution mass spectra object.
 821    """
 822
 823    def __init__(self, out_file_path, mass_spectra, output_type="excel"):
 824        super().__init__(
 825            out_file_path=out_file_path, mass_spectrum=None, output_type=output_type
 826        )
 827
 828        self.dir_loc = Path(out_file_path + ".corems")
 829        self.dir_loc.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
 830        # Place the output file in the directory
 831        self.output_file = self.dir_loc / Path(out_file_path).name
 832        self._output_type = output_type  # 'excel', 'csv', 'pandas', 'parquet' or 'hdf5'
 833        self.mass_spectra = mass_spectra
 834        self.atoms_order_list = None
 835        self._init_columns()
 836
 837    def get_pandas_df(self):
 838        """Get the mass spectra as a list of Pandas DataFrames."""
 839
 840        list_df = []
 841
 842        for mass_spectrum in self.mass_spectra:
 843            columns = self.columns_label + self.get_all_used_atoms_in_order(
 844                mass_spectrum
 845            )
 846
 847            dict_data_list = self.get_list_dict_data(mass_spectrum)
 848
 849            df = DataFrame(dict_data_list, columns=columns)
 850
 851            scan_number = mass_spectrum.scan_number
 852
 853            df.attrs["name"] = str(self.output_file) + "_" + str(scan_number)
 854
 855            list_df.append(df)
 856
 857        return list_df

 859    def to_pandas(self, write_metadata=True):
 860        """Export the data to a Pandas DataFrame and save it as a pickle file.
 861
 862        Parameters:
 863        ----------
 864        write_metadata : bool, optional
 865            Whether to write metadata to the output file. Default is True.

 867
 868        for mass_spectrum in self.mass_spectra:
 869            columns = self.columns_label + self.get_all_used_atoms_in_order(

 873            dict_data_list = self.get_list_dict_data(mass_spectrum)

 877            scan_number = mass_spectrum.scan_number
 878
 879            out_filename = Path(

 883            df.to_pickle(self.dir_loc / out_filename)

 885            if write_metadata:

 988    def get_mass_spectra_attrs(self):
 989        """Get the mass spectra attributes as a JSON string.

 998        str

1000        """
1001        dict_ms_attrs = {}
1002        dict_ms_attrs["analyzer"] = self.mass_spectra.analyzer
1003        dict_ms_attrs["instrument_label"] = self.mass_spectra.instrument_label

1005
1006        return json.dumps(
1007            dict_ms_attrs, sort_keys=False, indent=4, separators=(",", ": ")

1009
1010    def to_hdf(
1011        self,
1012        overwrite=False,
1013        export_raw=True,
1014        compression=DEFAULT_HDF5_COMPRESSION,
1015        profile_dtype="f4",
1016    ):
1017        """Export the data to an HDF5 file.
1018
1019        Parameters
1020        ----------
1021        overwrite : bool, optional
1022            Whether to overwrite the output file. Default is False.
1023        export_raw : bool, optional
1024            Whether to export the raw mass spectra data. Default is True.
1025        compression : int, str or None, optional
1026            Compression for the written datasets: a gzip level 0-9,
1027            ``"lzf"``, or ``None``/``"none"``. Default is 4. ``"lzf"`` is
1028            h5py's own filter, not a standard HDF5 one -- it needs h5py (or
1029            a tool with the lzf plugin) to read the result back.
1030        profile_dtype : str, optional
1031            dtype used for the stored profile m/z/abundance arrays
1032            (``"f4"`` or ``"f8"``). Default is ``"f4"``.
1033        """
1034        if overwrite:
1035            if self.output_file.with_suffix(".hdf5").exists():
1036                self.output_file.with_suffix(".hdf5").unlink()
1037
1038        with h5py.File(self.output_file.with_suffix(".hdf5"), "a") as hdf_handle:
1039            if not hdf_handle.attrs.get("date_utc"):
1040                # Set metadata for all mass spectra
1041                timenow = str(
1042                    datetime.now(timezone.utc).strftime("%d/%m/%Y %H:%M:%S %Z")
1043                )
1044                hdf_handle.attrs["date_utc"] = timenow
1045                hdf_handle.attrs["filename"] = self.mass_spectra.file_location.name
1046                hdf_handle.attrs["data_structure"] = "mass_spectra"
1047                hdf_handle.attrs["analyzer"] = self.mass_spectra.analyzer
1048                hdf_handle.attrs["instrument_label"] = (
1049                    self.mass_spectra.instrument_label
1050                )
1051                hdf_handle.attrs["sample_name"] = self.mass_spectra.sample_name
1052                hdf_handle.attrs["polarity"] = self.mass_spectra.polarity
1053                hdf_handle.attrs["parser_type"] = (
1054                    self.mass_spectra.spectra_parser_class.__name__
1055                )
1056                hdf_handle.attrs["original_file_location"] = (
1057                    self.mass_spectra.file_location._str
1058                )
1059
1060                # Save creation time from the cached parser when one is configured.
1061                try:
1062                    if (
1063                        getattr(self.mass_spectra, "spectra_parser_class", None)
1064                        is not None
1065                    ):
1066                        parser = self.mass_spectra.spectra_parser
1067                        if parser is not None and hasattr(parser, "get_creation_time"):
1068                            creation_time = parser.get_creation_time()
1069                            if creation_time is not None:
1070                                hdf_handle.attrs["creation_time"] = (
1071                                    creation_time.isoformat()
1072                                )
1073                except Exception:
1074                    pass  # If creation time cannot be retrieved, skip it
1075
1076            if "mass_spectra" not in hdf_handle:
1077                mass_spectra_group = hdf_handle.create_group("mass_spectra")
1078            else:
1079                mass_spectra_group = hdf_handle.get("mass_spectra")
1080
1081            for mass_spectrum in self.mass_spectra:
1082                group_key = str(int(mass_spectrum.scan_number))
1083
1084                self.add_mass_spectrum_to_hdf5(
1085                    hdf_handle,
1086                    mass_spectrum,
1087                    group_key,
1088                    mass_spectra_group,
1089                    export_raw,
1090                    compression=compression,
1091                    profile_dtype=profile_dtype,
1092                )
1093
1094
1095class LCMSExport(HighResMassSpectraExport):
1096    """A class to export high resolution LC-MS data.
1097
1098    This class provides methods to export high resolution LC-MS data to HDF5
1099    and Parquet (tabular datasets that mirror the main HDF5 groups).
1100
1101    Parameters
1102    ----------
1103    out_file_path : str | Path
1104        The output file path, do not include the file extension.
1105    lcms_object : LCMSBase
1106        The high resolution lc-ms object.
1107    """
1108
1109    def __init__(self, out_file_path, mass_spectra):
1110        super().__init__(out_file_path, mass_spectra, output_type="hdf5")
1111
1112    @staticmethod
1113    def _prepare_df_for_parquet(df):
1114        """Make a DataFrame Parquet-safe by normalizing nested/mixed object values.
1115
1116        Parameters
1117        ----------
1118        df : DataFrame
1119            Input dataframe.
1120
1121        Returns
1122        -------
1123        DataFrame
1124            Copy suitable for ``DataFrame.to_parquet``.
1125
1126        Notes
1127        -----
1128        Object columns with mixed Python types (especially ``bool`` mixed with
1129        ``int``) fail under pyarrow. Nested containers are JSON-serialized;
1130        mixed scalar object columns are coerced to a single type or strings.
1131        """
1132        if df is None or df.empty:
1133            return df
1134
1135        out = df.copy()
1136        out.columns = [str(c) for c in out.columns]
1137
1138        for col in out.columns:
1139            series = out[col]
1140            if series.dtype != object:
1141                continue
1142
1143            def _normalize(value):
1144                if value is None:
1145                    return None
1146                try:
1147                    # Avoid treating array-likes as NA; only scalar NA checks
1148                    if not isinstance(
1149                        value, (list, tuple, dict, np.ndarray)
1150                    ) and pd.isna(value):
1151                        return None
1152                except (TypeError, ValueError):
1153                    pass
1154                if isinstance(value, (list, tuple, dict)):
1155                    return json.dumps(value)
1156                if isinstance(value, np.ndarray):
1157                    return json.dumps(value.tolist())
1158                if isinstance(value, (bool, np.bool_)):
1159                    return bool(value)
1160                if isinstance(value, (np.integer,)):
1161                    return int(value)
1162                if isinstance(value, (np.floating,)):
1163                    return float(value)
1164                return value
1165
1166            normalized = series.map(_normalize)
1167            non_null = [v for v in normalized.tolist() if v is not None]
1168
1169            has_bool = any(isinstance(v, bool) for v in non_null)
1170            # bool is a subclass of int; exclude bools from int detection
1171            has_int = any(
1172                isinstance(v, int) and not isinstance(v, bool) for v in non_null
1173            )
1174            has_float = any(isinstance(v, float) for v in non_null)
1175            has_str = any(isinstance(v, str) for v in non_null)
1176            has_other = any(
1177                not isinstance(v, (bool, int, float, str)) for v in non_null
1178            )
1179
1180            if (
1181                has_other
1182                or (has_str and (has_bool or has_int or has_float))
1183                or (has_bool and has_int)
1184            ):
1185                out[col] = normalized.map(lambda v: None if v is None else str(v))
1186            elif has_bool and not has_float:
1187                out[col] = normalized.map(
1188                    lambda v: None if v is None else bool(v)
1189                ).astype("boolean")
1190            elif has_float or has_int:
1191                out[col] = pd.to_numeric(pd.Series(normalized), errors="coerce")
1192            else:
1193                out[col] = normalized.map(lambda v: None if v is None else str(v))
1194
1195        return out
1196
1197    def _write_parquet(self, df, filename, overwrite=False):
1198        """Write a dataframe to a Parquet file under the export directory.
1199
1200        Parameters
1201        ----------
1202        df : DataFrame
1203            Data to write.
1204        filename : str
1205            File name (with or without ``.parquet`` suffix).
1206        overwrite : bool, optional
1207            Whether to replace an existing file. Default is False.
1208
1209        Returns
1210        -------
1211        Path or None
1212            Output path if written, otherwise None.
1213        """
1214        if df is None or df.empty:
1215            return None
1216
1217        out_path = self.dir_loc / Path(filename).with_suffix(".parquet")
1218        if out_path.exists() and not overwrite:
1219            return out_path
1220
1221        self._prepare_df_for_parquet(df).to_parquet(out_path, index=False)
1222        return out_path
1223
1224    def _mass_spectra_to_parquet_df(self):
1225        """Build a single DataFrame of peak tables for all loaded mass spectra."""
1226        frames = []
1227        for mass_spectrum in self.mass_spectra:
1228            if mass_spectrum is None:
1229                continue
1230            columns = self.columns_label + self.get_all_used_atoms_in_order(
1231                mass_spectrum
1232            )
1233            dict_data_list = self.get_list_dict_data(mass_spectrum)
1234            df = DataFrame(dict_data_list, columns=columns)
1235            if df.empty:
1236                continue
1237            df.insert(0, "scan_number", mass_spectrum.scan_number)
1238            if getattr(mass_spectrum, "retention_time", None) is not None:
1239                df.insert(1, "retention_time", mass_spectrum.retention_time)
1240            frames.append(df)
1241
1242        if not frames:
1243            return DataFrame()
1244        return pd.concat(frames, ignore_index=True)
1245
1246    @staticmethod
1247    def _sequence_len(value):
1248        """Return length of a sequence/array, or 0 for None/empty/scalar-missing."""
1249        if value is None:
1250            return 0
1251        try:
1252            return len(value)
1253        except TypeError:
1254            return 0
1255
1256    def _eics_to_parquet_df(self):
1257        """Build a long-format DataFrame of EIC time series."""
1258        frames = []
1259        for mz, eic_data in self.mass_spectra.eics.items():
1260            if eic_data is None:
1261                continue
1262            # Avoid `array or []` — numpy arrays are ambiguous in boolean context
1263            time = getattr(eic_data, "time", None)
1264            n = self._sequence_len(time)
1265            if n == 0:
1266                continue
1267
1268            scans = getattr(eic_data, "scans", None)
1269            eic = getattr(eic_data, "eic", None)
1270            eic_smoothed = getattr(eic_data, "eic_smoothed", None)
1271
1272            frame = {
1273                "mz": [mz] * n,
1274                "scans": list(scans) if self._sequence_len(scans) == n else [None] * n,
1275                "time": list(time),
1276                "eic": list(eic) if self._sequence_len(eic) == n else [None] * n,
1277            }
1278            if self._sequence_len(eic_smoothed) == n:
1279                frame["eic_smoothed"] = list(eic_smoothed)
1280            frames.append(DataFrame(frame))
1281
1282        if not frames:
1283            return DataFrame()
1284        return pd.concat(frames, ignore_index=True)
1285
1286    def _spectral_search_results_to_parquet_df(self):
1287        """Flatten spectral search results into a single DataFrame."""
1288        frames = []
1289        for scan_id, by_precursor in self.mass_spectra.spectral_search_results.items():
1290            for precursor_key, result in by_precursor.items():
1291                try:
1292                    df = result.to_dataframe()
1293                except Exception:
1294                    continue
1295                if df is None or df.empty:
1296                    continue
1297                df = df.copy()
1298                # to_dataframe() already includes these fields from the result object;
1299                # only set them when missing so we do not insert duplicate columns.
1300                if "query_spectrum_id" not in df.columns:
1301                    df.insert(
1302                        0,
1303                        "query_spectrum_id",
1304                        getattr(result, "query_spectrum_id", scan_id),
1305                    )
1306                if "precursor_mz" not in df.columns:
1307                    loc = 1 if "query_spectrum_id" in df.columns else 0
1308                    df.insert(
1309                        loc,
1310                        "precursor_mz",
1311                        getattr(result, "precursor_mz", precursor_key),
1312                    )
1313                frames.append(df)
1314
1315        if not frames:
1316            return DataFrame()
1317        return pd.concat(frames, ignore_index=True)
1318
1319    def to_parquet(
1320        self,
1321        overwrite=False,
1322        save_parameters=True,
1323        parameter_format="toml",
1324        export_spectra=True,
1325    ):
1326        """Export LC-MS datasets to Parquet files (tabular mirror of ``to_hdf``).
1327
1328        Writes under ``{out_file_path}.corems/``:
1329
1330        - ``scan_info.parquet``
1331        - ``mass_features.parquet``
1332        - ``induced_mass_features.parquet`` (if present)
1333        - ``mass_spectra.parquet`` (optional; all peak tables with scan metadata)
1334        - ``eics.parquet`` (if EICs are present and export is enabled)
1335        - ``spectral_search_results.parquet`` (if search results are present)
1336        - parameters as JSON or TOML when ``save_parameters`` is True
1337
1338        Parameters
1339        ----------
1340        overwrite : bool, optional
1341            Whether to overwrite existing Parquet files. Default is False.
1342        save_parameters : bool, optional
1343            Whether to save processing parameters. Default is True.
1344        parameter_format : str, optional
1345            Parameter file format, ``'json'`` or ``'toml'``. Default is ``'toml'``.
1346        export_spectra : bool, optional
1347            Whether to export loaded mass-spectrum peak tables. Default is True.
1348
1349        Notes
1350        -----
1351        Requires ``pyarrow`` (or ``fastparquet``) for pandas Parquet I/O.
1352        Raw profile arrays and nested HDF5-only blobs are not reproduced in full;
1353        use ``to_hdf`` for a complete self-contained archive.
1354        """
1355        self.dir_loc.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
1356
1357        # Scan metadata (same source as the HDF5 scan_info group)
1358        scan_df = self.mass_spectra.scan_df
1359        if scan_df is not None and not scan_df.empty:
1360            self._write_parquet(
1361                scan_df.reset_index(drop=True), "scan_info", overwrite=overwrite
1362            )
1363
1364        # Mass features
1365        if len(self.mass_spectra.mass_features) > 0:
1366            mf_df = self.mass_spectra.mass_features_to_df().reset_index(drop=False)
1367            self._write_parquet(mf_df, "mass_features", overwrite=overwrite)
1368
1369        if len(getattr(self.mass_spectra, "induced_mass_features", {}) or {}) > 0:
1370            imf_df = self.mass_spectra.mass_features_to_df(
1371                induced_features=True
1372            ).reset_index(drop=False)
1373            self._write_parquet(imf_df, "induced_mass_features", overwrite=overwrite)
1374
1375        # Peak tables for loaded spectra
1376        if export_spectra:
1377            spectra_df = self._mass_spectra_to_parquet_df()
1378            self._write_parquet(spectra_df, "mass_spectra", overwrite=overwrite)
1379
1380        # EICs
1381        export_eics = self.mass_spectra.parameters.lc_ms.export_eics
1382        if export_eics and len(self.mass_spectra.eics) > 0:
1383            eic_df = self._eics_to_parquet_df()
1384            self._write_parquet(eic_df, "eics", overwrite=overwrite)
1385
1386        # Spectral search results
1387        if len(self.mass_spectra.spectral_search_results) > 0:
1388            search_df = self._spectral_search_results_to_parquet_df()
1389            self._write_parquet(
1390                search_df, "spectral_search_results", overwrite=overwrite
1391            )
1392
1393        if save_parameters:
1394            if parameter_format not in ["json", "toml"]:
1395                raise ValueError("parameter_format must be 'json' or 'toml'")
1396            if parameter_format == "json":
1397                dump_lcms_settings_json(
1398                    filename=self.output_file.with_suffix(".json"),
1399                    lcms_obj=self.mass_spectra,
1400                )
1401            elif parameter_format == "toml":
1402                dump_lcms_settings_toml(
1403                    filename=self.output_file.with_suffix(".toml"),
1404                    lcms_obj=self.mass_spectra,
1405                )
1406
1407    @staticmethod
1408    def _save_mass_features_dict_to_hdf5(
1409        mass_features_dict,
1410        mass_features_group,
1411        overwrite=False,
1412        compression=DEFAULT_HDF5_COMPRESSION,
1413    ):
1414        """Save a dictionary of mass features to an HDF5 group.
1415
1416        This is a helper method that can be reused by different export classes.
1417
1418        Parameters
1419        ----------
1420        mass_features_dict : dict
1421            Dictionary of mass features to save, keyed by mass feature ID.
1422        mass_features_group : h5py.Group
1423            The HDF5 group to save the mass features to.
1424        overwrite : bool, optional
1425            Whether to overwrite existing mass features. Default is False.
1426        compression : int, str or None, optional
1427            Compression for the written datasets: a gzip level 0-9,
1428            ``"lzf"``, or ``None``/``"none"``. Default is 4. ``"lzf"`` is
1429            h5py's own filter, not a standard HDF5 one -- it needs h5py (or
1430            a tool with the lzf plugin) to read the result back.
1431        """
1432
1433        # Create group for each mass feature, with key as the mass feature id
1434        for k, v in mass_features_dict.items():
1435            if str(k) not in mass_features_group or overwrite:
1436                if str(k) in mass_features_group and overwrite:
1437                    del mass_features_group[str(k)]
1438                mass_features_group.create_group(str(k))
1439                # Loop through each of the mass feature attributes and add them as attributes (if single value) or datasets (if array)
1440                for k2, v2 in v.__dict__.items():
1441                    if v2 is not None:
1442                        # Check if the attribute is an integer or float and set as an attribute in the mass feature group
1443                        if k2 not in [
1444                            "chromatogram_parent",
1445                            "ms2_mass_spectra",
1446                            "mass_spectrum",
1447                            "_eic_data",
1448                            "ms2_similarity_results",
1449                        ]:
1450                            if k2 == "ms2_scan_numbers":
1451                                array = np.array(v2)
1452                                # Convert int64 to int32
1453                                if array.dtype == np.int64:
1454                                    array = array.astype(np.int32)
1455                                mass_features_group[str(k)].create_dataset(
1456                                    str(k2),
1457                                    data=array,
1458                                    **hdf5_dataset_kwargs(
1459                                        array.shape, compression=compression
1460                                    ),
1461                                )
1462                            elif k2 == "_half_height_width":
1463                                array = np.array(v2)
1464                                # Convert float64 to float32
1465                                if array.dtype == np.float64:
1466                                    array = array.astype(np.float32)
1467                                mass_features_group[str(k)].create_dataset(
1468                                    str(k2),
1469                                    data=array,
1470                                    **hdf5_dataset_kwargs(
1471                                        array.shape, compression=compression
1472                                    ),
1473                                )
1474                            elif k2 == "_ms_deconvoluted_idx":
1475                                array = np.array(v2)
1476                                # Convert int64 to int32
1477                                if array.dtype == np.int64:
1478                                    array = array.astype(np.int32)
1479                                mass_features_group[str(k)].create_dataset(
1480                                    str(k2),
1481                                    data=array,
1482                                    **hdf5_dataset_kwargs(
1483                                        array.shape, compression=compression
1484                                    ),
1485                                )
1486                            elif k2 == "associated_mass_features_deconvoluted":
1487                                array = np.array(v2)
1488                                # Convert int64 to int32
1489                                if array.dtype == np.int64:
1490                                    array = array.astype(np.int32)
1491                                mass_features_group[str(k)].create_dataset(
1492                                    str(k2),
1493                                    data=array,
1494                                    **hdf5_dataset_kwargs(
1495                                        array.shape, compression=compression
1496                                    ),
1497                                )
1498                            elif k2 == "_noise_score":
1499                                array = np.array(v2)
1500                                # Convert float64 to float32
1501                                if array.dtype == np.float64:
1502                                    array = array.astype(np.float32)
1503                                mass_features_group[str(k)].create_dataset(
1504                                    str(k2),
1505                                    data=array,
1506                                    **hdf5_dataset_kwargs(
1507                                        array.shape, compression=compression
1508                                    ),
1509                                )
1510                            elif (
1511                                isinstance(v2, int)
1512                                or isinstance(v2, float)
1513                                or isinstance(v2, str)
1514                                or isinstance(v2, np.integer)
1515                                or isinstance(v2, np.float32)
1516                                or isinstance(v2, np.float64)
1517                                or isinstance(v2, np.bool_)
1518                            ):
1519                                # Convert numpy types to smaller precision for storage
1520                                if isinstance(v2, np.int64):
1521                                    v2 = np.int32(v2)
1522                                elif isinstance(v2, np.float64):
1523                                    v2 = np.float32(v2)
1524                                mass_features_group[str(k)].attrs[str(k2)] = v2
1525
1526    @staticmethod
1527    def _save_eics_dict_to_hdf5(
1528        eics_dict, eics_group, overwrite=False, compression=DEFAULT_HDF5_COMPRESSION
1529    ):
1530        """Save a dictionary of EICs to an HDF5 group.
1531
1532        This is a static helper method that can be reused by different export classes
1533        to save EIC data in a consistent format.
1534
1535        Parameters
1536        ----------
1537        eics_dict : dict
1538            Dictionary of EIC_Data objects, keyed by m/z value.
1539        eics_group : h5py.Group
1540            The HDF5 group to save the EICs to.
1541        overwrite : bool, optional
1542            Whether to overwrite existing EICs. Default is False.
1543        compression : int, str or None, optional
1544            Compression for the written datasets: a gzip level 0-9,
1545            ``"lzf"``, or ``None``/``"none"``. Default is 4. ``"lzf"`` is
1546            h5py's own filter, not a standard HDF5 one -- it needs h5py (or
1547            a tool with the lzf plugin) to read the result back.
1548        """
1549        for mz, eic_data in eics_dict.items():
1550            mz_str = str(mz)
1551            if mz_str not in eics_group or overwrite:
1552                if mz_str in eics_group and overwrite:
1553                    del eics_group[mz_str]
1554                eic_grp = eics_group.create_group(mz_str)
1555                eic_grp.attrs["mz"] = mz
1556
1557                # Save all EIC_Data attributes as datasets
1558                for attr_name, attr_value in eic_data.__dict__.items():
1559                    if attr_value is not None:
1560                        array = np.array(attr_value)
1561                        # Apply data type optimization and compression
1562                        if array.dtype == np.int64:
1563                            array = array.astype(np.int32)
1564                        elif array.dtype == np.float64:
1565                            array = array.astype(np.float32)
1566                        elif array.dtype.str[0:2] == "<U":
1567                            # Convert Unicode strings to UTF-8 encoded strings
1568                            string_data = [str(item) for item in array]
1569                            string_dtype = h5py.string_dtype(encoding="utf-8")
1570                            eic_grp.create_dataset(
1571                                str(attr_name),
1572                                data=string_data,
1573                                dtype=string_dtype,
1574                                **hdf5_dataset_kwargs(
1575                                    array.shape, compression=compression, vlen_str=True
1576                                ),
1577                            )
1578                            continue
1579                        eic_grp.create_dataset(
1580                            str(attr_name),
1581                            data=array,
1582                            **hdf5_dataset_kwargs(array.shape, compression=compression),
1583                        )
1584
1585    def _save_mass_features_to_hdf5(
1586        self,
1587        hdf_handle,
1588        group_name="mass_features",
1589        overwrite=False,
1590        compression=DEFAULT_HDF5_COMPRESSION,
1591    ):
1592        """Save the mass features to the HDF5 file.
1593
1594        Parameters
1595        ----------
1596        hdf_handle : h5py.File
1597            The HDF5 file handle.
1598        group_name : str, optional
1599            The name of the group to save the mass features to. Default is 'mass_features'.
1600        overwrite : bool, optional
1601            Whether to overwrite the group if it exists. Default is False.
1602        compression : int, str or None, optional
1603            Compression for the written datasets: a gzip level 0-9,
1604            ``"lzf"``, or ``None``/``"none"``. Default is 4. ``"lzf"`` is
1605            h5py's own filter, not a standard HDF5 one -- it needs h5py (or
1606            a tool with the lzf plugin) to read the result back.
1607        """
1608        # Determine which mass features to save based on group_name
1609        if group_name == "induced_mass_features":
1610            if len(self.mass_spectra.induced_mass_features) == 0:
1611                return  # No induced mass features to save
1612            mass_features_dict = self.mass_spectra.induced_mass_features
1613        else:
1614            if len(self.mass_spectra.mass_features) == 0:
1615                return  # No mass features to save
1616            mass_features_dict = self.mass_spectra.mass_features
1617
1618        # Add LCMS mass features to hdf5 file
1619        if group_name not in hdf_handle:
1620            mass_features_group = hdf_handle.create_group(group_name)
1621        else:
1622            mass_features_group = hdf_handle.get(group_name)
1623
1624        # Use the static helper method to save the mass features
1625        self._save_mass_features_dict_to_hdf5(
1626            mass_features_dict, mass_features_group, overwrite, compression=compression
1627        )
1628
1629    def to_hdf(
1630        self,
1631        overwrite=False,
1632        save_parameters=True,
1633        parameter_format="toml",
1634        compression=DEFAULT_HDF5_COMPRESSION,
1635        profile_dtype="f4",
1636    ):
1637        """Export the data to an HDF5.
1638
1639        Parameters
1640        ----------
1641        overwrite : bool, optional
1642            Whether to overwrite the output file. Default is False.
1643        save_parameters : bool, optional
1644            Whether to save the parameters as a separate json or toml file. Default is True.
1645        parameter_format : str, optional
1646            The format to save the parameters in. Default is 'toml'.
1647        compression : int, str or None, optional
1648            Compression for the written datasets: a gzip level 0-9,
1649            ``"lzf"``, or ``None``/``"none"``. Default is 4. ``"lzf"`` is
1650            h5py's own filter, not a standard HDF5 one -- it needs h5py (or
1651            a tool with the lzf plugin) to read the result back.
1652        profile_dtype : str, optional
1653            dtype used for the stored profile m/z and abundance arrays
1654            (``"f4"`` or ``"f8"``). Default is ``"f4"``.
1655
1656        Raises
1657        ------
1658        ValueError
1659            If parameter_format is not 'json' or 'toml'.
1660        """
1661        export_profile_spectra = (
1662            self.mass_spectra.parameters.lc_ms.export_profile_spectra
1663        )
1664
1665        # Write the mass spectra data to the hdf5 file
1666        super().to_hdf(
1667            overwrite=overwrite,
1668            export_raw=export_profile_spectra,
1669            compression=compression,
1670            profile_dtype=profile_dtype,
1671        )
1672
1673        # Write scan info, ms_unprocessed, mass features, eics, and ms2_search results to the hdf5 file
1674        with h5py.File(self.output_file.with_suffix(".hdf5"), "a") as hdf_handle:
1675            # Add scan_info to hdf5 file
1676            if "scan_info" not in hdf_handle or overwrite:
1677                if "scan_info" in hdf_handle and overwrite:
1678                    del hdf_handle["scan_info"]
1679                scan_info_group = hdf_handle.create_group("scan_info")
1680                for k, v in self.mass_spectra._scan_info.items():
1681                    array = np.array(list(v.values()))
1682                    if array.dtype.str[0:2] == "<U":
1683                        array = array.astype("S")
1684                    scan_info_group.create_dataset(
1685                        k,
1686                        data=array,
1687                        **hdf5_dataset_kwargs(array.shape, compression=compression),
1688                    )
1689
1690            # Add ms_unprocessed to hdf5 file
1691            export_unprocessed_ms1 = (
1692                self.mass_spectra.parameters.lc_ms.export_unprocessed_ms1
1693            )
1694            if self.mass_spectra._ms_unprocessed and export_unprocessed_ms1:
1695                if "ms_unprocessed" not in hdf_handle or overwrite:
1696                    if "ms_unprocessed" in hdf_handle and overwrite:
1697                        del hdf_handle["ms_unprocessed"]
1698                    ms_unprocessed_group = hdf_handle.create_group("ms_unprocessed")
1699                else:
1700                    ms_unprocessed_group = hdf_handle.get("ms_unprocessed")
1701                for k, v in self.mass_spectra._ms_unprocessed.items():
1702                    if str(k) not in ms_unprocessed_group or overwrite:
1703                        if str(k) in ms_unprocessed_group and overwrite:
1704                            del ms_unprocessed_group[str(k)]
1705                        array = np.array(v)
1706                        column_labels = (
1707                            list(v.columns)
1708                            if hasattr(v, "columns")
1709                            else ["scan", "mz", "intensity"]
1710                        )
1711                        ms_dset = ms_unprocessed_group.create_dataset(
1712                            str(k),
1713                            data=array,
1714                            **hdf5_dataset_kwargs(array.shape, compression=compression),
1715                        )
1716                        ms_dset.attrs["column_labels"] = json.dumps(column_labels)
1717
1718            # Add LCMS mass features to hdf5 file
1719            self._save_mass_features_to_hdf5(
1720                hdf_handle,
1721                group_name="mass_features",
1722                overwrite=overwrite,
1723                compression=compression,
1724            )
1725            self._save_mass_features_to_hdf5(
1726                hdf_handle,
1727                group_name="induced_mass_features",
1728                overwrite=overwrite,
1729                compression=compression,
1730            )
1731
1732            # Add EIC data to hdf5 file
1733            export_eics = self.mass_spectra.parameters.lc_ms.export_eics
1734            if len(self.mass_spectra.eics) > 0 and export_eics:
1735                if "eics" not in hdf_handle or overwrite:
1736                    if "eics" in hdf_handle and overwrite:
1737                        del hdf_handle["eics"]
1738                    eic_group = hdf_handle.create_group("eics")
1739                else:
1740                    eic_group = hdf_handle.get("eics")
1741
1742                # Use the static helper method to save the EICs
1743                self._save_eics_dict_to_hdf5(
1744                    self.mass_spectra.eics,
1745                    eic_group,
1746                    overwrite,
1747                    compression=compression,
1748                )
1749
1750            # Add ms2_search results to hdf5 file (parameterized)
1751            if len(self.mass_spectra.spectral_search_results) > 0:
1752                if "spectral_search_results" not in hdf_handle or overwrite:
1753                    if "spectral_search_results" in hdf_handle and overwrite:
1754                        del hdf_handle["spectral_search_results"]
1755                    spectral_search_results = hdf_handle.create_group(
1756                        "spectral_search_results"
1757                    )
1758                else:
1759                    spectral_search_results = hdf_handle.get("spectral_search_results")
1760                # Create group for each search result by ms2_scan / precursor_mz
1761                for k, v in self.mass_spectra.spectral_search_results.items():
1762                    # TODO KRH: Fix to handle if export_only_relevant and k not in relevant_scan_numbers: continue!
1763                    if str(k) not in spectral_search_results or overwrite:
1764                        if str(k) in spectral_search_results and overwrite:
1765                            del spectral_search_results[str(k)]
1766                        spectral_search_results.create_group(str(k))
1767                        for k2, v2 in v.items():
1768                            spectral_search_results[str(k)].create_group(str(k2))
1769                            spectral_search_results[str(k)][str(k2)].attrs[
1770                                "precursor_mz"
1771                            ] = v2.precursor_mz
1772                            spectral_search_results[str(k)][str(k2)].attrs[
1773                                "query_spectrum_id"
1774                            ] = v2.query_spectrum_id
1775                            # Loop through each of the attributes and add them as datasets (if array)
1776                            for k3, v3 in v2.__dict__.items():
1777                                if v3 is not None and k3 not in [
1778                                    "query_spectrum",
1779                                    "precursor_mz",
1780                                    "query_spectrum_id",
1781                                ]:
1782                                    if (
1783                                        k3 == "query_frag_types"
1784                                        or k3 == "ref_frag_types"
1785                                    ):
1786                                        v3 = [", ".join(x) for x in v3]
1787                                    if all(v3 is not None for v3 in v3):
1788                                        array = np.array(v3)
1789                                    if array.dtype.str[0:2] == "<U":
1790                                        array = array.astype("S")
1791                                    spectral_search_results[str(k)][
1792                                        str(k2)
1793                                    ].create_dataset(
1794                                        str(k3),
1795                                        data=array,
1796                                        **hdf5_dataset_kwargs(
1797                                            array.shape, compression=compression
1798                                        ),
1799                                    )
1800
1801            # Save parameters as separate json
1802            if save_parameters:
1803                # Check if parameter_format is valid
1804                if parameter_format not in ["json", "toml"]:
1805                    raise ValueError("parameter_format must be 'json' or 'toml'")
1806
1807                if parameter_format == "json":
1808                    dump_lcms_settings_json(
1809                        filename=self.output_file.with_suffix(".json"),
1810                        lcms_obj=self.mass_spectra,
1811                    )
1812                elif parameter_format == "toml":
1813                    dump_lcms_settings_toml(
1814                        filename=self.output_file.with_suffix(".toml"),
1815                        lcms_obj=self.mass_spectra,
1816                    )
1817

1819class LCMSMetabolomicsExport(LCMSExport):
1820    """A class to export LCMS metabolite data.
1821
1822    This class provides methods to export LCMS metabolite data to various formats
1823    (CSV/Parquet reports, HDF5) and summarize the metabolite report.
1824
1825    Parameters
1826    ----------
1827    out_file_path : str | Path
1828        The output file path, do not include the file extension.
1829    mass_spectra : object
1830        The high resolution mass spectra object.
1831    """
1832
1833    def __init__(self, out_file_path, mass_spectra):
1834        super().__init__(out_file_path, mass_spectra)
1835        self.ion_type_dict = MolecularFormulaCalc.ion_type_dict
1836
1837    @staticmethod
1838    def get_ion_formula(neutral_formula, ion_type):
1839        """From a neutral formula and an ion type, return the formula of the ion.
1840
1841        Notes
1842        -----
1843        Delegates to
1844        :meth:`corems.molecular_formula.calc.MolecularFormulaCalc.MolecularFormulaCalc.get_ion_formula`.
1845
1846        Parameters
1847        ----------
1848        neutral_formula : str
1849            The neutral formula, this should be a string form from the MolecularFormula class
1850            (e.g. 'C2 H4 O2', isotopes OK), or simple string (e.g. 'C2H4O2', no isotope handling in this case).
1851            In the case of a simple string, the atoms are parsed based on the presence of capital letters,
1852            e.g. MgCl2 is parsed as 'Mg Cl2.
1853        ion_type : str
1854            The ion type, e.g. 'protonated', '[M+H]+', '[M+Na]+', etc.
1855            See ``MolecularFormulaCalc.ion_type_dict`` for the available ion types.
1856
1857        Returns
1858        -------
1859        str
1860            The formula of the ion as a string (like 'C2 H4 O2'); or None if the neutral_formula is not a string.
1861        """
1862        return MolecularFormulaCalc.get_ion_formula(neutral_formula, ion_type)
1863
1864    @staticmethod
1865    def precursor_mz_from_formula(neutral_formula, ion_type, charge=None):
1866        """Calculated precursor m/z from neutral formula and adduct / ion type.
1867
1868        Notes
1869        -----
1870        Delegates to
1871        :meth:`corems.molecular_formula.calc.MolecularFormulaCalc.MolecularFormulaCalc.precursor_mz_from_formula`.
1872        """
1873        return MolecularFormulaCalc.precursor_mz_from_formula(
1874            neutral_formula, ion_type, charge=charge
1875        )
1876
1877    @staticmethod
1878    def get_isotope_type(ion_formula):
1879        """From an ion formula, return the 13C isotope type of the ion.
1880
1881        Notes
1882        -----
1883        This is a static method.
1884        If the ion_formula is not a string, this method will return None.
1885        This is currently only functional for 13C isotopes.
1886
1887        Parameters
1888        ----------
1889        ion_formula : str
1890            The formula of the ion, expected to be a string like 'C2 H4 O2'.
1891
1892        Returns
1893        -------
1894        str
1895            The isotope type of the ion, e.g. '13C1', '13C2', etc; or None if the ion_formula does not contain a 13C isotope.
1896
1897        Raises
1898        ------
1899        ValueError
1900            If the ion_formula is not a string.
1901        """
1902        if not isinstance(ion_formula, str):
1903            return None
1904
1905        if re.search(r"\s", ion_formula):
1906            ion_formula = MolecularFormula(ion_formula, ion_charge=0)
1907        else:
1908            raise ValueError('ion_formula should be a string like "C2 H4 O2"')
1909        ion_formula_dict = ion_formula.to_dict().copy()
1910
1911        try:
1912            iso_class = "13C" + str(ion_formula_dict.pop("13C"))
1913        except KeyError:
1914            iso_class = None
1915
1916        return iso_class
1917
1918    def report_to_csv(self, molecular_metadata=None):
1919        """Create a report of the mass features and their annotations and save it as a CSV file.
1920
1921        Parameters
1922        ----------
1923        molecular_metadata : dict, optional
1924            The molecular metadata. Default is None.
1925        """
1926        report = self.to_report(molecular_metadata=molecular_metadata)
1927        out_file = self.output_file.with_suffix(".csv")
1928        report.to_csv(out_file, index=False)
1929
1930    def report_to_parquet(self, molecular_metadata=None):
1931        """Create a report of the mass features and their annotations and save it as a Parquet file.
1932
1933        Parameters
1934        ----------
1935        molecular_metadata : dict, optional
1936            The molecular metadata. Default is None.
1937
1938        Notes
1939        -----
1940        Requires ``pyarrow`` (or ``fastparquet``) for pandas Parquet I/O.
1941        Shared by metabolomics and lipidomics exporters via inheritance.
1942        """
1943        report = self.to_report(molecular_metadata=molecular_metadata)
1944        out_file = self.output_file.with_suffix(".parquet")
1945        report.to_parquet(out_file, index=False)
1946
1947    def clean_ms1_report(self, ms1_summary_full):
1948        """Clean the MS1 report.
1949
1950        Parameters
1951        ----------
1952        ms1_summary_full : DataFrame
1953            The full MS1 summary DataFrame.
1954
1955        Returns
1956        -------
1957        DataFrame
1958            The cleaned MS1 summary DataFrame.
1959        """
1960        ms1_summary_full = ms1_summary_full.reset_index()
1961        cols_to_keep = [
1962            "mf_id",
1963            "Molecular Formula",
1964            "Ion Type",
1965            "Calculated m/z",
1966            "m/z Error (ppm)",
1967            "m/z Error Score",
1968            "Is Isotopologue",
1969            "Isotopologue Similarity",
1970            "Confidence Score",
1971        ]
1972        ms1_summary = ms1_summary_full[cols_to_keep].copy()
1973        ms1_summary["ion_formula"] = [
1974            self.get_ion_formula(f, a)
1975            for f, a in zip(ms1_summary["Molecular Formula"], ms1_summary["Ion Type"])
1976        ]
1977        ms1_summary["isotopologue_type"] = [
1978            self.get_isotope_type(f) for f in ms1_summary["ion_formula"].tolist()
1979        ]
1980
1981        # Keep MS1 neutral Molecular Formula so it is not confused with library formulas
1982        # from MS2 spectral metadata.
1983        ms1_summary = ms1_summary[
1984            [
1985                "mf_id",
1986                "ion_formula",
1987                "isotopologue_type",
1988                "Molecular Formula",
1989                "Calculated m/z",
1990                "m/z Error (ppm)",
1991                "m/z Error Score",
1992                "Isotopologue Similarity",
1993                "Confidence Score",
1994            ]
1995        ]
1996
1997        # Set the index to mf_id
1998        ms1_summary = ms1_summary.set_index("mf_id")
1999
2000        return ms1_summary
2001
2002    def summarize_ms2_report(self, ms2_annot_report):
2003        """
2004        Summarize the MS2 report.
2005
2006        Parameters
2007        ----------
2008        ms2_annot_report : DataFrame
2009            The MS2 annotation DataFrame with all annotations, output of mass_features_ms2_annot_to_df.
2010
2011        Returns
2012        -------
2013        """
2014
2015    def summarize_metabolomics_report(self, ms2_annot_report):
2016        """Summarize the MS2 hits for a metabolomics report
2017
2018        Parameters
2019        ----------
2020        ms2_annot : DataFrame
2021            The MS2 annotation DataFrame with all annotations.
2022
2023        Returns
2024        -------
2025        DataFrame
2026            The summarized metabolomics report.
2027        """
2028        columns_to_drop = [
2029            "precursor_mz",
2030            "precursor_mz_error_ppm",
2031            "cas",
2032            "data_id",
2033            "iupac_name",
2034            "traditional_name",
2035            "common_name",
2036            "casno",
2037        ]
2038        ms2_annot = ms2_annot_report.drop(
2039            columns=[col for col in columns_to_drop if col in ms2_annot_report.columns]
2040        )
2041
2042        # Prepare information about the search results, pulling out the best hit for the single report
2043        # Group by mf_id,ref_mol_id grab row with highest entropy similarity
2044        ms2_annot = ms2_annot.reset_index()
2045        # Add column called "n_spectra_contributing" that is the number of unique values in query_spectrum_id per mf_id,ref_mol_id
2046        ms2_annot["n_spectra_contributing"] = ms2_annot.groupby(
2047            ["mf_id", "ref_mol_id"]
2048        )["query_spectrum_id"].transform("nunique")
2049        # Sort by entropy similarity
2050        ms2_annot = ms2_annot.sort_values(
2051            by=["mf_id", "ref_mol_id", "entropy_similarity"],
2052            ascending=[True, True, False],
2053        )
2054        best_entropy = ms2_annot.drop_duplicates(
2055            subset=["mf_id", "ref_mol_id"], keep="first"
2056        )
2057
2058        return best_entropy
2059
2060    def clean_ms2_report(self, metabolite_summary):
2061        """Clean the MS2 report.
2062
2063        Parameters
2064        ----------
2065        metabolite_summary : DataFrame
2066            The full metabolomics summary DataFrame.
2067
2068        Returns
2069        -------
2070        DataFrame
2071            The cleaned metabolomics summary DataFrame.
2072        """
2073        metabolite_summary = metabolite_summary.reset_index()
2074        # Library (MS2 metadata) formulas — keep separate from MS1 search fields
2075        metabolite_summary["library_ion_formula"] = [
2076            self.get_ion_formula(f, a)
2077            for f, a in zip(
2078                metabolite_summary["formula"], metabolite_summary["ref_ion_type"]
2079            )
2080        ]
2081        metabolite_summary = metabolite_summary.rename(
2082            columns={"formula": "library_formula"}
2083        )
2084
2085        col_order = [
2086            "mf_id",
2087            "library_ion_formula",
2088            "ref_ion_type",
2089            "library_formula",
2090            "inchikey",
2091            "name",
2092            "inchi",
2093            "chebi",
2094            "smiles",
2095            "kegg",
2096            "cas",
2097            "database_name",
2098            "ref_ms_id",
2099            "entropy_similarity",
2100            "ref_mz_in_query_fract",
2101            "n_spectra_contributing",
2102        ]
2103
2104        # Reorder columns
2105        metabolite_summary = metabolite_summary[
2106            [col for col in col_order if col in metabolite_summary.columns]
2107        ]
2108
2109        # Convert chebi (if present) to int:
2110        if "chebi" in metabolite_summary.columns:
2111            metabolite_summary["chebi"] = metabolite_summary["chebi"].astype(
2112                "Int64", errors="ignore"
2113            )
2114
2115        # Set the index to mf_id
2116        metabolite_summary = metabolite_summary.set_index("mf_id")
2117
2118        return metabolite_summary
2119
2120    def combine_reports(self, mf_report, ms1_annot_report, ms2_annot_report):
2121        """Combine the mass feature report with the MS1 and MS2 reports.
2122
2123        Parameters
2124        ----------
2125        mf_report : DataFrame
2126            The mass feature report DataFrame.
2127        ms1_annot_report : DataFrame
2128            The MS1 annotation report DataFrame.
2129        ms2_annot_report : DataFrame
2130            The MS2 annotation report DataFrame.
2131
2132        Notes
2133        -----
2134        ``Molecular Formula`` / ``Ion Formula`` come only from MS1 molecular
2135        formula search. MS2 spectral library formulas are exposed as
2136        ``Library Molecular Formula`` / ``Library Ion Formula``.
2137        When MS1 and MS2 match (same ion formula), the library formula columns
2138        are cleared so they do not repeat the MS1 values on that row.
2139        """
2140        # If there is an ms1_annot_report, merge it with the mf_report
2141        if ms1_annot_report is not None and not ms1_annot_report.empty:
2142            # MS1 has been run and has molecular formula information
2143            mf_report = pd.merge(
2144                mf_report,
2145                ms1_annot_report,
2146                how="left",
2147                on=["mf_id", "isotopologue_type"],
2148            )
2149        if ms2_annot_report is not None:
2150            # Prefer joining MS2 hits to matching MS1 ion formula when both exist.
2151            # MS2 uses library_ion_formula so MS1 Ion Formula is not overwritten.
2152            if (
2153                "ion_formula" in mf_report.columns
2154                and "library_ion_formula" in ms2_annot_report.columns
2155            ):
2156                # pull out the records without ion_formula and merge on mf_id only
2157                mf_no_ion_formula = mf_report[mf_report["ion_formula"].isna()]
2158                mf_no_ion_formula = (
