2159                    mf_no_ion_formula.drop(columns=["ion_formula"])
2160                    if "ion_formula" in mf_no_ion_formula.columns
2161                    else mf_no_ion_formula
2162                )
2163                mf_no_ion_formula = pd.merge(
2164                    mf_no_ion_formula, ms2_annot_report, how="left", on=["mf_id"]
2165                )
2166
2167                # pull out the records with ion_formula and merge on mf_id + formula match
2168                mf_with_ion_formula = mf_report[~mf_report["ion_formula"].isna()]
2169                mf_with_ion_formula = pd.merge(
2170                    mf_with_ion_formula,
2171                    ms2_annot_report,
2172                    how="left",
2173                    left_on=["mf_id", "ion_formula"],
2174                    right_on=["mf_id", "library_ion_formula"],
2175                )
2176
2177                # put back together
2178                mf_report = pd.concat([mf_no_ion_formula, mf_with_ion_formula])
2179            else:
2180                # Fall back to merging on mf_id only (robust when ion_formula missing)
2181                mf_report = pd.merge(
2182                    mf_report, ms2_annot_report, how="left", on=["mf_id"]
2183                )
2184
2185        # Rename colums
2186        rename_dict = {
2187            "mf_id": "Mass Feature ID",
2188            "scan_time": "Retention Time (min)",
2189            "mz": "m/z",
2190            "apex_scan": "Apex Scan Number",
2191            "intensity": "Intensity",
2192            "persistence": "Persistence",
2193            "area": "Area",
2194            "half_height_width": "Half Height Width (min)",
2195            "tailing_factor": "Tailing Factor",
2196            "dispersity_index": "Dispersity Index",
2197            "ms2_spectrum": "MS2 Spectrum",
2198            "monoisotopic_mf_id": "Monoisotopic Mass Feature ID",
2199            "isotopologue_type": "Isotopologue Type",
2200            "mass_spectrum_deconvoluted_parent": "Is Largest Ion after Deconvolution",
2201            "associated_mass_features": "Associated Mass Features after Deconvolution",
2202            "ion_formula": "Ion Formula",
2203            "library_ion_formula": "Library Ion Formula",
2204            "library_formula": "Library Molecular Formula",
2205            "ref_ion_type": "Library Ion Type",
2206            "annot_level": "Lipid Annotation Level",
2207            "lipid_molecular_species_id": "Lipid Molecular Species",
2208            "lipid_summed_name": "Lipid Species",
2209            "lipid_subclass": "Lipid Subclass",
2210            "lipid_class": "Lipid Class",
2211            "lipid_category": "Lipid Category",
2212            "entropy_similarity": "Entropy Similarity",
2213            "ref_mz_in_query_fract": "Library mzs in Query (fraction)",
2214            "n_spectra_contributing": "Spectra with Annotation (n)",
2215        }
2216        mf_report = mf_report.rename(columns=rename_dict)
2217
2218        # When MS1 and MS2 co-annotate the same ion/molecular formula, library formula
2219        # columns only repeat MS1 fields — clear them so the row is not redundant.
2220        # Keep Library * columns populated for MS2-only (or mismatched) hits.
2221        if (
2222            "Ion Formula" in mf_report.columns
2223            and "Library Ion Formula" in mf_report.columns
2224        ):
2225            ion_match = (
2226                mf_report["Ion Formula"].notna()
2227                & mf_report["Library Ion Formula"].notna()
2228                & (mf_report["Ion Formula"] == mf_report["Library Ion Formula"])
2229            )
2230            mf_report.loc[ion_match, "Library Ion Formula"] = pd.NA
2231            if "Library Molecular Formula" in mf_report.columns:
2232                mf_report.loc[ion_match, "Library Molecular Formula"] = pd.NA
2233        elif (
2234            "Molecular Formula" in mf_report.columns
2235            and "Library Molecular Formula" in mf_report.columns
2236        ):
2237            mol_match = (
2238                mf_report["Molecular Formula"].notna()
2239                & mf_report["Library Molecular Formula"].notna()
2240                & (
2241                    mf_report["Molecular Formula"]
2242                    == mf_report["Library Molecular Formula"]
2243                )
2244            )
2245            mf_report.loc[mol_match, "Library Molecular Formula"] = pd.NA
2246            if "Library Ion Formula" in mf_report.columns:
2247                mf_report.loc[mol_match, "Library Ion Formula"] = pd.NA
2248
2249        mf_report["Sample Name"] = self.mass_spectra.sample_name
2250        mf_report["Polarity"] = self.mass_spectra.polarity
2251        mf_report = mf_report[
2252            ["Mass Feature ID", "Sample Name", "Polarity"]
2253            + [
2254                col
2255                for col in mf_report.columns
2256                if col not in ["Mass Feature ID", "Sample Name", "Polarity"]
2257            ]
2258        ]
2259
2260        # Reorder rows by "Mass Feature ID", then "Entropy Similarity" (descending), then "Confidence Score" (descending)
2261        if (
2262            "Entropy Similarity" in mf_report.columns
2263            and "Confidence Score" in mf_report.columns
2264        ):
2265            mf_report = mf_report.sort_values(
2266                by=["Mass Feature ID", "Entropy Similarity", "Confidence Score"],
2267                ascending=[True, False, False],
2268            )
2269        elif "Entropy Similarity" in mf_report.columns:
2270            mf_report = mf_report.sort_values(
2271                by=["Mass Feature ID", "Entropy Similarity"],
2272                ascending=[True, False],
2273            )
2274        elif "Confidence Score" in mf_report.columns:
2275            mf_report = mf_report.sort_values(
2276                by=["Mass Feature ID", "Confidence Score"],
2277                ascending=[True, False],
2278            )
2279        # If neither "Entropy Similarity" nor "Confidence Score" are in the columns, just sort by "Mass Feature ID"
2280        else:
2281            mf_report = mf_report.sort_values("Mass Feature ID")
2282
2283        # Reset index
2284        mf_report = mf_report.reset_index(drop=True)
2285
2286        return mf_report
2287
2288    def to_report(self, molecular_metadata=None, suppress_warnings=False):
2289        """Create a report of the mass features and their annotations.
2290
2291        Parameters
2292        ----------
2293        molecular_metadata : dict, optional
2294            The molecular metadata. Default is None.
2295        suppress_warnings : bool, optional
2296            If True, suppresses warnings from mass_features_ms2_annot_to_df.
2297            Default is False.
2298
2299        Returns
2300        -------
2301        DataFrame
2302            The report as a Pandas DataFrame.
2303        """
2304        # Get mass feature dataframe
2305        mf_report = self.mass_spectra.mass_features_to_df()
2306        mf_report = mf_report.reset_index(drop=False)
2307
2308        # Get and clean ms1 annotation dataframe
2309        ms1_annot_report = self.mass_spectra.mass_features_ms1_annot_to_df(
2310            suppress_warnings=suppress_warnings
2311        )
2312        if ms1_annot_report is not None:
2313            ms1_annot_report = ms1_annot_report.copy()
2314            ms1_annot_report = self.clean_ms1_report(ms1_annot_report)
2315            ms1_annot_report = ms1_annot_report.reset_index(drop=False)
2316        else:
2317            ms1_annot_report = None
2318
2319        # Get, summarize, and clean ms2 annotation dataframe
2320        ms2_annot_report = self.mass_spectra.mass_features_ms2_annot_to_df(
2321            molecular_metadata=molecular_metadata, suppress_warnings=suppress_warnings
2322        )
2323        if ms2_annot_report is not None and molecular_metadata is not None:
2324            ms2_annot_report = self.summarize_metabolomics_report(ms2_annot_report)
2325            ms2_annot_report = self.clean_ms2_report(ms2_annot_report)
2326            ms2_annot_report = ms2_annot_report.dropna(axis=1, how="all")
2327            ms2_annot_report = ms2_annot_report.reset_index(drop=False)
2328        else:
2329            ms2_annot_report = None
2330
2331        report = self.combine_reports(
2332            mf_report=mf_report,
2333            ms1_annot_report=ms1_annot_report,
2334            ms2_annot_report=ms2_annot_report,
2335        )
2336
2337        return report
2338
2339
2340class LipidomicsExport(LCMSMetabolomicsExport):
2341    """A class to export lipidomics data.
2342
2343    This class provides methods to export lipidomics data to various formats
2344    (CSV/Parquet reports, HDF5) and summarize the lipid report.
2345
2346    Parameters
2347    ----------
2348    out_file_path : str | Path
2349        The output file path, do not include the file extension.
2350    mass_spectra : object
2351        The high resolution mass spectra object.
2352    """
2353
2354    def __init__(self, out_file_path, mass_spectra):
2355        super().__init__(out_file_path, mass_spectra)
2356
2357    def summarize_lipid_report(self, ms2_annot):
2358        """Summarize the lipid report.
2359
2360        Parameters
2361        ----------
2362        ms2_annot : DataFrame
2363            The MS2 annotation DataFrame with all annotations.
2364
2365        Returns
2366        -------
2367        DataFrame
2368            The summarized lipid report.
2369        """
2370        # Drop unnecessary columns for easier viewing
2371        columns_to_drop = [
2372            "precursor_mz",
2373            "precursor_mz_error_ppm",
2374            "ref_mol_id",
2375            "ref_precursor_mz",
2376            "cas",
2377            "inchikey",
2378            "inchi",
2379            "chebi",
2380            "smiles",
2381            "kegg",
2382            "data_id",
2383            "iupac_name",
2384            "traditional_name",
2385            "common_name",
2386            "casno",
2387        ]
2388        ms2_annot = ms2_annot.drop(
2389            columns=[col for col in columns_to_drop if col in ms2_annot.columns]
2390        )
2391
2392        # If ion_types_excluded is not empty, remove those ion types
2393        ion_types_excluded = self.mass_spectra.parameters.mass_spectrum[
2394            "ms2"
2395        ].molecular_search.ion_types_excluded
2396        if len(ion_types_excluded) > 0:
2397            ms2_annot = ms2_annot[~ms2_annot["ref_ion_type"].isin(ion_types_excluded)]
2398
2399        # If mf_id is not present, check that the index name is mf_id and reset the index
2400        if "mf_id" not in ms2_annot.columns:
2401            if ms2_annot.index.name == "mf_id":
2402                ms2_annot = ms2_annot.reset_index()
2403            else:
2404                raise ValueError("mf_id is not present in the dataframe")
2405
2406        # Attempt to get consensus annotations to the MLF level
2407        mlf_results_all = []
2408        for mf_id in ms2_annot["mf_id"].unique():
2409            mlf_results_perid = []
2410            ms2_annot_mf = ms2_annot[ms2_annot["mf_id"] == mf_id].copy()
2411            ms2_annot_mf["n_spectra_contributing"] = (
2412                ms2_annot_mf.query_spectrum_id.nunique()
2413            )
2414
2415            for query_scan in ms2_annot["query_spectrum_id"].unique():
2416                ms2_annot_sub = ms2_annot_mf[
2417                    ms2_annot_mf["query_spectrum_id"] == query_scan
2418                ].copy()
2419
2420                if ms2_annot_sub["lipid_summed_name"].nunique() == 1:
2421                    # If there is only one lipid_summed_name, let's try to get consensus molecular species annotation
2422                    if ms2_annot_sub["lipid_summed_name"].nunique() == 1:
2423                        ms2_annot_sub["entropy_max"] = (
2424                            ms2_annot_sub["entropy_similarity"]
2425                            == ms2_annot_sub["entropy_similarity"].max()
2426                        )
2427                        ms2_annot_sub["ref_match_fract_max"] = (
2428                            ms2_annot_sub["ref_mz_in_query_fract"]
2429                            == ms2_annot_sub["ref_mz_in_query_fract"].max()
2430                        )
2431                        ms2_annot_sub["frag_max"] = ms2_annot_sub[
2432                            "query_frag_types"
2433                        ].apply(lambda x: True if "MLF" in x else False)
2434
2435                        # New column that looks if there is a consensus between the ranks (one row that is highest in all ranks)
2436                        ms2_annot_sub["consensus"] = ms2_annot_sub[
2437                            ["entropy_max", "ref_match_fract_max", "frag_max"]
2438                        ].all(axis=1)
2439
2440                        # If there is a consensus, take the row with the highest entropy_similarity
2441                        if ms2_annot_sub["consensus"].any():
2442                            ms2_annot_sub = ms2_annot_sub[
2443                                ms2_annot_sub["entropy_similarity"]
2444                                == ms2_annot_sub["entropy_similarity"].max()
2445                            ].head(1)
2446                            mlf_results_perid.append(ms2_annot_sub)
2447            if len(mlf_results_perid) == 0:
2448                mlf_results_perid = pd.DataFrame()
2449            else:
2450                mlf_results_perid = pd.concat(mlf_results_perid)
2451                if mlf_results_perid["name"].nunique() == 1:
2452                    mlf_results_perid = mlf_results_perid[
2453                        mlf_results_perid["entropy_similarity"]
2454                        == mlf_results_perid["entropy_similarity"].max()
2455                    ].head(1)
2456                else:
2457                    mlf_results_perid = pd.DataFrame()
2458                mlf_results_all.append(mlf_results_perid)
2459
2460        # These are the consensus annotations to the MLF level
2461        if len(mlf_results_all) > 0:
2462            mlf_results_all = pd.concat(mlf_results_all)
2463            mlf_results_all["annot_level"] = mlf_results_all["structure_level"]
2464        else:
2465            # Make an empty dataframe
2466            mlf_results_all = ms2_annot.head(0)
2467
2468        # For remaining mf_ids, try to get a consensus annotation to the species level
2469        species_results_all = []
2470        # Remove mf_ids that have consensus annotations to the MLF level
2471        ms2_annot_spec = ms2_annot[
2472            ~ms2_annot["mf_id"].isin(mlf_results_all["mf_id"].unique())
2473        ]
2474        for mf_id in ms2_annot_spec["mf_id"].unique():
2475            # Do all the hits have the same lipid_summed_name?
2476            ms2_annot_sub = ms2_annot_spec[ms2_annot_spec["mf_id"] == mf_id].copy()
2477            ms2_annot_sub["n_spectra_contributing"] = len(ms2_annot_sub)
2478
2479            if ms2_annot_sub["lipid_summed_name"].nunique() == 1:
2480                # Grab the highest entropy_similarity result
2481                ms2_annot_sub = ms2_annot_sub[
2482                    ms2_annot_sub["entropy_similarity"]
2483                    == ms2_annot_sub["entropy_similarity"].max()
2484                ].head(1)
2485                species_results_all.append(ms2_annot_sub)
2486
2487        # These are the consensus annotations to the species level
2488        if len(species_results_all) > 0:
2489            species_results_all = pd.concat(species_results_all)
2490            species_results_all["annot_level"] = "species"
2491        else:
2492            # Make an empty dataframe
2493            species_results_all = ms2_annot.head(0)
2494
2495        # Deal with the remaining mf_ids that do not have consensus annotations to the species level or MLF level
2496        # Remove mf_ids that have consensus annotations to the species level
2497        ms2_annot_remaining = ms2_annot_spec[
2498            ~ms2_annot_spec["mf_id"].isin(species_results_all["mf_id"].unique())
2499        ]
2500        no_consensus = []
2501        for mf_id in ms2_annot_remaining["mf_id"].unique():
2502            id_sub = []
2503            id_no_con = []
2504            ms2_annot_sub_mf = ms2_annot_remaining[
2505                ms2_annot_remaining["mf_id"] == mf_id
2506            ].copy()
2507            for query_scan in ms2_annot_sub_mf["query_spectrum_id"].unique():
2508                ms2_annot_sub = ms2_annot_sub_mf[
2509                    ms2_annot_sub_mf["query_spectrum_id"] == query_scan
2510                ].copy()
2511
2512                # New columns for ranking [HIGHER RANK = BETTER]
2513                ms2_annot_sub["entropy_max"] = (
2514                    ms2_annot_sub["entropy_similarity"]
2515                    == ms2_annot_sub["entropy_similarity"].max()
2516                )
2517                ms2_annot_sub["ref_match_fract_max"] = (
2518                    ms2_annot_sub["ref_mz_in_query_fract"]
2519                    == ms2_annot_sub["ref_mz_in_query_fract"].max()
2520                )
2521                ms2_annot_sub["frag_max"] = ms2_annot_sub["query_frag_types"].apply(
2522                    lambda x: True if "MLF" in x else False
2523                )
2524
2525                # New column that looks if there is a consensus between the ranks (one row that is highest in all ranks)
2526                ms2_annot_sub["consensus"] = ms2_annot_sub[
2527                    ["entropy_max", "ref_match_fract_max", "frag_max"]
2528                ].all(axis=1)
2529                ms2_annot_sub_con = ms2_annot_sub[ms2_annot_sub["consensus"]]
2530                id_sub.append(ms2_annot_sub_con)
2531                id_no_con.append(ms2_annot_sub)
2532            id_sub = pd.concat(id_sub)
2533            id_no_con = pd.concat(id_no_con)
2534
2535            # Scenario 1: Multiple scans are being resolved to different MLFs [could be coelutions and should both be kept and annotated to MS level]
2536            if (
2537                id_sub["query_frag_types"]
2538                .apply(lambda x: True if "MLF" in x else False)
2539                .all()
2540                and len(id_sub) > 0
2541            ):
2542                idx = id_sub.groupby("name")["entropy_similarity"].idxmax()
2543                id_sub = id_sub.loc[idx]
2544                # Reorder so highest entropy_similarity is first
2545                id_sub = id_sub.sort_values("entropy_similarity", ascending=False)
2546                id_sub["annot_level"] = id_sub["structure_level"]
2547                no_consensus.append(id_sub)
2548
2549            # Scenario 2: Multiple scans are being resolved to different species, keep both and annotate to appropriate level
2550            elif len(id_sub) == 0:
2551                for lipid_summed_name in id_no_con["lipid_summed_name"].unique():
2552                    summed_sub = id_no_con[
2553                        id_no_con["lipid_summed_name"] == lipid_summed_name
2554                    ]
2555                    # Any consensus to MLF?
2556                    if summed_sub["consensus"].any():
2557                        summed_sub = summed_sub[summed_sub["consensus"]]
2558                        summed_sub["annot_level"] = summed_sub["structure_level"]
2559                        no_consensus.append(summed_sub)
2560                    else:
2561                        # Grab the highest entropy_similarity, if there are multiple, grab the first one
2562                        summed_sub = summed_sub[
2563                            summed_sub["entropy_similarity"]
2564                            == summed_sub["entropy_similarity"].max()
2565                        ].head(1)
2566                        # get first row
2567                        summed_sub["annot_level"] = "species"
2568                        summed_sub["name"] = ""
2569                        no_consensus.append(summed_sub)
2570            else:
2571                raise ValueError("Unexpected scenario for summarizing mf_id: ", mf_id)
2572
2573        if len(no_consensus) > 0:
2574            no_consensus = pd.concat(no_consensus)
2575        else:
2576            no_consensus = ms2_annot.head(0)
2577
2578        # Combine all the consensus annotations and reformat the dataframe for output
2579        species_results_all = species_results_all.drop(columns=["name"])
2580        species_results_all["lipid_molecular_species_id"] = ""
2581        mlf_results_all["lipid_molecular_species_id"] = mlf_results_all["name"]
2582        no_consensus["lipid_molecular_species_id"] = no_consensus["name"]
2583        consensus_annotations = pd.concat(
2584            [mlf_results_all, species_results_all, no_consensus]
2585        )
2586        consensus_annotations = consensus_annotations.sort_values(
2587            "mf_id", ascending=True
2588        )
2589        cols_to_keep = [
2590            "mf_id",
2591            "ref_ion_type",
2592            "entropy_similarity",
2593            "ref_mz_in_query_fract",
2594            "lipid_molecular_species_id",
2595            "lipid_summed_name",
2596            "lipid_subclass",
2597            "lipid_class",
2598            "lipid_category",
2599            "formula",
2600            "annot_level",
2601            "n_spectra_contributing",
2602        ]
2603        consensus_annotations = consensus_annotations[cols_to_keep]
2604        consensus_annotations = consensus_annotations.set_index("mf_id")
2605
2606        return consensus_annotations
2607
2608    def clean_ms2_report(self, lipid_summary):
2609        """Clean the MS2 report.
2610
2611        Parameters
2612        ----------
2613        lipid_summary : DataFrame
2614            The full lipid summary DataFrame.
2615
2616        Returns
2617        -------
2618        DataFrame
2619            The cleaned lipid summary DataFrame.
2620        """
2621        lipid_summary = lipid_summary.reset_index()
2622        # Library (MS2 metadata) formulas — keep separate from MS1 search fields
2623        lipid_summary["library_ion_formula"] = [
2624            self.get_ion_formula(f, a)
2625            for f, a in zip(lipid_summary["formula"], lipid_summary["ref_ion_type"])
2626        ]
2627        lipid_summary = lipid_summary.rename(columns={"formula": "library_formula"})
2628
2629        # Reorder columns
2630        lipid_summary = lipid_summary[
2631            [
2632                "mf_id",
2633                "library_ion_formula",
2634                "ref_ion_type",
2635                "library_formula",
2636                "annot_level",
2637                "lipid_molecular_species_id",
2638                "lipid_summed_name",
2639                "lipid_subclass",
2640                "lipid_class",
2641                "lipid_category",
2642                "entropy_similarity",
2643                "ref_mz_in_query_fract",
2644                "n_spectra_contributing",
2645            ]
2646        ]
2647
2648        # Set the index to mf_id
2649        lipid_summary = lipid_summary.set_index("mf_id")
2650
2651        return lipid_summary
2652
2653    def to_report(self, molecular_metadata=None):
2654        """Create a report of the mass features and their annotations.
2655
2656        Parameters
2657        ----------
2658        molecular_metadata : dict, optional
2659            The molecular metadata. Default is None.
2660
2661        Returns
2662        -------
2663        DataFrame
2664            The report of the mass features and their annotations.
2665
2666        Notes
2667        -----
2668        The report will contain the mass features and their annotations from MS1 and MS2 (if available).
2669        """
2670        # Get mass feature dataframe
2671        mf_report = self.mass_spectra.mass_features_to_df()
2672        mf_report = mf_report.reset_index(drop=False)
2673
2674        # Get and clean ms1 annotation dataframe
2675        ms1_annot_report = self.mass_spectra.mass_features_ms1_annot_to_df().copy()
2676        ms1_annot_report = self.clean_ms1_report(ms1_annot_report)
2677        ms1_annot_report = ms1_annot_report.reset_index(drop=False)
2678
2679        # Get, summarize, and clean ms2 annotation dataframe
2680        ms2_annot_report = self.mass_spectra.mass_features_ms2_annot_to_df(
2681            molecular_metadata=molecular_metadata
2682        )
2683        if ms2_annot_report is not None and molecular_metadata is not None:
2684            ms2_annot_report = self.summarize_lipid_report(ms2_annot_report)
2685            ms2_annot_report = self.clean_ms2_report(ms2_annot_report)
2686            ms2_annot_report = ms2_annot_report.dropna(axis=1, how="all")
2687            ms2_annot_report = ms2_annot_report.reset_index(drop=False)
2688        report = self.combine_reports(
2689            mf_report=mf_report,
2690            ms1_annot_report=ms1_annot_report,
2691            ms2_annot_report=ms2_annot_report,
2692        )
2693        return report
2694
2695
2696class LCMSCollectionExport:
2697    """A class to export an LCMS collection to HDF5 or Parquet format.
2698
2699    This class provides methods to export collection-level data from multi-sample LC-MS
2700    experiments to HDF5 or Parquet files. It handles the export of metadata, retention time
2701    alignments, cluster assignments, and induced mass features (gap-filled features) across
2702    the collection.
2703
2704    The exporter is designed to work with LCMSCollection objects and complements the individual
2705    LCMSExport class by focusing on collection-wide data rather than individual sample data.
2706
2707    Parameters
2708    ----------
2709    out_file_path : str | Path
2710        The output file path, do not include the file extension. The .hdf5 / .parquet
2711        extensions are added automatically as needed.
2712    mass_spectra_collection : LCMSCollection
2713        The LCMS collection object containing multiple LCMS samples with processed mass features,
2714        alignments, and clustering information.
2715
2716    Attributes
2717    ----------
2718    out_file_path : Path
2719        The output file path as a Path object.
2720    mass_spectra_collection : LCMSCollection
2721        The LCMS collection object to be exported.
2722
2723    Methods
2724    -------
2725    export_to_hdf5(overwrite=False)
2726        Export the LCMS collection to an HDF5 file with collection-level data.
2727    export_to_parquet(overwrite=False)
2728        Export collection-level tabular datasets to Parquet files.
2729
2730    Notes
2731    -----
2732    This class exports collection-level data including:
2733    - Sample manifest (metadata about all samples in the collection)
2734    - Retention time alignment data (if RT alignment has been performed)
2735    - Cluster assignments (consensus mass feature groupings across samples)
2736    - Induced mass features (gap-filled features saved to individual LCMS object HDF5 files)
2737
2738    Individual sample data (mass spectra, mass features, EICs, etc.) should be exported
2739    separately using the LCMSExport class for each LCMS object in the collection.
2740
2741    Examples
2742    --------
2743    Export a collection after clustering and gap-filling:
2744
2745    >>> from corems.mass_spectra.output.export import LCMSCollectionExporter
2746    >>> exporter = LCMSCollectionExporter("my_collection", lcms_collection)
2747    >>> exporter.export_to_hdf5(overwrite=True)
2748
2749    The resulting HDF5 file will contain collection-level metadata and can be used
2750    to reconstruct the collection state for further analysis.
2751
2752    See Also
2753    --------
2754    LCMSExport : Export individual LCMS objects to HDF5
2755    LCMSCollection : The collection object being exported
2756    """
2757
2758    def __init__(self, out_file_path, mass_spectra_collection):
2759        self.out_file_path = Path(out_file_path)
2760        self.mass_spectra_collection = mass_spectra_collection
2761
2762    def export_to_hdf5(
2763        self,
2764        overwrite=False,
2765        save_parameters=True,
2766        parameter_format="toml",
2767        update_lcms_objects=True,
2768    ):
2769        """Export the LCMS collection to an HDF5 file.
2770
2771        This method saves the collection-level data to an HDF5 file, including:
2772        - Basic metadata (date, folder location, gap-filling status)
2773        - Sample manifest
2774        - Retention time alignments (if available)
2775        - Cluster assignments (if available)
2776        - Induced mass features for each LCMS object (if gap-filling was performed)
2777
2778        Individual LCMS objects in the collection are not exported by this method.
2779        Use LCMSExport for exporting individual LCMS objects.
2780
2781        Parameters
2782        ----------
2783        overwrite : bool, optional
2784            If True, overwrites the output file if it already exists and replaces
2785            existing groups within the HDF5 file. If False, appends new data to
2786            existing file without overwriting existing groups. Default is False.
2787        save_parameters : bool, optional
2788            If True, saves the collection-level parameters to a separate file in the specified format.
2789            Default is True.
2790        parameter_format : str, optional
2791            The format for saving parameters, either "json" or "toml". Default is "toml".
2792        update_lcms_objects : bool, optional
2793            If True, updates the individual LCMS object HDF5 files with new raw file locations and any additional
2794            information produced during the processing of the collection (e.g. cluster mass feature associations). Default is True.
2795
2796        Notes
2797        -----
2798        The HDF5 file structure includes:
2799        - Attributes: date_utc, lcms_objects_folder, missing_mass_features_searched, manifest
2800        - Groups: rt_alignments, cluster_assignments (if available)
2801
2802        Induced mass features are saved to the individual LCMS object HDF5 files
2803        within the .corems folder structure, not in the collection-level HDF5 file.
2804
2805        Examples
2806        --------
2807        >>> exporter = LCMSCollectionExporter("my_collection", lcms_collection)
2808        >>> exporter.export_to_hdf5(overwrite=True)
2809        """
2810        if overwrite:
2811            if self.out_file_path.with_suffix(".hdf5").exists():
2812                self.out_file_path.with_suffix(".hdf5").unlink()
2813
2814        with h5py.File(self.out_file_path.with_suffix(".hdf5"), "a") as hdf_handle:
2815            # Add basic attributes to the HDF5 file, always overwrite these
2816            timenow = str(datetime.now(timezone.utc).strftime("%d/%m/%Y %H:%M:%S %Z"))
2817            hdf_handle.attrs["date_utc"] = timenow
2818            hdf_handle.attrs["lcms_objects_folder"] = str(
2819                self.mass_spectra_collection.collection_parser.folder_location
2820            )
2821            hdf_handle.attrs["missing_mass_features_searched"] = (
2822                self.mass_spectra_collection.missing_mass_features_searched
2823            )
2824            hdf_handle.attrs["rt_aligned"] = self.mass_spectra_collection.rt_aligned
2825            hdf_handle.attrs["rt_alignment_attempted"] = (
2826                self.mass_spectra_collection.rt_alignment_attempted
2827            )
2828
2829            # Add the manifest to the HDF5 file, always overwrite this
2830            hdf_handle.attrs["manifest"] = self._convert_manifest_to_json()
2831
2832            # Save retention time alignments if they exist, only overwrite if specified
2833            self._save_rt_alignments_to_hdf5(hdf_handle, overwrite)
2834
2835            # Save cluster assignments if they exist, only overwrite if specified
2836            self._save_cluster_assignments_to_hdf5(hdf_handle, overwrite)
2837
2838            # Save consensus feature-group labels if present
2839            self._save_feature_group_labels_to_hdf5(hdf_handle, overwrite)
2840
2841        # Save new raw file locations to each LCMS object's HDF5 file if needed
2842        if (
2843            hasattr(self.mass_spectra_collection, "raw_files_relocated")
2844            and self.mass_spectra_collection.raw_files_relocated
2845        ):
2846            self._update_raw_file_locations_in_hdf5()
2847
2848        # Save induced mass features to the collection with associations to each individual, only if lcms_collection.missing_mass_features_searched is True
2849        if self.mass_spectra_collection.missing_mass_features_searched:
2850            self._save_induced_mass_features_to_hdf5(overwrite)
2851            # Save EICs for induced mass features at collection level
2852            self._save_induced_eics_to_hdf5(overwrite)
2853
2854        # Build cluster mass feature map to know which features to update
2855        # This uses the same logic as process_consensus_features to determine loaded features
2856        cluster_mf_map = self._build_cluster_mf_map()
2857
2858        # Save updated mass features for each LCMS object
2859        # This implements selective update: only loaded features are updated, non-cluster features are preserved
2860        if update_lcms_objects:
2861            self._save_lcms_objects_to_hdf5(cluster_mf_map, overwrite)
2862
2863        # Save collection-level parameters as separate file
2864        if save_parameters:
2865            # Check if parameter_format is valid
2866            if parameter_format not in ["json", "toml"]:
2867                raise ValueError("parameter_format must be 'json' or 'toml'")
2868
2869            if parameter_format == "json":
2870                dump_lcms_collection_settings_json(
2871                    filename=self.out_file_path.with_suffix(".json"),
2872                    lcms_collection=self.mass_spectra_collection,
2873                )
2874            elif parameter_format == "toml":
2875                dump_lcms_collection_settings_toml(
2876                    filename=self.out_file_path.with_suffix(".toml"),
2877                    lcms_collection=self.mass_spectra_collection,
2878                )
2879
2880    def export_to_parquet(
2881        self, overwrite=False, save_parameters=True, parameter_format="toml"
2882    ):
2883        """Export collection-level LC-MS datasets to Parquet files.
2884
2885        Writes next to ``out_file_path`` (same stem as the HDF5 export):
2886
2887        - ``{stem}_manifest.parquet`` — sample manifest
2888        - ``{stem}_cluster_assignments.parquet`` — cluster labels (if present)
2889        - ``{stem}_mass_features.parquet`` — collection mass-features table (if present)
2890        - ``{stem}_rt_alignments.parquet`` — RT alignment curves (if aligned)
2891        - parameters as JSON or TOML when ``save_parameters`` is True
2892
2893        Parameters
2894        ----------
2895        overwrite : bool, optional
2896            Whether to overwrite existing Parquet files. Default is False.
2897        save_parameters : bool, optional
2898            Whether to save collection parameters. Default is True.
2899        parameter_format : str, optional
2900            Parameter file format, ``'json'`` or ``'toml'``. Default is ``'toml'``.
2901
2902        Notes
2903        -----
2904        Requires ``pyarrow`` (or ``fastparquet``) for pandas Parquet I/O.
2905        This is a tabular companion to ``export_to_hdf5``; it does not replace
2906        per-sample HDF5 archives or gap-fill side effects on individual LCMS files.
2907        """
2908        stem = self.out_file_path
2909
2910        def _write(df, suffix):
2911            if df is None or df.empty:
2912                return
2913            out_path = Path(f"{stem}_{suffix}").with_suffix(".parquet")
2914            if out_path.exists() and not overwrite:
2915                return
2916            LCMSExport._prepare_df_for_parquet(df).to_parquet(out_path, index=False)
2917
2918        # Manifest — prefer the tidy samples-as-rows dataframe
2919        manifest_df = getattr(self.mass_spectra_collection, "manifest_dataframe", None)
2920        if manifest_df is None or getattr(manifest_df, "empty", True):
2921            manifest = getattr(
2922                self.mass_spectra_collection, "manifest", None
2923            ) or getattr(
2924                getattr(self.mass_spectra_collection, "collection_parser", None),
2925                "manifest",
2926                None,
2927            )
2928            if isinstance(manifest, DataFrame):
2929                manifest_df = manifest
2930            elif isinstance(manifest, dict) and manifest:
2931                try:
2932                    # Collection manifests are sample -> attrs; transpose to rows
2933                    manifest_df = pd.DataFrame(manifest).T
2934                except ValueError:
2935                    manifest_df = DataFrame(
2936                        [{"manifest_json": self._convert_manifest_to_json()}]
2937                    )
2938            else:
2939                manifest_df = None
2940
2941        if manifest_df is not None and not manifest_df.empty:
2942            _write(manifest_df.reset_index(drop=False), "manifest")
2943
2944        # Cluster assignments / mass features table
2945        mf_df = getattr(self.mass_spectra_collection, "mass_features_dataframe", None)
2946        if mf_df is not None and not mf_df.empty:
2947            _write(mf_df.reset_index(drop=False), "mass_features")
2948            if "cluster" in mf_df.columns:
2949                cluster_df = mf_df[["cluster"]].copy().reset_index(drop=False)
2950                _write(cluster_df, "cluster_assignments")
2951
2952        # RT alignments as long-format table
2953        if getattr(self.mass_spectra_collection, "rt_aligned", False) and getattr(
2954            self.mass_spectra_collection, "rt_alignments", None
2955        ):
2956            frames = []
2957            for (
2958                sample_idx,
2959                alignment_data,
2960            ) in self.mass_spectra_collection.rt_alignments.items():
2961                arr = np.asarray(alignment_data)
2962                if arr.ndim == 1:
2963                    frames.append(
2964                        DataFrame(
2965                            {
2966                                "sample_idx": sample_idx,
2967                                "point": np.arange(len(arr)),
2968                                "value": arr,
2969                            }
2970                        )
2971                    )
2972                elif arr.ndim == 2 and arr.shape[1] >= 2:
2973                    frames.append(
2974                        DataFrame(
2975                            {
2976                                "sample_idx": sample_idx,
2977                                "rt_original": arr[:, 0],
2978                                "rt_aligned": arr[:, 1],
2979                            }
2980                        )
2981                    )
2982                else:
2983                    frames.append(
2984                        DataFrame(
2985                            {
2986                                "sample_idx": [sample_idx],
2987                                "alignment_json": [json.dumps(arr.tolist())],
2988                            }
2989                        )
2990                    )
2991            if frames:
2992                _write(pd.concat(frames, ignore_index=True), "rt_alignments")
2993
2994        if save_parameters:
2995            if parameter_format not in ["json", "toml"]:
2996                raise ValueError("parameter_format must be 'json' or 'toml'")
2997            if parameter_format == "json":
2998                dump_lcms_collection_settings_json(
2999                    filename=self.out_file_path.with_suffix(".json"),
3000                    lcms_collection=self.mass_spectra_collection,
3001                )
3002            elif parameter_format == "toml":
3003                dump_lcms_collection_settings_toml(
3004                    filename=self.out_file_path.with_suffix(".toml"),
3005                    lcms_collection=self.mass_spectra_collection,
3006                )
3007
3008    def _save_rt_alignments_to_hdf5(self, hdf_handle, overwrite):
3009        """Save retention time alignments to HDF5 file."""
3010        # If no rt_alignments, return early
3011        if not self.mass_spectra_collection.rt_aligned:
3012            return
3013
3014        # If rt_alignments exist, save them
3015        if self.mass_spectra_collection.rt_aligned:
3016            group_name = "rt_alignments"
3017            # grab dictionary of rt_alignments
3018            rt_alignments = self.mass_spectra_collection.rt_alignments
3019
3020        if rt_alignments:
3021            # Check if group exists and handle overwrite logic
3022            if group_name in hdf_handle:
3023                if not overwrite:
3024                    return
3025                del hdf_handle[group_name]
3026
3027            grp = hdf_handle.create_group(group_name)
3028
3029            # Save each alignment as a dataset
3030            for sample_idx, alignment_data in rt_alignments.items():
3031                grp.create_dataset(str(sample_idx), data=alignment_data)
3032
3033    def _convert_manifest_to_json(self):
3034        """Clean the manifest for export to HDF5."""
3035        manifest = self.mass_spectra_collection.collection_parser.manifest
3036
3037        # Process the manifest to convert numpy.bool_ or bool values for the 'use_rt_alignment' key
3038        def convert_bool_values(data):
3039            if isinstance(data, dict):
3040                # Process each key-value pair recursively
3041                return {
3042                    k: (
3043                        int(v)
3044                        if k == "use_rt_alignment" and isinstance(v, (bool, np.bool_))
3045                        else convert_bool_values(v)
3046                    )
3047                    for k, v in data.items()
3048                }
3049            elif isinstance(data, list):
3050                # Recursively process lists
3051                return [convert_bool_values(item) for item in data]
3052            else:
3053                # Return non-dict/list types unchanged
3054                return data
3055
3056        # Clean the whole manifest
3057        cleaned_manifest = convert_bool_values(manifest)
3058
3059        # Serialize the cleaned manifest into JSON format
3060        json_manifest = json.dumps(cleaned_manifest)
3061        return json_manifest
3062
3063    def _save_cluster_assignments_to_hdf5(self, hdf_handle, overwrite):
3064        """Save cluster assignments to HDF5 file."""
3065        # Check if column "cluster" is present in self.mass_features_dataframe
3066        if "cluster" in self.mass_spectra_collection.mass_features_dataframe.columns:
3067            group_name = "cluster_assignments"
3068            cluster_assignments = self.mass_spectra_collection.mass_features_dataframe[
3069                ["cluster"]
3070            ].copy()
3071
3072            # Check if group exists and handle overwrite logic
3073            if group_name in hdf_handle:
3074                if not overwrite:
3075                    return
3076                del hdf_handle[group_name]
3077
3078            grp = hdf_handle.create_group(group_name)
3079
3080            # Save the index, converting strings to bytes.
3081            # Avoid Index.astype(str).values under pandas 3 string/CoW semantics;
3082            # build a plain numpy bytes array instead.
3083            index_bytes = np.asarray(
3084                [str(x).encode("utf-8") for x in cluster_assignments.index],
3085                dtype="S",
3086            )
3087            grp.create_dataset("index", data=index_bytes)
3088
3089            # Save the "cluster" column
3090            grp.create_dataset(
3091                "cluster", data=cluster_assignments["cluster"].to_numpy()
3092            )
3093
3094    def _save_feature_group_labels_to_hdf5(self, hdf_handle, overwrite):
3095        """Save cluster-indexed feature-group labels to the collection HDF5."""
3096        from corems.mass_spectra.calc.feature_grouping import GROUP_COLUMNS
3097
3098        labels = getattr(self.mass_spectra_collection, "feature_group_dataframe", None)
3099        if labels is None or len(labels) == 0:
3100            return
3101
3102        group_name = "feature_group_labels"
3103        if group_name in hdf_handle:
3104            if not overwrite:
3105                return
3106            del hdf_handle[group_name]
3107
3108        grp = hdf_handle.create_group(group_name)
3109        index_vals = np.asarray(
3110            [int(x) for x in labels.index],
3111            dtype=np.int64,
3112        )
3113        grp.create_dataset("cluster", data=index_vals)
3114
3115        for col in GROUP_COLUMNS:
3116            if col not in labels.columns:
3117                continue
3118            series = labels[col]
3119            if col in ("feature_group_id", "mono_cluster_id"):
3120                # Nullable ints → float with NaN for missing
3121                data = series.astype("Float64").to_numpy(dtype=float)
3122                grp.create_dataset(col, data=data)
3123            else:
3124                # Object / string columns
3125                encoded = np.asarray(
3126                    [
3127                        (
3128                            b""
3129                            if v is None
3130                            or (isinstance(v, float) and np.isnan(v))
3131                            or (hasattr(pd, "isna") and pd.isna(v))
3132                            else str(v).encode("utf-8")
3133                        )
3134                        for v in series.tolist()
3135                    ],
3136                    dtype="S",
3137                )
3138                grp.create_dataset(col, data=encoded)
3139
3140    def _build_cluster_mf_map(self):
3141        """Build a mapping of which mass features should be saved for each sample.
3142
3143        This uses the same logic as process_consensus_features to determine which
3144        mass features were loaded and should be updated in HDF5 files.
3145
3146        Returns
3147        -------
3148        dict
3149            Dictionary mapping sample_id to list of tuples (mf_id, cluster_id).
3150            Only includes samples that have loaded representative features.
3151            Returns empty dict if no clusters exist.
3152
3153        Notes
3154        -----
3155        This follows the DRY principle by using the same get_sample_mf_map_for_representatives
3156        method used by process_consensus_features and ReadSavedLCMSCollection.
3157        """
3158        # Check if clusters exist
3159        if (
3160            "cluster"
3161            not in self.mass_spectra_collection.mass_features_dataframe.columns
3162        ):
3163            return {}
3164
3165        # Check if cluster_summary_dataframe exists (needed by get_sample_mf_map_for_representatives)
3166        if (
3167            not hasattr(self.mass_spectra_collection, "cluster_summary_dataframe")
3168            or self.mass_spectra_collection.cluster_summary_dataframe is None
3169        ):
3170            return {}
3171
3172        # Use the same DRY helper method that process_consensus_features uses
3173        # This ensures consistency across the codebase
3174        cluster_mf_map = (
3175            self.mass_spectra_collection.get_sample_mf_map_for_representatives(
3176                include_cluster_id=True
3177            )
3178        )
3179
3180        return cluster_mf_map
3181
3182    def _update_raw_file_locations_in_hdf5(self):
3183        """Update raw file locations in each LCMS object's HDF5 file.
3184
3185        This method updates the 'original_file_location' attribute in each LCMS object's
3186        HDF5 file to reflect the new raw file location after files have been relocated.
3187        """
3188        for lcms_obj in self.mass_spectra_collection:
3189            # Get the HDF5 file path for this LCMS object
3190            hdf5_path = lcms_obj.file_location.with_suffix(".hdf5")
3191
3192            if hdf5_path.exists():
3193                with h5py.File(hdf5_path, "a") as hdf_handle:
3194                    # Update the original_file_location attribute
3195                    if "original_file_location" in hdf_handle.attrs:
3196                        hdf_handle.attrs["original_file_location"] = str(
3197                            lcms_obj.raw_file_location
3198                        )
3199                    # If the attribute does not exist, create it
3200                    else:
3201                        hdf_handle.attrs.create(
3202                            "original_file_location", str(lcms_obj.raw_file_location)
3203                        )
3204
3205    def _save_induced_mass_features_to_hdf5(self, overwrite):
3206        """Save induced mass features to the collection HDF5 file.
3207
3208        Induced mass features are gap-filled features that only exist at the collection level.
3209        They are saved with full detail (all attributes and datasets) in the collection HDF5 file
3210        and distributed to individual LCMS objects when the collection is loaded.
3211
3212        The induced mass features are stored in the collection's induced_mass_features_dataframe
3213        and are regenerated as LCMSMassFeature objects for saving.
3214
3215        Parameters
3216        ----------
3217        overwrite : bool
3218            If True, overwrites existing induced mass features group. If False, skips if group exists.
3219        """
3220        # Check if we have any induced mass features to save
3221        if (
3222            self.mass_spectra_collection.induced_mass_features_dataframe is None
3223            or self.mass_spectra_collection.induced_mass_features_dataframe.empty
3224        ):
3225            return
3226
3227        # Open the collection HDF5 file to save induced mass features
3228        with h5py.File(self.out_file_path.with_suffix(".hdf5"), "a") as hdf_handle:
3229            group_name = "induced_mass_features"
3230
3231            # Check if group exists and handle overwrite logic
3232            if group_name in hdf_handle:
3233                if not overwrite:
3234                    return
3235                del hdf_handle[group_name]
3236
3237            # Create top-level group for induced mass features
3238            imf_group = hdf_handle.create_group(group_name)
3239
3240            # Get the induced mass features dataframe
3241            induced_df = self.mass_spectra_collection.induced_mass_features_dataframe
3242
3243            # Get unique sample IDs from the dataframe
3244            sample_ids = induced_df["sample_id"].unique()
3245
3246            # Iterate through each sample and save its induced mass features
3247            for sample_id in sample_ids:
3248                # Filter dataframe to this sample
3249                sample_df = induced_df[induced_df["sample_id"] == sample_id].copy()
3250
3251                if sample_df.empty:
3252                    continue
3253
3254                # Regenerate mass features from the dataframe
3255                regenerated_features = self._regenerate_mass_features_from_sample_df(
3256                    sample_df, sample_id
3257                )
3258
3259                if not regenerated_features:
3260                    continue
3261
3262                # Create a subgroup for this sample's induced mass features
3263                sample_group = imf_group.create_group(str(sample_id))
3264
3265                # Use the static helper method from LCMSExport to save the mass features
3266                LCMSExport._save_mass_features_dict_to_hdf5(
3267                    regenerated_features, sample_group, overwrite=overwrite
3268                )
3269
3270    def _save_induced_eics_to_hdf5(self, overwrite):
3271        """Save EICs for induced mass features to the collection HDF5 file.
3272
3273        Induced mass features are gap-filled features created during process_consensus_features.
3274        Their associated EICs need to be saved at the collection level so they can be reloaded.
3275
3276        The induced mass features are identified from the collection's induced_mass_features_dataframe,
3277        and their EICs are retrieved from the individual LCMS objects.
3278
3279        Parameters
3280        ----------
3281        overwrite : bool
3282            If True, overwrites existing induced EICs group. If False, skips if group exists.
3283        """
3284        # Check if we have any induced mass features to save
3285        if (
3286            self.mass_spectra_collection.induced_mass_features_dataframe is None
3287            or self.mass_spectra_collection.induced_mass_features_dataframe.empty
3288        ):
3289            return
3290
3291        # Open the collection HDF5 file to save induced EICs
3292        with h5py.File(self.out_file_path.with_suffix(".hdf5"), "a") as hdf_handle:
3293            group_name = "induced_eics"
3294
3295            # Check if group exists and handle overwrite logic
3296            if group_name in hdf_handle:
3297                if not overwrite:
3298                    return
3299                del hdf_handle[group_name]
3300
3301            # Create top-level group for induced EICs
3302            induced_eics_group = hdf_handle.create_group(group_name)
3303
3304            # Get the induced mass features dataframe
3305            induced_df = self.mass_spectra_collection.induced_mass_features_dataframe
3306
3307            # Get unique sample IDs from the dataframe
3308            sample_ids = induced_df["sample_id"].unique()
3309
3310            # Iterate through each sample and save EICs for its induced mass features
3311            for sample_id in sample_ids:
3312                lcms_obj = self.mass_spectra_collection[sample_id]
3313
3314                # Filter dataframe to this sample
3315                sample_df = induced_df[induced_df["sample_id"] == sample_id].copy()
3316
3317                if sample_df.empty:
3318                    continue
3319
3320                # Collect EICs for induced mass features using _eic_mz from dataframe
3321                induced_eics = {}
3322                for _, row in sample_df.iterrows():
3323                    # Get the EIC m/z from the dataframe
3324                    eic_mz = row.get("_eic_mz")
3325
3326                    if eic_mz is not None and pd.notna(eic_mz):
3327                        # Try to get the EIC from the LCMS object
3328                        if (
3329                            hasattr(lcms_obj, "eics")
3330                            and lcms_obj.eics
3331                            and eic_mz in lcms_obj.eics
3332                        ):
3333                            induced_eics[eic_mz] = lcms_obj.eics[eic_mz]
3334
3335                if not induced_eics:
3336                    continue
3337
3338                # Create a subgroup for this sample's induced EICs
3339                sample_group = induced_eics_group.create_group(str(sample_id))
3340
3341                # Use the static helper method from LCMSExport to save the EICs
3342                LCMSExport._save_eics_dict_to_hdf5(
3343                    induced_eics, sample_group, overwrite
3344                )
3345
3346    def _regenerate_mass_features_from_sample_df(self, sample_df, sample_id):
3347        """Regenerate induced mass features from a sample-specific dataframe.
3348
3349        This method creates LCMSMassFeature objects from rows in the induced_mass_features_dataframe
3350        for a specific sample. The regenerated features are used for saving to HDF5.
3351
3352        Parameters
3353        ----------
3354        sample_df : pd.DataFrame
3355            DataFrame containing induced mass features for a specific sample.
3356        sample_id : int
3357            The sample ID (index in the collection).
3358
3359        Returns
3360        -------
3361        dict
3362            Dictionary of regenerated LCMSMassFeature objects keyed by feature ID.
3363        """
3364        from corems.chroma_peak.factory.chroma_peak_classes import LCMSMassFeature
3365
3366        if sample_df.empty:
3367            return {}
3368
3369        # Get the corresponding LCMS object for proper parent reference
3370        lcms_obj = self.mass_spectra_collection[sample_id]
3371
3372        # Regenerate mass features from the dataframe
3373        regenerated_features = {}
3374
3375        for _, row in sample_df.iterrows():
3376            # Extract the original ID from mf_id (format: c{cluster}_{index}_i)
3377            # This is the ID used in lcms_obj.induced_mass_features dict
3378            original_id = row["mf_id"]
3379
3380            # Create a new LCMSMassFeature with proper parent reference
3381            # Note: dataframe uses 'scan_time' but __init__ parameter is 'retention_time'
3382            mass_feature = LCMSMassFeature(
3383                lcms_parent=lcms_obj,
3384                mz=row["mz"],
3385                retention_time=row["scan_time"],  # Column is 'scan_time' in dataframe
3386                intensity=row["intensity"],
3387                apex_scan=int(row["apex_scan"]),
3388                persistence=row.get("persistence", None)
3389                if "persistence" in row
3390                else None,
3391                id=original_id,  # Use the original string ID from gap-filling
3392            )
3393
3394            # Set additional attributes dynamically from dataframe columns
3395            # Skip columns already handled in __init__ or structural metadata
3396            skip_cols = {
3397                "sample_id",
3398                "mf_id",
3399                "mz",
3400                "scan_time",
3401                "scan_time_aligned",
3402                "intensity",
3403                "apex_scan",
3404                "persistence",
3405            }
3406
3407            # Iterate through all columns and set via property setters
3408            for col_name in row.index:
3409                if col_name in skip_cols:
3410                    continue
3411                value = row[col_name]
3412                try:
3413                    if pd.isna(value):
3414                        continue
3415                except (TypeError, ValueError):
3416                    pass  # value is array-like; not NA, proceed
3417
3418                # Set via property (public interface handles private attributes)
3419                # Don't save empty lists
3420                if isinstance(value, list) and len(value) == 0:
3421                    continue
3422                try:
3423                    setattr(mass_feature, col_name, value)
3424                except (AttributeError, TypeError):
3425                    pass  # Skip attributes that don't exist or can't be set
3426
3427            # Set cluster_index if present
3428            if "cluster" in row and pd.notna(row["cluster"]):
3429                mass_feature.cluster_index = int(row["cluster"])
3430
3431            regenerated_features[mass_feature.id] = mass_feature
3432
3433        return regenerated_features
3434
3435    def _save_lcms_objects_to_hdf5(self, cluster_mf_map, overwrite):
3436        """Save updated mass features for each LCMS object.
3437
3438        This method implements a "selective update" strategy for mass features:
3439        - For mass features specified in cluster_mf_map (loaded representatives), we selectively
3440          update them by deleting their old entries and re-saving with new attributes.
3441        - Non-cluster features (not loaded) are never touched/overwritten.
3442
3443        Note: EICs are NOT saved here. Induced feature EICs are saved at the collection level.
3444
3445        Parameters
3446        ----------
3447        cluster_mf_map : dict
3448            Dictionary mapping sample_id to list of tuples (mf_id, cluster_id).
3449            This explicitly defines which mass features should be updated.
3450        overwrite : bool
3451            If True, allows overwriting of existing data. If False, skips if data exists.
3452        """
3453        for sample_id, lcms_obj in enumerate(self.mass_spectra_collection):
3454            hdf5_path = lcms_obj.file_location.with_suffix(".hdf5")
3455
3456            if not hdf5_path.exists():
3457                # If HDF5 doesn't exist, we can't do selective update, raise error
3458                raise FileNotFoundError(
3459                    f"HDF5 file for LCMS object {lcms_obj.sample_name} not found at {hdf5_path}"
3460                )
3461
3462            # Check if this sample has any loaded features in the map
3463            if sample_id not in cluster_mf_map or not cluster_mf_map[sample_id]:
3464                # Nothing loaded for this sample, nothing to update
3465                continue
3466
3467            # Extract mf_ids from the map (cluster_mf_map contains tuples of (mf_id, cluster_id))
3468            mf_ids_to_update = [
3469                mf_id for mf_id, cluster_id in cluster_mf_map[sample_id]
3470            ]
3471
3472            # Perform selective update of mass features
3473            self._selective_update_mass_features(
3474                lcms_obj, hdf5_path, mf_ids_to_update, overwrite
3475            )
3476
3477            # Save any new mass spectra that were added during processing
3478            self._save_new_mass_spectra(lcms_obj, hdf5_path, overwrite)
3479
3480    def _save_new_mass_spectra(self, lcms_obj, hdf5_path, overwrite):
3481        """Save new mass spectra that were added during processing.
3482
3483        This method checks what mass spectra are in lcms_obj._ms and saves any
3484        that aren't already in the HDF5 file's mass_spectra group. Uses the
3485        existing add_mass_spectrum_to_hdf5 method for consistency with original
3486        export logic.
3487
3488        Parameters
3489        ----------
3490        lcms_obj : LCMSBase
3491            The LCMS object with potentially new mass spectra.
3492        hdf5_path : Path
3493            Path to the HDF5 file.
3494        overwrite : bool
3495            If True, allows overwriting existing spectra.
3496        """
3497        # Check if there are any mass spectra to save
3498        if not hasattr(lcms_obj, "_ms") or not lcms_obj._ms:
3499            return
3500
3501        # Create an LCMS exporter instance for this LCMS object
3502        # This gives us access to add_mass_spectrum_to_hdf5 method inherited from HighResMassSpecExport
3503        # Turn hdf5_path into str without suffix for LCMSExport
3504        hdf5_path_str = str(hdf5_path.with_suffix(""))
3505        exporter = LCMSExport(out_file_path=hdf5_path_str, mass_spectra=lcms_obj)
3506
3507        # Open HDF5 file and check existing mass spectra
3508        with h5py.File(hdf5_path, "a") as hdf_handle:
3509            # Create mass_spectra group if it doesn't exist
3510            if "mass_spectra" not in hdf_handle:
3511                ms_group = hdf_handle.create_group("mass_spectra")
3512                existing_scan_numbers = set()
3513            else:
3514                ms_group = hdf_handle["mass_spectra"]
3515                existing_scan_numbers = set(int(k) for k in ms_group.keys())
3516
3517            # Find new mass spectra (in _ms but not in HDF5)
3518            new_scan_numbers = set(lcms_obj._ms.keys()) - existing_scan_numbers
3519
3520            if not new_scan_numbers:
3521                return
3522
3523            # Save new mass spectra using existing add_mass_spectrum_to_hdf5 method
3524            export_profile = lcms_obj.parameters.lc_ms.export_profile_spectra
3525            for scan_number in new_scan_numbers:
3526                mass_spec = lcms_obj._ms[scan_number]
3527                scan_group_name = str(scan_number)
3528
3529                # Delete existing group if overwrite is True
3530                if scan_group_name in ms_group and overwrite:
3531                    del ms_group[scan_group_name]
3532                elif scan_group_name in ms_group:
3533                    continue
3534
3535                # Use the existing method from HighResMassSpecExport
3536                exporter.add_mass_spectrum_to_hdf5(
3537                    hdf_handle=hdf_handle,
3538                    mass_spectrum=mass_spec,
3539                    group_key=scan_group_name,
3540                    mass_spectra_group=ms_group,
3541                    export_raw=export_profile,
3542                )
3543
3544    def _selective_update_mass_features(
3545        self, lcms_obj, hdf5_path, mf_ids_to_update, overwrite
3546    ):
3547        """Selectively update mass features in HDF5 file.
3548
3549        This method deletes only the mass features specified in mf_ids_to_update,
3550        then re-saves them with their potentially updated attributes. Non-cluster features
3551        in the HDF5 file are left untouched.
3552
3553        Parameters
3554        ----------
3555        lcms_obj : LCMSBase
3556            The LCMS object with mass features to update.
3557        hdf5_path : Path
3558            Path to the HDF5 file.
3559        mf_ids_to_update : list of int
3560            List of mass feature IDs that should be updated. This explicitly defines
3561            which features were loaded and should be saved.
3562        overwrite : bool
3563            If True, allows overwriting. If False, skips if group exists.
3564        """
3565        if not mf_ids_to_update:
3566            return
3567
3568        # Open HDF5 file and delete specified feature IDs, then re-save
3569        with h5py.File(hdf5_path, "a") as hdf_handle:
3570            if "mass_features" not in hdf_handle:
3571                return
3572
3573            mf_group = hdf_handle["mass_features"]
3574
3575            # Delete features that are being updated
3576            for feature_id in mf_ids_to_update:
3577                feature_id_str = str(feature_id)
3578                if feature_id_str in mf_group:
3579                    del mf_group[feature_id_str]
3580
3581            # Re-save updated features (only those that exist in mass_features dict)
3582            updated_features = {
3583                mf.id: mf
3584                for mf in lcms_obj.mass_features.values()
3585                if mf.id in mf_ids_to_update
3586            }
3587
3588            if updated_features:
3589                LCMSExport._save_mass_features_dict_to_hdf5(
3590                    updated_features, mf_group, overwrite=overwrite
3591                )

 43class LowResGCMSExport:
 44    """A class to export low resolution GC-MS data.
 45
 46    This class provides methods to export low resolution GC-MS data to various formats such as Excel, CSV, Parquet, HDF5, and Pandas DataFrame.
 47
 48    Parameters:
 49    ----------
 50    out_file_path : str
 51        The output file path.
 52    gcms : object
 53        The low resolution GCMS object.
 54
 55    Attributes:
 56    ----------
 57    output_file : Path
 58        The output file path as a Path object.
 59    gcms : object
 60        The low resolution GCMS object.
 61
 62    Methods:
 63    -------
 64    * get_pandas_df(id_label="corems:"). Get the exported data as a Pandas DataFrame.
 65    * get_json(nan=False, id_label="corems:"). Get the exported data as a JSON string.
 66    * to_pandas(write_metadata=True, id_label="corems:"). Export the data to a Pandas DataFrame and save it as a pickle file.
 67    * to_excel(write_mode='a', write_metadata=True, id_label="corems:"),
 68        Export the data to an Excel file.
 69    * to_csv(separate_output=False, write_mode="w", write_metadata=True, id_label="corems:").
 70        Export the data to a CSV file.
 71    * to_parquet(write_metadata=True, id_label="corems:").
 72        Export the data to a Parquet file.
 73    * to_hdf(id_label="corems:").
 74        Export the data to an HDF5 file.
 75    * get_data_stats(gcms).
 76        Get statistics about the GCMS data.
 77
 78    """
 79
 80    def __init__(self, out_file_path, gcms):
 81        self.output_file = Path(out_file_path)
 82
 83        self.gcms = gcms
 84
 85        self._init_columns()
 86
 87    def _init_columns(self):
 88        """Initialize the column names for the exported data.
 89
 90        Returns:
 91        -------
 92        list
 93            The list of column names.
 94        """
 95
 96        columns = [
 97            "Sample name",
 98            "Peak Index",
 99            "Retention Time",
100            "Retention Time Ref",
101            "Peak Height",
102            "Peak Area",
103            "Retention index",
104            "Retention index Ref",
105            "Retention Index Score",
106            "Similarity Score",
107            "Spectral Similarity Score",
108            "Compound Name",
109            "Chebi ID",
110            "Kegg Compound ID",
111            "Inchi",
112            "Inchi Key",
113            "Smiles",
114            "Molecular Formula",
115            "IUPAC Name",
116            "Traditional Name",
117            "Common Name",
118            "Derivatization",
119        ]
120
121        if self.gcms.molecular_search_settings.exploratory_mode:
122            columns.extend(
123                [
124                    "Weighted Cosine Correlation",
125                    "Cosine Correlation",
126                    "Stein Scott Similarity",
127                    "Pearson Correlation",
128                    "Spearman Correlation",
129                    "Kendall Tau Correlation",
130                    "Euclidean Distance",
131                    "Manhattan Distance",
132                    "Jaccard Distance",
133                    "DWT Correlation",
134                    "DFT Correlation",
135                ]
136            )
137
138            columns.extend(list(methods_name.values()))
139
140        return columns
141
142    def get_pandas_df(self, id_label="corems:"):
143        """Get the exported data as a Pandas DataFrame.
144
145        Parameters:
146        ----------
147        id_label : str, optional
148            The ID label for the data. Default is "corems:".
149
150        Returns:
151        -------
152        DataFrame
153            The exported data as a Pandas DataFrame.
154        """
155
156        columns = self._init_columns()
157
158        dict_data_list = self.get_list_dict_data(self.gcms)
159
160        df = DataFrame(dict_data_list, columns=columns)
161
162        df.attrs["name"] = self.gcms.sample_name
163
164        return df
165
166    def get_json(self, nan=False, id_label="corems:"):
167        """Get the exported data as a JSON string.
168
169        Parameters:
170        ----------
171        nan : bool, optional
172            Whether to include NaN values in the JSON string. Default is False.
173        id_label : str, optional
174            The ID label for the data. Default is "corems:".
175
176        """
177
178        import json
179
180        dict_data_list = self.get_list_dict_data(self.gcms)
181
182        return json.dumps(
183            dict_data_list, sort_keys=False, indent=4, separators=(",", ": ")
