186    def to_pandas(self, write_metadata=True, id_label="corems:"):
187        """Export the data to a Pandas DataFrame and save it as a pickle file.
188
189        Parameters:
190        ----------
191        write_metadata : bool, optional
192            Whether to write metadata to the output file.
193        id_label : str, optional
194            The ID label for the data.
195        """
196
197        columns = self._init_columns()
198
199        dict_data_list = self.get_list_dict_data(self.gcms)
200
201        df = DataFrame(dict_data_list, columns=columns)
202
203        df.to_pickle(self.output_file.with_suffix(".pkl"))
204
205        if write_metadata:
206            self.write_settings(
207                self.output_file.with_suffix(".pkl"), self.gcms, id_label="corems:"
208            )
209
210    def to_excel(self, write_mode="a", write_metadata=True, id_label="corems:"):
211        """Export the data to an Excel file.
212
213        Parameters:
214        ----------
215        write_mode : str, optional
216            The write mode for the Excel file. Default is 'a' (append).
217        write_metadata : bool, optional
218            Whether to write metadata to the output file. Default is True.
219        id_label : str, optional
220            The ID label for the data. Default is "corems:".
221        """
222
223        out_put_path = self.output_file.with_suffix(".xlsx")
224
225        columns = self._init_columns()
226
227        dict_data_list = self.get_list_dict_data(self.gcms)
228
229        df = DataFrame(dict_data_list, columns=columns)
230
231        if write_mode == "a" and out_put_path.exists():
232            writer = ExcelWriter(out_put_path, engine="openpyxl")
233            # try to open an existing workbook
234            writer.book = load_workbook(out_put_path)
235            # copy existing sheets
236            writer.sheets = dict((ws.title, ws) for ws in writer.book.worksheets)
237            # read existing file
238            reader = read_excel(out_put_path)
239            # write out the new sheet
240            df.to_excel(writer, index=False, header=False, startrow=len(reader) + 1)
241
242            writer.close()
243        else:
244            df.to_excel(
245                self.output_file.with_suffix(".xlsx"), index=False, engine="openpyxl"
246            )
247
248        if write_metadata:
249            self.write_settings(out_put_path, self.gcms, id_label=id_label)
250
251    def to_csv(
252        self,
253        separate_output=False,
254        write_mode="w",
255        write_metadata=True,
256        id_label="corems:",
257    ):
258        """Export the data to a CSV file.
259
260        Parameters:
261        ----------
262        separate_output : bool, optional
263            Whether to separate the output into multiple files. Default is False.
264        write_mode : str, optional
265            The write mode for the CSV file. Default is 'w' (write).
266        write_metadata : bool, optional
267            Whether to write metadata to the output file. Default is True.
268        id_label : str, optional
269            The ID label for the data. Default is "corems:".
270        """
271
272        if separate_output:
273            # set write mode to write
274            # this mode will overwrite the file without warning
275            write_mode = "w"
276        else:
277            # set write mode to append
278            write_mode = "a"
279
280        columns = self._init_columns()
281
282        dict_data_list = self.get_list_dict_data(self.gcms)
283
284        out_put_path = self.output_file.with_suffix(".csv")
285
286        write_header = not out_put_path.exists()
287
288        try:
289            with open(out_put_path, write_mode, newline="") as csvfile:
290                writer = csv.DictWriter(csvfile, fieldnames=columns)
291                if write_header:
292                    writer.writeheader()
293                for data in dict_data_list:
294                    writer.writerow(data)
295
296            if write_metadata:
297                self.write_settings(out_put_path, self.gcms, id_label=id_label)
298
299        except IOError as ioerror:
300            print(ioerror)
301
302    def to_parquet(self, write_metadata=True, id_label="corems:"):
303        """Export the data to a Parquet file.
304
305        Parameters:
306        ----------
307        write_metadata : bool, optional
308            Whether to write metadata to the output file. Default is True.
309        id_label : str, optional
310            The ID label for the data. Default is "corems:".
311
312        Notes
313        -----
314        Requires ``pyarrow`` (or ``fastparquet``) for pandas Parquet I/O.
315        """
316
317        columns = self._init_columns()
318
319        dict_data_list = self.get_list_dict_data(self.gcms)
320
321        df = DataFrame(dict_data_list, columns=columns)
322
323        out_put_path = self.output_file.with_suffix(".parquet")
324        df.to_parquet(out_put_path, index=False)
325
326        if write_metadata:
327            self.write_settings(out_put_path, self.gcms, id_label=id_label)
328
329    def to_hdf(self, id_label="corems:"):
330        """Export the data to an HDF5 file.
331
332        Parameters:
333        ----------
334        id_label : str, optional
335            The ID label for the data. Default is "corems:".
336        """
337
338        # save sample at a time
339        def add_compound(gc_peak, compound_obj):
340            modifier = compound_obj.classify if compound_obj.classify else ""
341            compound_group = compound_obj.name.replace("/", "") + " " + modifier
342
343            if compound_group not in peak_group:
344                compound_group = peak_group.create_group(compound_group)
345
346                # compound_group.attrs["retention_time"] = compound_obj.retention_time
347                compound_group.attrs["retention_index"] = compound_obj.ri
348                compound_group.attrs["retention_index_score"] = compound_obj.ri_score
349                compound_group.attrs["spectral_similarity_score"] = (
350                    compound_obj.spectral_similarity_score
351                )
352                compound_group.attrs["similarity_score"] = compound_obj.similarity_score
353
354                compond_mz = compound_group.create_dataset(
355                    "mz", data=np.array(compound_obj.mz), dtype="f8"
356                )
357                compond_abundance = compound_group.create_dataset(
358                    "abundance", data=np.array(compound_obj.abundance), dtype="f8"
359                )
360
361                if self.gcms.molecular_search_settings.exploratory_mode:
362                    compound_group.attrs["Spectral Similarities"] = json.dumps(
363                        compound_obj.spectral_similarity_scores,
364                        sort_keys=False,
365                        indent=4,
366                        separators=(",", ":"),
367                    )
368            else:
369                warnings.warn("Skipping duplicate reference compound.")
370
371        import json
372        from datetime import datetime, timezone
373
374        import h5py
375        import numpy as np
376
377        output_path = self.output_file.with_suffix(".hdf5")
378
379        with h5py.File(output_path, "w") as hdf_handle:
380            timenow = str(datetime.now(timezone.utc).strftime("%d/%m/%Y %H:%M:%S %Z"))
381            hdf_handle.attrs["time_stamp"] = timenow
382            hdf_handle.attrs["data_structure"] = "gcms"
383            hdf_handle.attrs["analyzer"] = self.gcms.analyzer
384            hdf_handle.attrs["instrument_label"] = self.gcms.instrument_label
385
386            hdf_handle.attrs["sample_id"] = "self.gcms.id"
387            hdf_handle.attrs["sample_name"] = self.gcms.sample_name
388            hdf_handle.attrs["input_data"] = str(self.gcms.file_location)
389            hdf_handle.attrs["output_data"] = str(output_path)
390            hdf_handle.attrs["output_data_id"] = id_label + uuid.uuid4().hex
391            hdf_handle.attrs["corems_version"] = __version__
392
393            hdf_handle.attrs["Stats"] = json.dumps(
394                self.get_data_stats(self.gcms),
395                sort_keys=False,
396                indent=4,
397                separators=(",", ": "),
398            )
399            hdf_handle.attrs["Calibration"] = json.dumps(
400                self.get_calibration_stats(self.gcms, id_label),
401                sort_keys=False,
402                indent=4,
403                separators=(",", ": "),
404            )
405            hdf_handle.attrs["Blank"] = json.dumps(
406                self.get_blank_stats(self.gcms),
407                sort_keys=False,
408                indent=4,
409                separators=(",", ": "),
410            )
411
412            corems_dict_setting = parameter_to_dict.get_dict_data_gcms(self.gcms)
413            hdf_handle.attrs["CoreMSParameters"] = json.dumps(
414                corems_dict_setting, sort_keys=False, indent=4, separators=(",", ": ")
415            )
416
417            scans_dataset = hdf_handle.create_dataset(
418                "scans", data=np.array(self.gcms.scans_number), dtype="f8"
419            )
420            rt_dataset = hdf_handle.create_dataset(
421                "rt", data=np.array(self.gcms.retention_time), dtype="f8"
422            )
423            tic_dataset = hdf_handle.create_dataset(
424                "tic", data=np.array(self.gcms.tic), dtype="f8"
425            )
426            processed_tic_dataset = hdf_handle.create_dataset(
427                "processed_tic", data=np.array(self.gcms.processed_tic), dtype="f8"
428            )
429
430            output_score_method = (
431                self.gcms.molecular_search_settings.output_score_method
432            )
433
434            for gc_peak in self.gcms:
435                # print(gc_peak.retention_time)
436                # print(gc_peak.tic)
437
438                # check if there is a compound candidate
439                peak_group = hdf_handle.create_group(str(gc_peak.retention_time))
440                peak_group.attrs["deconvolution"] = int(
441                    self.gcms.chromatogram_settings.use_deconvolution
442                )
443
444                peak_group.attrs["start_scan"] = gc_peak.start_scan
445                peak_group.attrs["apex_scan"] = gc_peak.apex_scan
446                peak_group.attrs["final_scan"] = gc_peak.final_scan
447
448                peak_group.attrs["retention_index"] = gc_peak.ri
449                peak_group.attrs["retention_time"] = gc_peak.retention_time
450                peak_group.attrs["area"] = gc_peak.area
451
452                mz = peak_group.create_dataset(
453                    "mz", data=np.array(gc_peak.mass_spectrum.mz_exp), dtype="f8"
454                )
455                abundance = peak_group.create_dataset(
456                    "abundance",
457                    data=np.array(gc_peak.mass_spectrum.abundance),
458                    dtype="f8",
459                )
460
461                if gc_peak:
462                    if output_score_method == "highest_sim_score":
463                        compound_obj = gc_peak.highest_score_compound
464                        add_compound(gc_peak, compound_obj)
465
466                    elif output_score_method == "highest_ss":
467                        compound_obj = gc_peak.highest_ss_compound
468                        add_compound(gc_peak, compound_obj)
469
470                    else:
471                        for compound_obj in gc_peak:
472                            add_compound(gc_peak, compound_obj)
473
474    def get_data_stats(self, gcms):
475        """Get statistics about the GCMS data.
476
477        Parameters:
478        ----------
479        gcms : object
480            The low resolution GCMS object.
481
482        Returns:
483        -------
484        dict
485            A dictionary containing the data statistics.
486        """
487
488        matched_peaks = gcms.matched_peaks
489        no_matched_peaks = gcms.no_matched_peaks
490        unique_metabolites = gcms.unique_metabolites
491
492        peak_matchs_above_0p85 = 0
493        unique_peak_match_above_0p85 = 0
494        for match_peak in matched_peaks:
495            gc_peak_above_85 = 0
496            matches_above_85 = list(
497                filter(lambda m: m.similarity_score >= 0.85, match_peak)
498            )
499            if matches_above_85:
500                peak_matchs_above_0p85 += 1
501            if len(matches_above_85) == 1:
502                unique_peak_match_above_0p85 += 1
503
504        data_stats = {}
505        data_stats["average_signal_noise"] = "ni"
506        data_stats["chromatogram_dynamic_range"] = gcms.dynamic_range
507        data_stats["total_number_peaks"] = len(gcms)
508        data_stats["total_peaks_matched"] = len(matched_peaks)
509        data_stats["total_peaks_without_matches"] = len(no_matched_peaks)
510        data_stats["total_matches_above_similarity_score_0.85"] = peak_matchs_above_0p85
511        data_stats["single_matches_above_similarity_score_0.85"] = (
512            unique_peak_match_above_0p85
513        )
514        data_stats["unique_metabolites"] = len(unique_metabolites)
515
516        return data_stats
517
518    def get_calibration_stats(self, gcms, id_label):
519        """Get statistics about the GC-MS calibration.
520

524        calibration_parameters = {}

526        calibration_parameters["calibration_rt_ri_pairs_ref"] = gcms.ri_pairs_ref
527        calibration_parameters["data_url"] = str(gcms.cal_file_path)
528        calibration_parameters["has_input"] = id_label + corems_md5(gcms.cal_file_path)
529        calibration_parameters["data_name"] = str(gcms.cal_file_path.stem)
530        calibration_parameters["calibration_method"] = ""
531
532        return calibration_parameters
533
534    def get_blank_stats(self, gcms):
535        """Get statistics about the GC-MS blank."""
536        blank_parameters = {}
537
538        blank_parameters["data_name"] = "ni"
539        blank_parameters["blank_id"] = "ni"
540        blank_parameters["data_url"] = "ni"
541        blank_parameters["has_input"] = "ni"
542        blank_parameters["common_features_to_blank"] = "ni"
543
544        return blank_parameters
545
546    def get_instrument_metadata(self, gcms):
547        """Get metadata about the GC-MS instrument."""
548        instrument_metadata = {}
549
550        instrument_metadata["analyzer"] = gcms.analyzer
551        instrument_metadata["instrument_label"] = gcms.instrument_label
552        instrument_metadata["instrument_id"] = uuid.uuid4().hex
553
554        return instrument_metadata
555
556    def get_data_metadata(self, gcms, id_label, output_path):
557        """Get metadata about the GC-MS data.
558
559        Parameters:
560        ----------
561        gcms : object
562            The low resolution GCMS object.
563        id_label : str
564            The ID label for the data.
565        output_path : str
566            The output file path.
567
568        Returns:
569        -------
570        dict
571            A dictionary containing the data metadata.
572        """
573        if isinstance(output_path, str):
574            output_path = Path(output_path)
575
576        paramaters_path = output_path.with_suffix(".json")
577
578        if paramaters_path.exists():
579            with paramaters_path.open() as current_param:
580                metadata = json.load(current_param)
581                data_metadata = metadata.get("Data")
582        else:
583            data_metadata = {}
584            data_metadata["data_name"] = []
585            data_metadata["input_data_url"] = []
586            data_metadata["has_input"] = []
587
588        data_metadata["data_name"].append(gcms.sample_name)
589        data_metadata["input_data_url"].append(str(gcms.file_location))
590        data_metadata["has_input"].append(id_label + corems_md5(gcms.file_location))
591
592        data_metadata["output_data_name"] = str(output_path.stem)
593        data_metadata["output_data_url"] = str(output_path)
594        data_metadata["has_output"] = id_label + corems_md5(output_path)
595
596        return data_metadata
597
598    def get_parameters_json(self, gcms, id_label, output_path):
599        """Get the parameters as a JSON string.
600
601        Parameters:
602        ----------
603        gcms : GCMS object
604            The low resolution GCMS object.
605        id_label : str
606            The ID label for the data.
607        output_path : str
608            The output file path.
609
610        Returns:
611        -------
612        str
613            The parameters as a JSON string.
614        """
615
616        output_parameters_dict = {}
617        output_parameters_dict["Data"] = self.get_data_metadata(
618            gcms, id_label, output_path
619        )
620        output_parameters_dict["Stats"] = self.get_data_stats(gcms)
621        output_parameters_dict["Calibration"] = self.get_calibration_stats(
622            gcms, id_label
623        )
624        output_parameters_dict["Blank"] = self.get_blank_stats(gcms)
625        output_parameters_dict["Instrument"] = self.get_instrument_metadata(gcms)
626        corems_dict_setting = parameter_to_dict.get_dict_data_gcms(gcms)
627        corems_dict_setting["corems_version"] = __version__
628        output_parameters_dict["CoreMSParameters"] = corems_dict_setting
629        output_parameters_dict["has_metabolite"] = gcms.metabolites_data
630        output = json.dumps(
631            output_parameters_dict, sort_keys=False, indent=4, separators=(",", ": ")
632        )
633
634        return output
635
636    def write_settings(self, output_path, gcms, id_label="emsl:"):
637        """Write the settings to a JSON file.
638
639        Parameters:
640        ----------
641        output_path : str
642            The output file path.
643        gcms : GCMS object
644            The low resolution GCMS object.
645        id_label : str
646            The ID label for the data. Default is "emsl:".
647
648        """
649
650        output = self.get_parameters_json(gcms, id_label, output_path)
651
652        with open(
653            output_path.with_suffix(".json"),
654            "w",
655            encoding="utf8",
656        ) as outfile:
657            outfile.write(output)
658
659    def get_list_dict_data(self, gcms, include_no_match=True, no_match_inline=False):
660        """Get the exported data as a list of dictionaries.
661
662        Parameters:
663        ----------
664        gcms : object
665            The low resolution GCMS object.
666        include_no_match : bool, optional
667            Whether to include no match data. Default is True.
668        no_match_inline : bool, optional
669            Whether to include no match data inline. Default is False.
670
671        Returns:
672        -------
673        list
674            The exported data as a list of dictionaries.
675        """
676
677        output_score_method = gcms.molecular_search_settings.output_score_method
678
679        dict_data_list = []
680
681        def add_match_dict_data():
682            derivatization = "{}:{}:{}".format(
683                compound_obj.classify,
684                compound_obj.derivativenum,
685                compound_obj.derivatization,
686            )
687            out_dict = {
688                "Sample name": gcms.sample_name,
689                "Peak Index": gcpeak_index,
690                "Retention Time": gc_peak.retention_time,
691                "Retention Time Ref": compound_obj.retention_time,
692                "Peak Height": gc_peak.tic,
693                "Peak Area": gc_peak.area,
694                "Retention index": gc_peak.ri,
695                "Retention index Ref": compound_obj.ri,
696                "Retention Index Score": compound_obj.ri_score,
697                "Spectral Similarity Score": compound_obj.spectral_similarity_score,
698                "Similarity Score": compound_obj.similarity_score,
699                "Compound Name": compound_obj.name,
700                "Chebi ID": compound_obj.metadata.chebi,
701                "Kegg Compound ID": compound_obj.metadata.kegg,
702                "Inchi": compound_obj.metadata.inchi,
703                "Inchi Key": compound_obj.metadata.inchikey,
704                "Smiles": compound_obj.metadata.smiles,
705                "Molecular Formula": compound_obj.formula,
706                "IUPAC Name": compound_obj.metadata.iupac_name,
707                "Traditional Name": compound_obj.metadata.traditional_name,
708                "Common Name": compound_obj.metadata.common_name,
709                "Derivatization": derivatization,
710            }
711
712            if self.gcms.molecular_search_settings.exploratory_mode:
713                out_dict.update(
714                    {
715                        "Weighted Cosine Correlation": compound_obj.spectral_similarity_scores.get(
716                            "weighted_cosine_correlation"
717                        ),
718                        "Cosine Correlation": compound_obj.spectral_similarity_scores.get(
719                            "cosine_correlation"
720                        ),
721                        "Stein Scott Similarity": compound_obj.spectral_similarity_scores.get(
722                            "stein_scott_similarity"
723                        ),
724                        "Pearson Correlation": compound_obj.spectral_similarity_scores.get(
725                            "pearson_correlation"
726                        ),
727                        "Spearman Correlation": compound_obj.spectral_similarity_scores.get(
728                            "spearman_correlation"
729                        ),
730                        "Kendall Tau Correlation": compound_obj.spectral_similarity_scores.get(
731                            "kendall_tau_correlation"
732                        ),
733                        "DFT Correlation": compound_obj.spectral_similarity_scores.get(
734                            "dft_correlation"
735                        ),
736                        "DWT Correlation": compound_obj.spectral_similarity_scores.get(
737                            "dwt_correlation"
738                        ),
739                        "Euclidean Distance": compound_obj.spectral_similarity_scores.get(
740                            "euclidean_distance"
741                        ),
742                        "Manhattan Distance": compound_obj.spectral_similarity_scores.get(
743                            "manhattan_distance"
744                        ),
745                        "Jaccard Distance": compound_obj.spectral_similarity_scores.get(
746                            "jaccard_distance"
747                        ),
748                    }
749                )
750                for method in methods_name:
751                    out_dict[methods_name.get(method)] = (
752                        compound_obj.spectral_similarity_scores.get(method)
753                    )
754
755            dict_data_list.append(out_dict)
756
757        def add_no_match_dict_data():
758            dict_data_list.append(
759                {
760                    "Sample name": gcms.sample_name,
761                    "Peak Index": gcpeak_index,
762                    "Retention Time": gc_peak.retention_time,
763                    "Peak Height": gc_peak.tic,
764                    "Peak Area": gc_peak.area,
765                    "Retention index": gc_peak.ri,
766                }
767            )
768
769        for gcpeak_index, gc_peak in enumerate(gcms.sorted_gcpeaks):
770            # check if there is a compound candidate
771            if gc_peak:
772                if output_score_method == "highest_sim_score":
773                    compound_obj = gc_peak.highest_score_compound
774                    add_match_dict_data()
775
776                elif output_score_method == "highest_ss":
777                    compound_obj = gc_peak.highest_ss_compound
778                    add_match_dict_data()
779
780                else:
781                    for compound_obj in gc_peak:
782                        add_match_dict_data()  # add monoisotopic peak
783
784            else:
785                # include not_match
786                if include_no_match and no_match_inline:
787                    add_no_match_dict_data()
788
789        if include_no_match and not no_match_inline:
790            for gcpeak_index, gc_peak in enumerate(gcms.sorted_gcpeaks):
791                if not gc_peak:
792                    add_no_match_dict_data()
793
794        return dict_data_list

A class to export low resolution GC-MS data.

This class provides methods to export low resolution GC-MS data to various formats such as Excel, CSV, Parquet, HDF5, and Pandas DataFrame.

Parameters:

out_file_path : str The output file path. gcms : object The low resolution GCMS object.

Attributes:

output_file : Path The output file path as a Path object. gcms : object The low resolution GCMS object.

Methods:

  • get_pandas_df(id_label="corems:"). Get the exported data as a Pandas DataFrame.
  • get_json(nan=False, id_label="corems:"). Get the exported data as a JSON string.
  • to_pandas(write_metadata=True, id_label="corems:"). Export the data to a Pandas DataFrame and save it as a pickle file.
  • to_excel(write_mode='a', write_metadata=True, id_label="corems:"), Export the data to an Excel file.
  • to_csv(separate_output=False, write_mode="w", write_metadata=True, id_label="corems:"). Export the data to a CSV file.
  • to_parquet(write_metadata=True, id_label="corems:"). Export the data to a Parquet file.
  • to_hdf(id_label="corems:"). Export the data to an HDF5 file.
  • get_data_stats(gcms). Get statistics about the GCMS data.

def to_csv( self, separate_output=False, write_mode='w', write_metadata=True, id_label='corems:'): 
251    def to_csv(
252        self,
253        separate_output=False,
254        write_mode="w",
255        write_metadata=True,
256        id_label="corems:",
257    ):
258        """Export the data to a CSV file.
259
260        Parameters:
261        ----------
262        separate_output : bool, optional
263            Whether to separate the output into multiple files. Default is False.
264        write_mode : str, optional
265            The write mode for the CSV file. Default is 'w' (write).
266        write_metadata : bool, optional
267            Whether to write metadata to the output file. Default is True.
268        id_label : str, optional
269            The ID label for the data. Default is "corems:".
270        """
271
272        if separate_output:
273            # set write mode to write
274            # this mode will overwrite the file without warning
275            write_mode = "w"
276        else:
277            # set write mode to append
278            write_mode = "a"
279
280        columns = self._init_columns()
281
282        dict_data_list = self.get_list_dict_data(self.gcms)
283
284        out_put_path = self.output_file.with_suffix(".csv")
285
286        write_header = not out_put_path.exists()
287
288        try:
289            with open(out_put_path, write_mode, newline="") as csvfile:
290                writer = csv.DictWriter(csvfile, fieldnames=columns)
291                if write_header:
292                    writer.writeheader()
293                for data in dict_data_list:
294                    writer.writerow(data)
295
296            if write_metadata:
297                self.write_settings(out_put_path, self.gcms, id_label=id_label)
298
299        except IOError as ioerror:
300            print(ioerror)

329    def to_hdf(self, id_label="corems:"):
330        """Export the data to an HDF5 file.
331
332        Parameters:
333        ----------
334        id_label : str, optional
335            The ID label for the data. Default is "corems:".
336        """
337
338        # save sample at a time
339        def add_compound(gc_peak, compound_obj):
340            modifier = compound_obj.classify if compound_obj.classify else ""
341            compound_group = compound_obj.name.replace("/", "") + " " + modifier
342
343            if compound_group not in peak_group:
344                compound_group = peak_group.create_group(compound_group)
345
346                # compound_group.attrs["retention_time"] = compound_obj.retention_time
347                compound_group.attrs["retention_index"] = compound_obj.ri
348                compound_group.attrs["retention_index_score"] = compound_obj.ri_score
349                compound_group.attrs["spectral_similarity_score"] = (
350                    compound_obj.spectral_similarity_score
351                )
352                compound_group.attrs["similarity_score"] = compound_obj.similarity_score
353
354                compond_mz = compound_group.create_dataset(
355                    "mz", data=np.array(compound_obj.mz), dtype="f8"
356                )
357                compond_abundance = compound_group.create_dataset(
358                    "abundance", data=np.array(compound_obj.abundance), dtype="f8"
359                )
360
361                if self.gcms.molecular_search_settings.exploratory_mode:
362                    compound_group.attrs["Spectral Similarities"] = json.dumps(
363                        compound_obj.spectral_similarity_scores,
364                        sort_keys=False,
365                        indent=4,
366                        separators=(",", ":"),
367                    )
368            else:
369                warnings.warn("Skipping duplicate reference compound.")
370
371        import json
372        from datetime import datetime, timezone
373
374        import h5py
375        import numpy as np
376
377        output_path = self.output_file.with_suffix(".hdf5")
378
379        with h5py.File(output_path, "w") as hdf_handle:
380            timenow = str(datetime.now(timezone.utc).strftime("%d/%m/%Y %H:%M:%S %Z"))
381            hdf_handle.attrs["time_stamp"] = timenow
382            hdf_handle.attrs["data_structure"] = "gcms"
383            hdf_handle.attrs["analyzer"] = self.gcms.analyzer
384            hdf_handle.attrs["instrument_label"] = self.gcms.instrument_label
385
386            hdf_handle.attrs["sample_id"] = "self.gcms.id"
387            hdf_handle.attrs["sample_name"] = self.gcms.sample_name
388            hdf_handle.attrs["input_data"] = str(self.gcms.file_location)
389            hdf_handle.attrs["output_data"] = str(output_path)
390            hdf_handle.attrs["output_data_id"] = id_label + uuid.uuid4().hex
391            hdf_handle.attrs["corems_version"] = __version__
392
393            hdf_handle.attrs["Stats"] = json.dumps(
394                self.get_data_stats(self.gcms),
395                sort_keys=False,
396                indent=4,
397                separators=(",", ": "),
398            )
399            hdf_handle.attrs["Calibration"] = json.dumps(
400                self.get_calibration_stats(self.gcms, id_label),
401                sort_keys=False,
402                indent=4,
403                separators=(",", ": "),
404            )
405            hdf_handle.attrs["Blank"] = json.dumps(
406                self.get_blank_stats(self.gcms),
407                sort_keys=False,
408                indent=4,
409                separators=(",", ": "),
410            )
411
412            corems_dict_setting = parameter_to_dict.get_dict_data_gcms(self.gcms)
413            hdf_handle.attrs["CoreMSParameters"] = json.dumps(
414                corems_dict_setting, sort_keys=False, indent=4, separators=(",", ": ")
415            )
416
417            scans_dataset = hdf_handle.create_dataset(
418                "scans", data=np.array(self.gcms.scans_number), dtype="f8"
419            )
420            rt_dataset = hdf_handle.create_dataset(
421                "rt", data=np.array(self.gcms.retention_time), dtype="f8"
422            )
423            tic_dataset = hdf_handle.create_dataset(
424                "tic", data=np.array(self.gcms.tic), dtype="f8"
425            )
426            processed_tic_dataset = hdf_handle.create_dataset(
427                "processed_tic", data=np.array(self.gcms.processed_tic), dtype="f8"
428            )
429
430            output_score_method = (
431                self.gcms.molecular_search_settings.output_score_method
432            )
433
434            for gc_peak in self.gcms:
435                # print(gc_peak.retention_time)
436                # print(gc_peak.tic)
437
438                # check if there is a compound candidate
439                peak_group = hdf_handle.create_group(str(gc_peak.retention_time))
440                peak_group.attrs["deconvolution"] = int(
441                    self.gcms.chromatogram_settings.use_deconvolution
442                )
443
444                peak_group.attrs["start_scan"] = gc_peak.start_scan
445                peak_group.attrs["apex_scan"] = gc_peak.apex_scan
446                peak_group.attrs["final_scan"] = gc_peak.final_scan
447
448                peak_group.attrs["retention_index"] = gc_peak.ri
449                peak_group.attrs["retention_time"] = gc_peak.retention_time
450                peak_group.attrs["area"] = gc_peak.area
451
452                mz = peak_group.create_dataset(
453                    "mz", data=np.array(gc_peak.mass_spectrum.mz_exp), dtype="f8"
454                )
455                abundance = peak_group.create_dataset(
456                    "abundance",
457                    data=np.array(gc_peak.mass_spectrum.abundance),
458                    dtype="f8",
459                )
460
461                if gc_peak:
462                    if output_score_method == "highest_sim_score":
463                        compound_obj = gc_peak.highest_score_compound
464                        add_compound(gc_peak, compound_obj)
465
466                    elif output_score_method == "highest_ss":
467                        compound_obj = gc_peak.highest_ss_compound
468                        add_compound(gc_peak, compound_obj)
469
470                    else:
471                        for compound_obj in gc_peak:
472                            add_compound(gc_peak, compound_obj)

def get_data_stats(self, gcms): 
474    def get_data_stats(self, gcms):
475        """Get statistics about the GCMS data.
476
477        Parameters:
478        ----------
479        gcms : object
480            The low resolution GCMS object.
481
482        Returns:
483        -------
484        dict
485            A dictionary containing the data statistics.
486        """
487
488        matched_peaks = gcms.matched_peaks
489        no_matched_peaks = gcms.no_matched_peaks
490        unique_metabolites = gcms.unique_metabolites
491
492        peak_matchs_above_0p85 = 0
493        unique_peak_match_above_0p85 = 0
494        for match_peak in matched_peaks:
495            gc_peak_above_85 = 0
496            matches_above_85 = list(
497                filter(lambda m: m.similarity_score >= 0.85, match_peak)
498            )
499            if matches_above_85:
500                peak_matchs_above_0p85 += 1
501            if len(matches_above_85) == 1:
502                unique_peak_match_above_0p85 += 1
503
504        data_stats = {}
505        data_stats["average_signal_noise"] = "ni"
506        data_stats["chromatogram_dynamic_range"] = gcms.dynamic_range
507        data_stats["total_number_peaks"] = len(gcms)
508        data_stats["total_peaks_matched"] = len(matched_peaks)
509        data_stats["total_peaks_without_matches"] = len(no_matched_peaks)
510        data_stats["total_matches_above_similarity_score_0.85"] = peak_matchs_above_0p85
511        data_stats["single_matches_above_similarity_score_0.85"] = (
512            unique_peak_match_above_0p85
513        )
514        data_stats["unique_metabolites"] = len(unique_metabolites)
515
516        return data_stats

518    def get_calibration_stats(self, gcms, id_label):
519        """Get statistics about the GC-MS calibration.
520
521        Parameters:

def get_list_dict_data(self, gcms, include_no_match=True, no_match_inline=False): 
659    def get_list_dict_data(self, gcms, include_no_match=True, no_match_inline=False):
660        """Get the exported data as a list of dictionaries.
661
662        Parameters:
663        ----------
664        gcms : object
665            The low resolution GCMS object.
666        include_no_match : bool, optional
667            Whether to include no match data. Default is True.
668        no_match_inline : bool, optional
669            Whether to include no match data inline. Default is False.
670
671        Returns:
672        -------
673        list
674            The exported data as a list of dictionaries.
675        """
676
677        output_score_method = gcms.molecular_search_settings.output_score_method
678
679        dict_data_list = []
680
681        def add_match_dict_data():
682            derivatization = "{}:{}:{}".format(
683                compound_obj.classify,
684                compound_obj.derivativenum,
685                compound_obj.derivatization,
686            )
687            out_dict = {
688                "Sample name": gcms.sample_name,
689                "Peak Index": gcpeak_index,
690                "Retention Time": gc_peak.retention_time,
691                "Retention Time Ref": compound_obj.retention_time,
692                "Peak Height": gc_peak.tic,
693                "Peak Area": gc_peak.area,
694                "Retention index": gc_peak.ri,
695                "Retention index Ref": compound_obj.ri,
696                "Retention Index Score": compound_obj.ri_score,
697                "Spectral Similarity Score": compound_obj.spectral_similarity_score,
698                "Similarity Score": compound_obj.similarity_score,
699                "Compound Name": compound_obj.name,
700                "Chebi ID": compound_obj.metadata.chebi,
701                "Kegg Compound ID": compound_obj.metadata.kegg,
702                "Inchi": compound_obj.metadata.inchi,
703                "Inchi Key": compound_obj.metadata.inchikey,
704                "Smiles": compound_obj.metadata.smiles,
705                "Molecular Formula": compound_obj.formula,
706                "IUPAC Name": compound_obj.metadata.iupac_name,
707                "Traditional Name": compound_obj.metadata.traditional_name,
708                "Common Name": compound_obj.metadata.common_name,
709                "Derivatization": derivatization,
710            }
711
712            if self.gcms.molecular_search_settings.exploratory_mode:
713                out_dict.update(
714                    {
715                        "Weighted Cosine Correlation": compound_obj.spectral_similarity_scores.get(
716                            "weighted_cosine_correlation"
717                        ),
718                        "Cosine Correlation": compound_obj.spectral_similarity_scores.get(
719                            "cosine_correlation"
720                        ),
721                        "Stein Scott Similarity": compound_obj.spectral_similarity_scores.get(
722                            "stein_scott_similarity"
723                        ),
724                        "Pearson Correlation": compound_obj.spectral_similarity_scores.get(
725                            "pearson_correlation"
726                        ),
727                        "Spearman Correlation": compound_obj.spectral_similarity_scores.get(
728                            "spearman_correlation"
729                        ),
730                        "Kendall Tau Correlation": compound_obj.spectral_similarity_scores.get(
731                            "kendall_tau_correlation"
732                        ),
733                        "DFT Correlation": compound_obj.spectral_similarity_scores.get(
734                            "dft_correlation"
735                        ),
736                        "DWT Correlation": compound_obj.spectral_similarity_scores.get(
737                            "dwt_correlation"
738                        ),
739                        "Euclidean Distance": compound_obj.spectral_similarity_scores.get(
740                            "euclidean_distance"
741                        ),
742                        "Manhattan Distance": compound_obj.spectral_similarity_scores.get(
743                            "manhattan_distance"
744                        ),
745                        "Jaccard Distance": compound_obj.spectral_similarity_scores.get(
746                            "jaccard_distance"
747                        ),
748                    }
749                )
750                for method in methods_name:
751                    out_dict[methods_name.get(method)] = (
752                        compound_obj.spectral_similarity_scores.get(method)
753                    )
754
755            dict_data_list.append(out_dict)
756
757        def add_no_match_dict_data():
758            dict_data_list.append(
759                {
760                    "Sample name": gcms.sample_name,
761                    "Peak Index": gcpeak_index,
762                    "Retention Time": gc_peak.retention_time,
763                    "Peak Height": gc_peak.tic,
764                    "Peak Area": gc_peak.area,
765                    "Retention index": gc_peak.ri,
766                }
767            )
768
769        for gcpeak_index, gc_peak in enumerate(gcms.sorted_gcpeaks):
770            # check if there is a compound candidate
771            if gc_peak:
772                if output_score_method == "highest_sim_score":
773                    compound_obj = gc_peak.highest_score_compound
774                    add_match_dict_data()
775
776                elif output_score_method == "highest_ss":
777                    compound_obj = gc_peak.highest_ss_compound
778                    add_match_dict_data()
779
780                else:
781                    for compound_obj in gc_peak:
782                        add_match_dict_data()  # add monoisotopic peak
783
784            else:
785                # include not_match
786                if include_no_match and no_match_inline:
787                    add_no_match_dict_data()
788
789        if include_no_match and not no_match_inline:
790            for gcpeak_index, gc_peak in enumerate(gcms.sorted_gcpeaks):
791                if not gc_peak:
792                    add_no_match_dict_data()
793
794        return dict_data_list

1011    def to_hdf(
1012        self,
1013        overwrite=False,
1014        export_raw=True,
1015        compression=DEFAULT_HDF5_COMPRESSION,
1016        profile_dtype="f4",
1017    ):
1018        """Export the data to an HDF5 file.
1019
1020        Parameters
1021        ----------
1022        overwrite : bool, optional
1023            Whether to overwrite the output file. Default is False.
1024        export_raw : bool, optional
1025            Whether to export the raw mass spectra data. Default is True.
1026        compression : int, str or None, optional
1027            Compression for the written datasets: a gzip level 0-9,
1028            ``"lzf"``, or ``None``/``"none"``. Default is 4. ``"lzf"`` is
1029            h5py's own filter, not a standard HDF5 one -- it needs h5py (or
1030            a tool with the lzf plugin) to read the result back.
1031        profile_dtype : str, optional
1032            dtype used for the stored profile m/z/abundance arrays
1033            (``"f4"`` or ``"f8"``). Default is ``"f4"``.
1034        """
1035        if overwrite:
1036            if self.output_file.with_suffix(".hdf5").exists():
1037                self.output_file.with_suffix(".hdf5").unlink()
1038
1039        with h5py.File(self.output_file.with_suffix(".hdf5"), "a") as hdf_handle:
1040            if not hdf_handle.attrs.get("date_utc"):
1041                # Set metadata for all mass spectra
1042                timenow = str(
1043                    datetime.now(timezone.utc).strftime("%d/%m/%Y %H:%M:%S %Z")
1044                )
1045                hdf_handle.attrs["date_utc"] = timenow
1046                hdf_handle.attrs["filename"] = self.mass_spectra.file_location.name
1047                hdf_handle.attrs["data_structure"] = "mass_spectra"
1048                hdf_handle.attrs["analyzer"] = self.mass_spectra.analyzer
1049                hdf_handle.attrs["instrument_label"] = (
1050                    self.mass_spectra.instrument_label
1051                )
1052                hdf_handle.attrs["sample_name"] = self.mass_spectra.sample_name
1053                hdf_handle.attrs["polarity"] = self.mass_spectra.polarity
1054                hdf_handle.attrs["parser_type"] = (
1055                    self.mass_spectra.spectra_parser_class.__name__
1056                )
1057                hdf_handle.attrs["original_file_location"] = (
1058                    self.mass_spectra.file_location._str
1059                )
1060
1061                # Save creation time from the cached parser when one is configured.
1062                try:
1063                    if (
1064                        getattr(self.mass_spectra, "spectra_parser_class", None)
1065                        is not None
1066                    ):
1067                        parser = self.mass_spectra.spectra_parser
1068                        if parser is not None and hasattr(parser, "get_creation_time"):
1069                            creation_time = parser.get_creation_time()
1070                            if creation_time is not None:
1071                                hdf_handle.attrs["creation_time"] = (
1072                                    creation_time.isoformat()
1073                                )
1074                except Exception:
1075                    pass  # If creation time cannot be retrieved, skip it
1076
1077            if "mass_spectra" not in hdf_handle:
1078                mass_spectra_group = hdf_handle.create_group("mass_spectra")
1079            else:
1080                mass_spectra_group = hdf_handle.get("mass_spectra")
1081
1082            for mass_spectrum in self.mass_spectra:
1083                group_key = str(int(mass_spectrum.scan_number))
1084
1085                self.add_mass_spectrum_to_hdf5(
1086                    hdf_handle,
1087                    mass_spectrum,
1088                    group_key,
1089                    mass_spectra_group,
1090                    export_raw,
1091                    compression=compression,
1092                    profile_dtype=profile_dtype,
1093                )

This constructor should always be called with keyword arguments. Arguments are:

group should be None; reserved for future extension when a ThreadGroup class is implemented.

target is the callable object to be invoked by the run() method. Defaults to None, meaning nothing is called.

name is the thread name. By default, a unique name is constructed of the form "Thread-N" where N is a small decimal number.

args is a list or tuple of arguments for the target invocation. Defaults to ().

kwargs is a dictionary of keyword arguments for the target invocation. Defaults to {}.

If a subclass overrides the constructor, it must make sure to invoke the base class constructor (Thread.__init__()) before doing anything else to the thread.

def to_hdf( self, overwrite=False, export_raw=True, compression=4, profile_dtype='f4'): 
1011    def to_hdf(
1012        self,
1013        overwrite=False,
1014        export_raw=True,
1015        compression=DEFAULT_HDF5_COMPRESSION,
1016        profile_dtype="f4",
1017    ):
1018        """Export the data to an HDF5 file.
1019
1020        Parameters
1021        ----------
1022        overwrite : bool, optional
1023            Whether to overwrite the output file. Default is False.
1024        export_raw : bool, optional
1025            Whether to export the raw mass spectra data. Default is True.
1026        compression : int, str or None, optional
1027            Compression for the written datasets: a gzip level 0-9,
1028            ``"lzf"``, or ``None``/``"none"``. Default is 4. ``"lzf"`` is
1029            h5py's own filter, not a standard HDF5 one -- it needs h5py (or
1030            a tool with the lzf plugin) to read the result back.
1031        profile_dtype : str, optional
1032            dtype used for the stored profile m/z/abundance arrays
1033            (``"f4"`` or ``"f8"``). Default is ``"f4"``.
1034        """
1035        if overwrite:
1036            if self.output_file.with_suffix(".hdf5").exists():
1037                self.output_file.with_suffix(".hdf5").unlink()
1038
1039        with h5py.File(self.output_file.with_suffix(".hdf5"), "a") as hdf_handle:
1040            if not hdf_handle.attrs.get("date_utc"):
1041                # Set metadata for all mass spectra
1042                timenow = str(
1043                    datetime.now(timezone.utc).strftime("%d/%m/%Y %H:%M:%S %Z")
1044                )
1045                hdf_handle.attrs["date_utc"] = timenow
1046                hdf_handle.attrs["filename"] = self.mass_spectra.file_location.name
1047                hdf_handle.attrs["data_structure"] = "mass_spectra"
1048                hdf_handle.attrs["analyzer"] = self.mass_spectra.analyzer
1049                hdf_handle.attrs["instrument_label"] = (
1050                    self.mass_spectra.instrument_label
1051                )
1052                hdf_handle.attrs["sample_name"] = self.mass_spectra.sample_name
1053                hdf_handle.attrs["polarity"] = self.mass_spectra.polarity
1054                hdf_handle.attrs["parser_type"] = (
1055                    self.mass_spectra.spectra_parser_class.__name__
1056                )
1057                hdf_handle.attrs["original_file_location"] = (
1058                    self.mass_spectra.file_location._str
1059                )
1060
1061                # Save creation time from the cached parser when one is configured.
1062                try:
1063                    if (
1064                        getattr(self.mass_spectra, "spectra_parser_class", None)
1065                        is not None
1066                    ):
1067                        parser = self.mass_spectra.spectra_parser
1068                        if parser is not None and hasattr(parser, "get_creation_time"):
1069                            creation_time = parser.get_creation_time()
1070                            if creation_time is not None:
1071                                hdf_handle.attrs["creation_time"] = (
1072                                    creation_time.isoformat()
1073                                )
1074                except Exception:
1075                    pass  # If creation time cannot be retrieved, skip it
1076
1077            if "mass_spectra" not in hdf_handle:
1078                mass_spectra_group = hdf_handle.create_group("mass_spectra")
1079            else:
1080                mass_spectra_group = hdf_handle.get("mass_spectra")
1081
1082            for mass_spectrum in self.mass_spectra:
1083                group_key = str(int(mass_spectrum.scan_number))
1084
1085                self.add_mass_spectrum_to_hdf5(
1086                    hdf_handle,
1087                    mass_spectrum,
1088                    group_key,
1089                    mass_spectra_group,
1090                    export_raw,
1091                    compression=compression,
1092                    profile_dtype=profile_dtype,
1093                )

class LCMSExport(HighResMassSpectraExport): 
1096class LCMSExport(HighResMassSpectraExport):
1097    """A class to export high resolution LC-MS data.
1098
1099    This class provides methods to export high resolution LC-MS data to HDF5
1100    and Parquet (tabular datasets that mirror the main HDF5 groups).
1101
1102    Parameters
1103    ----------
1104    out_file_path : str | Path
1105        The output file path, do not include the file extension.
1106    lcms_object : LCMSBase
1107        The high resolution lc-ms object.
1108    """
1109
1110    def __init__(self, out_file_path, mass_spectra):
1111        super().__init__(out_file_path, mass_spectra, output_type="hdf5")
1112
1113    @staticmethod
1114    def _prepare_df_for_parquet(df):
1115        """Make a DataFrame Parquet-safe by normalizing nested/mixed object values.
1116
1117        Parameters
1118        ----------
1119        df : DataFrame
1120            Input dataframe.
1121
1122        Returns
1123        -------
1124        DataFrame
1125            Copy suitable for ``DataFrame.to_parquet``.
1126
1127        Notes
1128        -----
1129        Object columns with mixed Python types (especially ``bool`` mixed with
1130        ``int``) fail under pyarrow. Nested containers are JSON-serialized;
1131        mixed scalar object columns are coerced to a single type or strings.
1132        """
1133        if df is None or df.empty:
1134            return df
1135
1136        out = df.copy()
1137        out.columns = [str(c) for c in out.columns]
1138
1139        for col in out.columns:
1140            series = out[col]
1141            if series.dtype != object:
1142                continue
1143
1144            def _normalize(value):
1145                if value is None:
1146                    return None
1147                try:
1148                    # Avoid treating array-likes as NA; only scalar NA checks
1149                    if not isinstance(
1150                        value, (list, tuple, dict, np.ndarray)
1151                    ) and pd.isna(value):
1152                        return None
1153                except (TypeError, ValueError):
1154                    pass
1155                if isinstance(value, (list, tuple, dict)):
1156                    return json.dumps(value)
1157                if isinstance(value, np.ndarray):
1158                    return json.dumps(value.tolist())
1159                if isinstance(value, (bool, np.bool_)):
1160                    return bool(value)
1161                if isinstance(value, (np.integer,)):
1162                    return int(value)
1163                if isinstance(value, (np.floating,)):
1164                    return float(value)
1165                return value
1166
1167            normalized = series.map(_normalize)
1168            non_null = [v for v in normalized.tolist() if v is not None]
1169
1170            has_bool = any(isinstance(v, bool) for v in non_null)
1171            # bool is a subclass of int; exclude bools from int detection
1172            has_int = any(
1173                isinstance(v, int) and not isinstance(v, bool) for v in non_null
1174            )
1175            has_float = any(isinstance(v, float) for v in non_null)
1176            has_str = any(isinstance(v, str) for v in non_null)
1177            has_other = any(
1178                not isinstance(v, (bool, int, float, str)) for v in non_null
1179            )
1180
1181            if (
1182                has_other
1183                or (has_str and (has_bool or has_int or has_float))
1184                or (has_bool and has_int)
1185            ):
1186                out[col] = normalized.map(lambda v: None if v is None else str(v))
1187            elif has_bool and not has_float:
1188                out[col] = normalized.map(
1189                    lambda v: None if v is None else bool(v)
1190                ).astype("boolean")
1191            elif has_float or has_int:
1192                out[col] = pd.to_numeric(pd.Series(normalized), errors="coerce")
1193            else:
1194                out[col] = normalized.map(lambda v: None if v is None else str(v))
1195
1196        return out
1197
1198    def _write_parquet(self, df, filename, overwrite=False):
1199        """Write a dataframe to a Parquet file under the export directory.
1200
1201        Parameters
1202        ----------
1203        df : DataFrame
1204            Data to write.
1205        filename : str
1206            File name (with or without ``.parquet`` suffix).
1207        overwrite : bool, optional
1208            Whether to replace an existing file. Default is False.
1209
1210        Returns
1211        -------
1212        Path or None
1213            Output path if written, otherwise None.
1214        """
1215        if df is None or df.empty:
1216            return None
1217
1218        out_path = self.dir_loc / Path(filename).with_suffix(".parquet")
1219        if out_path.exists() and not overwrite:
1220            return out_path
1221
1222        self._prepare_df_for_parquet(df).to_parquet(out_path, index=False)
1223        return out_path
1224
1225    def _mass_spectra_to_parquet_df(self):
1226        """Build a single DataFrame of peak tables for all loaded mass spectra."""
1227        frames = []
1228        for mass_spectrum in self.mass_spectra:
1229            if mass_spectrum is None:
1230                continue
1231            columns = self.columns_label + self.get_all_used_atoms_in_order(
1232                mass_spectrum
1233            )
1234            dict_data_list = self.get_list_dict_data(mass_spectrum)
1235            df = DataFrame(dict_data_list, columns=columns)
1236            if df.empty:
1237                continue
1238            df.insert(0, "scan_number", mass_spectrum.scan_number)
1239            if getattr(mass_spectrum, "retention_time", None) is not None:
1240                df.insert(1, "retention_time", mass_spectrum.retention_time)
1241            frames.append(df)
1242
1243        if not frames:
1244            return DataFrame()
1245        return pd.concat(frames, ignore_index=True)
1246
1247    @staticmethod
1248    def _sequence_len(value):
1249        """Return length of a sequence/array, or 0 for None/empty/scalar-missing."""
1250        if value is None:
1251            return 0
1252        try:
1253            return len(value)
1254        except TypeError:
1255            return 0
1256
1257    def _eics_to_parquet_df(self):
1258        """Build a long-format DataFrame of EIC time series."""
1259        frames = []
1260        for mz, eic_data in self.mass_spectra.eics.items():
1261            if eic_data is None:
1262                continue
1263            # Avoid `array or []` — numpy arrays are ambiguous in boolean context
1264            time = getattr(eic_data, "time", None)
1265            n = self._sequence_len(time)
1266            if n == 0:
1267                continue
1268
1269            scans = getattr(eic_data, "scans", None)
1270            eic = getattr(eic_data, "eic", None)
1271            eic_smoothed = getattr(eic_data, "eic_smoothed", None)
1272
1273            frame = {
1274                "mz": [mz] * n,
1275                "scans": list(scans) if self._sequence_len(scans) == n else [None] * n,
1276                "time": list(time),
1277                "eic": list(eic) if self._sequence_len(eic) == n else [None] * n,
1278            }
1279            if self._sequence_len(eic_smoothed) == n:
1280                frame["eic_smoothed"] = list(eic_smoothed)
1281            frames.append(DataFrame(frame))
1282
1283        if not frames:
1284            return DataFrame()
1285        return pd.concat(frames, ignore_index=True)
1286
1287    def _spectral_search_results_to_parquet_df(self):
1288        """Flatten spectral search results into a single DataFrame."""
1289        frames = []
1290        for scan_id, by_precursor in self.mass_spectra.spectral_search_results.items():
1291            for precursor_key, result in by_precursor.items():
1292                try:
1293                    df = result.to_dataframe()
1294                except Exception:
1295                    continue
1296                if df is None or df.empty:
1297                    continue
1298                df = df.copy()
1299                # to_dataframe() already includes these fields from the result object;
1300                # only set them when missing so we do not insert duplicate columns.
1301                if "query_spectrum_id" not in df.columns:
1302                    df.insert(
1303                        0,
1304                        "query_spectrum_id",
1305                        getattr(result, "query_spectrum_id", scan_id),
1306                    )
1307                if "precursor_mz" not in df.columns:
1308                    loc = 1 if "query_spectrum_id" in df.columns else 0
1309                    df.insert(
1310                        loc,
1311                        "precursor_mz",
1312                        getattr(result, "precursor_mz", precursor_key),
1313                    )
1314                frames.append(df)
1315
1316        if not frames:
1317            return DataFrame()
1318        return pd.concat(frames, ignore_index=True)
1319
1320    def to_parquet(
1321        self,
1322        overwrite=False,
1323        save_parameters=True,
1324        parameter_format="toml",
1325        export_spectra=True,
1326    ):
1327        """Export LC-MS datasets to Parquet files (tabular mirror of ``to_hdf``).
1328
1329        Writes under ``{out_file_path}.corems/``:
1330
1331        - ``scan_info.parquet``
1332        - ``mass_features.parquet``
1333        - ``induced_mass_features.parquet`` (if present)
1334        - ``mass_spectra.parquet`` (optional; all peak tables with scan metadata)
1335        - ``eics.parquet`` (if EICs are present and export is enabled)
1336        - ``spectral_search_results.parquet`` (if search results are present)
1337        - parameters as JSON or TOML when ``save_parameters`` is True
1338
1339        Parameters
1340        ----------
1341        overwrite : bool, optional
1342            Whether to overwrite existing Parquet files. Default is False.
1343        save_parameters : bool, optional
1344            Whether to save processing parameters. Default is True.
1345        parameter_format : str, optional
1346            Parameter file format, ``'json'`` or ``'toml'``. Default is ``'toml'``.
1347        export_spectra : bool, optional
1348            Whether to export loaded mass-spectrum peak tables. Default is True.
1349
1350        Notes
1351        -----
1352        Requires ``pyarrow`` (or ``fastparquet``) for pandas Parquet I/O.
1353        Raw profile arrays and nested HDF5-only blobs are not reproduced in full;
1354        use ``to_hdf`` for a complete self-contained archive.
1355        """
1356        self.dir_loc.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
1357
1358        # Scan metadata (same source as the HDF5 scan_info group)
1359        scan_df = self.mass_spectra.scan_df
1360        if scan_df is not None and not scan_df.empty:
1361            self._write_parquet(
1362                scan_df.reset_index(drop=True), "scan_info", overwrite=overwrite
1363            )
1364
1365        # Mass features
1366        if len(self.mass_spectra.mass_features) > 0:
1367            mf_df = self.mass_spectra.mass_features_to_df().reset_index(drop=False)
1368            self._write_parquet(mf_df, "mass_features", overwrite=overwrite)
1369
1370        if len(getattr(self.mass_spectra, "induced_mass_features", {}) or {}) > 0:
1371            imf_df = self.mass_spectra.mass_features_to_df(
1372                induced_features=True
1373            ).reset_index(drop=False)
1374            self._write_parquet(imf_df, "induced_mass_features", overwrite=overwrite)
1375
1376        # Peak tables for loaded spectra
1377        if export_spectra:
1378            spectra_df = self._mass_spectra_to_parquet_df()
1379            self._write_parquet(spectra_df, "mass_spectra", overwrite=overwrite)
1380
1381        # EICs
1382        export_eics = self.mass_spectra.parameters.lc_ms.export_eics
1383        if export_eics and len(self.mass_spectra.eics) > 0:
1384            eic_df = self._eics_to_parquet_df()
1385            self._write_parquet(eic_df, "eics", overwrite=overwrite)
1386
1387        # Spectral search results
1388        if len(self.mass_spectra.spectral_search_results) > 0:
1389            search_df = self._spectral_search_results_to_parquet_df()
1390            self._write_parquet(
1391                search_df, "spectral_search_results", overwrite=overwrite
1392            )
1393
1394        if save_parameters:
1395            if parameter_format not in ["json", "toml"]:
1396                raise ValueError("parameter_format must be 'json' or 'toml'")
1397            if parameter_format == "json":
1398                dump_lcms_settings_json(
1399                    filename=self.output_file.with_suffix(".json"),
1400                    lcms_obj=self.mass_spectra,
1401                )
1402            elif parameter_format == "toml":
1403                dump_lcms_settings_toml(
1404                    filename=self.output_file.with_suffix(".toml"),
1405                    lcms_obj=self.mass_spectra,
1406                )

1408    @staticmethod
1409    def _save_mass_features_dict_to_hdf5(
1410        mass_features_dict,
1411        mass_features_group,
1412        overwrite=False,
1413        compression=DEFAULT_HDF5_COMPRESSION,
1414    ):
1415        """Save a dictionary of mass features to an HDF5 group.
1416
1417        This is a helper method that can be reused by different export classes.
1418
1419        Parameters
1420        ----------
1421        mass_features_dict : dict
1422            Dictionary of mass features to save, keyed by mass feature ID.
1423        mass_features_group : h5py.Group
1424            The HDF5 group to save the mass features to.
1425        overwrite : bool, optional
1426            Whether to overwrite existing mass features. Default is False.
1427        compression : int, str or None, optional
1428            Compression for the written datasets: a gzip level 0-9,
1429            ``"lzf"``, or ``None``/``"none"``. Default is 4. ``"lzf"`` is
1430            h5py's own filter, not a standard HDF5 one -- it needs h5py (or
1431            a tool with the lzf plugin) to read the result back.
1432        """
1433
1434        # Create group for each mass feature, with key as the mass feature id
1435        for k, v in mass_features_dict.items():
1436            if str(k) not in mass_features_group or overwrite:
1437                if str(k) in mass_features_group and overwrite:
1438                    del mass_features_group[str(k)]
1439                mass_features_group.create_group(str(k))
1440                # Loop through each of the mass feature attributes and add them as attributes (if single value) or datasets (if array)
1441                for k2, v2 in v.__dict__.items():
1442                    if v2 is not None:
1443                        # Check if the attribute is an integer or float and set as an attribute in the mass feature group
1444                        if k2 not in [
1445                            "chromatogram_parent",
1446                            "ms2_mass_spectra",
1447                            "mass_spectrum",
1448                            "_eic_data",
1449                            "ms2_similarity_results",
1450                        ]:
1451                            if k2 == "ms2_scan_numbers":
1452                                array = np.array(v2)
1453                                # Convert int64 to int32
1454                                if array.dtype == np.int64:
1455                                    array = array.astype(np.int32)
1456                                mass_features_group[str(k)].create_dataset(
1457                                    str(k2),
1458                                    data=array,
1459                                    **hdf5_dataset_kwargs(
1460                                        array.shape, compression=compression
1461                                    ),
1462                                )
1463                            elif k2 == "_half_height_width":
1464                                array = np.array(v2)
1465                                # Convert float64 to float32
1466                                if array.dtype == np.float64:
1467                                    array = array.astype(np.float32)
1468                                mass_features_group[str(k)].create_dataset(
1469                                    str(k2),
1470                                    data=array,
1471                                    **hdf5_dataset_kwargs(
1472                                        array.shape, compression=compression
1473                                    ),
1474                                )
1475                            elif k2 == "_ms_deconvoluted_idx":
1476                                array = np.array(v2)
1477                                # Convert int64 to int32
1478                                if array.dtype == np.int64:
1479                                    array = array.astype(np.int32)
1480                                mass_features_group[str(k)].create_dataset(
1481                                    str(k2),
1482                                    data=array,
1483                                    **hdf5_dataset_kwargs(
1484                                        array.shape, compression=compression
1485                                    ),
1486                                )
1487                            elif k2 == "associated_mass_features_deconvoluted":
1488                                array = np.array(v2)
1489                                # Convert int64 to int32
1490                                if array.dtype == np.int64:
1491                                    array = array.astype(np.int32)
1492                                mass_features_group[str(k)].create_dataset(
1493                                    str(k2),
1494                                    data=array,
1495                                    **hdf5_dataset_kwargs(
1496                                        array.shape, compression=compression
1497                                    ),
1498                                )
1499                            elif k2 == "_noise_score":
1500                                array = np.array(v2)
1501                                # Convert float64 to float32
1502                                if array.dtype == np.float64:
1503                                    array = array.astype(np.float32)
1504                                mass_features_group[str(k)].create_dataset(
1505                                    str(k2),
1506                                    data=array,
1507                                    **hdf5_dataset_kwargs(
1508                                        array.shape, compression=compression
1509                                    ),
1510                                )
1511                            elif (
1512                                isinstance(v2, int)
1513                                or isinstance(v2, float)
1514                                or isinstance(v2, str)
1515                                or isinstance(v2, np.integer)
1516                                or isinstance(v2, np.float32)
1517                                or isinstance(v2, np.float64)
1518                                or isinstance(v2, np.bool_)
1519                            ):
1520                                # Convert numpy types to smaller precision for storage
1521                                if isinstance(v2, np.int64):
1522                                    v2 = np.int32(v2)
1523                                elif isinstance(v2, np.float64):
1524                                    v2 = np.float32(v2)
1525                                mass_features_group[str(k)].attrs[str(k2)] = v2

1527    @staticmethod
1528    def _save_eics_dict_to_hdf5(
1529        eics_dict, eics_group, overwrite=False, compression=DEFAULT_HDF5_COMPRESSION
1530    ):
1531        """Save a dictionary of EICs to an HDF5 group.
1532
1533        This is a static helper method that can be reused by different export classes
1534        to save EIC data in a consistent format.
1535
1536        Parameters
1537        ----------
1538        eics_dict : dict
1539            Dictionary of EIC_Data objects, keyed by m/z value.
1540        eics_group : h5py.Group
1541            The HDF5 group to save the EICs to.
1542        overwrite : bool, optional
1543            Whether to overwrite existing EICs. Default is False.
1544        compression : int, str or None, optional
1545            Compression for the written datasets: a gzip level 0-9,
1546            ``"lzf"``, or ``None``/``"none"``. Default is 4. ``"lzf"`` is
1547            h5py's own filter, not a standard HDF5 one -- it needs h5py (or
1548            a tool with the lzf plugin) to read the result back.
1549        """
1550        for mz, eic_data in eics_dict.items():
1551            mz_str = str(mz)
1552            if mz_str not in eics_group or overwrite:
1553                if mz_str in eics_group and overwrite:
1554                    del eics_group[mz_str]
1555                eic_grp = eics_group.create_group(mz_str)
1556                eic_grp.attrs["mz"] = mz
1557
1558                # Save all EIC_Data attributes as datasets
1559                for attr_name, attr_value in eic_data.__dict__.items():
1560                    if attr_value is not None:
1561                        array = np.array(attr_value)
1562                        # Apply data type optimization and compression
1563                        if array.dtype == np.int64:
1564                            array = array.astype(np.int32)
1565                        elif array.dtype == np.float64:
1566                            array = array.astype(np.float32)
1567                        elif array.dtype.str[0:2] == "<U":
1568                            # Convert Unicode strings to UTF-8 encoded strings
1569                            string_data = [str(item) for item in array]
1570                            string_dtype = h5py.string_dtype(encoding="utf-8")
1571                            eic_grp.create_dataset(
1572                                str(attr_name),
1573                                data=string_data,
1574                                dtype=string_dtype,
1575                                **hdf5_dataset_kwargs(
1576                                    array.shape, compression=compression, vlen_str=True
1577                                ),
1578                            )
1579                            continue
1580                        eic_grp.create_dataset(
1581                            str(attr_name),
1582                            data=array,
1583                            **hdf5_dataset_kwargs(array.shape, compression=compression),
1584                        )
1585
1586    def _save_mass_features_to_hdf5(
1587        self,
1588        hdf_handle,
1589        group_name="mass_features",
1590        overwrite=False,
1591        compression=DEFAULT_HDF5_COMPRESSION,
1592    ):
1593        """Save the mass features to the HDF5 file.
1594
1595        Parameters
1596        ----------
1597        hdf_handle : h5py.File
1598            The HDF5 file handle.
1599        group_name : str, optional
1600            The name of the group to save the mass features to. Default is 'mass_features'.
1601        overwrite : bool, optional
1602            Whether to overwrite the group if it exists. Default is False.
1603        compression : int, str or None, optional
1604            Compression for the written datasets: a gzip level 0-9,
1605            ``"lzf"``, or ``None``/``"none"``. Default is 4. ``"lzf"`` is
1606            h5py's own filter, not a standard HDF5 one -- it needs h5py (or
1607            a tool with the lzf plugin) to read the result back.
1608        """
1609        # Determine which mass features to save based on group_name
1610        if group_name == "induced_mass_features":
1611            if len(self.mass_spectra.induced_mass_features) == 0:
1612                return  # No induced mass features to save
1613            mass_features_dict = self.mass_spectra.induced_mass_features
1614        else:
1615            if len(self.mass_spectra.mass_features) == 0:
1616                return  # No mass features to save
1617            mass_features_dict = self.mass_spectra.mass_features
1618
1619        # Add LCMS mass features to hdf5 file
1620        if group_name not in hdf_handle:
1621            mass_features_group = hdf_handle.create_group(group_name)
1622        else:
1623            mass_features_group = hdf_handle.get(group_name)
1624
1625        # Use the static helper method to save the mass features
1626        self._save_mass_features_dict_to_hdf5(
1627            mass_features_dict, mass_features_group, overwrite, compression=compression
1628        )
