class LCMSCollectionExport: 
2697class LCMSCollectionExport:
2698    """A class to export an LCMS collection to HDF5 or Parquet format.
2699
2700    This class provides methods to export collection-level data from multi-sample LC-MS
2701    experiments to HDF5 or Parquet files. It handles the export of metadata, retention time
2702    alignments, cluster assignments, and induced mass features (gap-filled features) across
2703    the collection.
2704
2705    The exporter is designed to work with LCMSCollection objects and complements the individual
2706    LCMSExport class by focusing on collection-wide data rather than individual sample data.
2707
2708    Parameters
2709    ----------
2710    out_file_path : str | Path
2711        The output file path, do not include the file extension. The .hdf5 / .parquet
2712        extensions are added automatically as needed.
2713    mass_spectra_collection : LCMSCollection
2714        The LCMS collection object containing multiple LCMS samples with processed mass features,
2715        alignments, and clustering information.
2716
2717    Attributes
2718    ----------
2719    out_file_path : Path
2720        The output file path as a Path object.
2721    mass_spectra_collection : LCMSCollection
2722        The LCMS collection object to be exported.
2723
2724    Methods
2725    -------
2726    export_to_hdf5(overwrite=False)
2727        Export the LCMS collection to an HDF5 file with collection-level data.
2728    export_to_parquet(overwrite=False)
2729        Export collection-level tabular datasets to Parquet files.
2730
2731    Notes
2732    -----
2733    This class exports collection-level data including:
2734    - Sample manifest (metadata about all samples in the collection)
2735    - Retention time alignment data (if RT alignment has been performed)
2736    - Cluster assignments (consensus mass feature groupings across samples)
2737    - Induced mass features (gap-filled features saved to individual LCMS object HDF5 files)
2738
2739    Individual sample data (mass spectra, mass features, EICs, etc.) should be exported
2740    separately using the LCMSExport class for each LCMS object in the collection.
2741
2742    Examples
2743    --------
2744    Export a collection after clustering and gap-filling:
2745
2746    >>> from corems.mass_spectra.output.export import LCMSCollectionExporter
2747    >>> exporter = LCMSCollectionExporter("my_collection", lcms_collection)
2748    >>> exporter.export_to_hdf5(overwrite=True)
2749
2750    The resulting HDF5 file will contain collection-level metadata and can be used
2751    to reconstruct the collection state for further analysis.
2752
2753    See Also
2754    --------
2755    LCMSExport : Export individual LCMS objects to HDF5
2756    LCMSCollection : The collection object being exported
2757    """
2758
2759    def __init__(self, out_file_path, mass_spectra_collection):
2760        self.out_file_path = Path(out_file_path)
2761        self.mass_spectra_collection = mass_spectra_collection
2762
2763    def export_to_hdf5(
2764        self,
2765        overwrite=False,
2766        save_parameters=True,
2767        parameter_format="toml",
2768        update_lcms_objects=True,
2769    ):
2770        """Export the LCMS collection to an HDF5 file.
2771
2772        This method saves the collection-level data to an HDF5 file, including:
2773        - Basic metadata (date, folder location, gap-filling status)
2774        - Sample manifest
2775        - Retention time alignments (if available)
2776        - Cluster assignments (if available)
2777        - Induced mass features for each LCMS object (if gap-filling was performed)
2778
2779        Individual LCMS objects in the collection are not exported by this method.
2780        Use LCMSExport for exporting individual LCMS objects.
2781
2782        Parameters
2783        ----------
2784        overwrite : bool, optional
2785            If True, overwrites the output file if it already exists and replaces
2786            existing groups within the HDF5 file. If False, appends new data to
2787            existing file without overwriting existing groups. Default is False.
2788        save_parameters : bool, optional
2789            If True, saves the collection-level parameters to a separate file in the specified format.
2790            Default is True.
2791        parameter_format : str, optional
2792            The format for saving parameters, either "json" or "toml". Default is "toml".
2793        update_lcms_objects : bool, optional
2794            If True, updates the individual LCMS object HDF5 files with new raw file locations and any additional
2795            information produced during the processing of the collection (e.g. cluster mass feature associations). Default is True.
2796
2797        Notes
2798        -----
2799        The HDF5 file structure includes:
2800        - Attributes: date_utc, lcms_objects_folder, missing_mass_features_searched, manifest
2801        - Groups: rt_alignments, cluster_assignments (if available)
2802
2803        Induced mass features are saved to the individual LCMS object HDF5 files
2804        within the .corems folder structure, not in the collection-level HDF5 file.
2805
2806        Examples
2807        --------
2808        >>> exporter = LCMSCollectionExporter("my_collection", lcms_collection)
2809        >>> exporter.export_to_hdf5(overwrite=True)
2810        """
2811        if overwrite:
2812            if self.out_file_path.with_suffix(".hdf5").exists():
2813                self.out_file_path.with_suffix(".hdf5").unlink()
2814
2815        with h5py.File(self.out_file_path.with_suffix(".hdf5"), "a") as hdf_handle:
2816            # Add basic attributes to the HDF5 file, always overwrite these
2817            timenow = str(datetime.now(timezone.utc).strftime("%d/%m/%Y %H:%M:%S %Z"))
2818            hdf_handle.attrs["date_utc"] = timenow
2819            hdf_handle.attrs["lcms_objects_folder"] = str(
2820                self.mass_spectra_collection.collection_parser.folder_location
2821            )
2822            hdf_handle.attrs["missing_mass_features_searched"] = (
2823                self.mass_spectra_collection.missing_mass_features_searched
2824            )
2825            hdf_handle.attrs["rt_aligned"] = self.mass_spectra_collection.rt_aligned
2826            hdf_handle.attrs["rt_alignment_attempted"] = (
2827                self.mass_spectra_collection.rt_alignment_attempted
2828            )
2829
2830            # Add the manifest to the HDF5 file, always overwrite this
2831            hdf_handle.attrs["manifest"] = self._convert_manifest_to_json()
2832
2833            # Save retention time alignments if they exist, only overwrite if specified
2834            self._save_rt_alignments_to_hdf5(hdf_handle, overwrite)
2835
2836            # Save cluster assignments if they exist, only overwrite if specified
2837            self._save_cluster_assignments_to_hdf5(hdf_handle, overwrite)
2838
2839            # Save consensus feature-group labels if present
2840            self._save_feature_group_labels_to_hdf5(hdf_handle, overwrite)
2841
2842        # Save new raw file locations to each LCMS object's HDF5 file if needed
2843        if (
2844            hasattr(self.mass_spectra_collection, "raw_files_relocated")
2845            and self.mass_spectra_collection.raw_files_relocated
2846        ):
2847            self._update_raw_file_locations_in_hdf5()
2848
2849        # Save induced mass features to the collection with associations to each individual, only if lcms_collection.missing_mass_features_searched is True
2850        if self.mass_spectra_collection.missing_mass_features_searched:
2851            self._save_induced_mass_features_to_hdf5(overwrite)
2852            # Save EICs for induced mass features at collection level
2853            self._save_induced_eics_to_hdf5(overwrite)
2854
2855        # Build cluster mass feature map to know which features to update
2856        # This uses the same logic as process_consensus_features to determine loaded features
2857        cluster_mf_map = self._build_cluster_mf_map()
2858
2859        # Save updated mass features for each LCMS object
2860        # This implements selective update: only loaded features are updated, non-cluster features are preserved
2861        if update_lcms_objects:
2862            self._save_lcms_objects_to_hdf5(cluster_mf_map, overwrite)
2863
2864        # Save collection-level parameters as separate file
2865        if save_parameters:
2866            # Check if parameter_format is valid
2867            if parameter_format not in ["json", "toml"]:
2868                raise ValueError("parameter_format must be 'json' or 'toml'")
2869
2870            if parameter_format == "json":
2871                dump_lcms_collection_settings_json(
2872                    filename=self.out_file_path.with_suffix(".json"),
2873                    lcms_collection=self.mass_spectra_collection,
2874                )
2875            elif parameter_format == "toml":
2876                dump_lcms_collection_settings_toml(
2877                    filename=self.out_file_path.with_suffix(".toml"),
2878                    lcms_collection=self.mass_spectra_collection,
2879                )
2880
2881    def export_to_parquet(
2882        self, overwrite=False, save_parameters=True, parameter_format="toml"
2883    ):
2884        """Export collection-level LC-MS datasets to Parquet files.
2885
2886        Writes next to ``out_file_path`` (same stem as the HDF5 export):
2887
2888        - ``{stem}_manifest.parquet`` — sample manifest
2889        - ``{stem}_cluster_assignments.parquet`` — cluster labels (if present)
2890        - ``{stem}_mass_features.parquet`` — collection mass-features table (if present)
2891        - ``{stem}_rt_alignments.parquet`` — RT alignment curves (if aligned)
2892        - parameters as JSON or TOML when ``save_parameters`` is True
2893
2894        Parameters
2895        ----------
2896        overwrite : bool, optional
2897            Whether to overwrite existing Parquet files. Default is False.
2898        save_parameters : bool, optional
2899            Whether to save collection parameters. Default is True.
2900        parameter_format : str, optional
2901            Parameter file format, ``'json'`` or ``'toml'``. Default is ``'toml'``.
2902
2903        Notes
2904        -----
2905        Requires ``pyarrow`` (or ``fastparquet``) for pandas Parquet I/O.
2906        This is a tabular companion to ``export_to_hdf5``; it does not replace
2907        per-sample HDF5 archives or gap-fill side effects on individual LCMS files.
2908        """
2909        stem = self.out_file_path
2910
2911        def _write(df, suffix):
2912            if df is None or df.empty:
2913                return
2914            out_path = Path(f"{stem}_{suffix}").with_suffix(".parquet")
2915            if out_path.exists() and not overwrite:
2916                return
2917            LCMSExport._prepare_df_for_parquet(df).to_parquet(out_path, index=False)
2918
2919        # Manifest — prefer the tidy samples-as-rows dataframe
2920        manifest_df = getattr(self.mass_spectra_collection, "manifest_dataframe", None)
2921        if manifest_df is None or getattr(manifest_df, "empty", True):
2922            manifest = getattr(
2923                self.mass_spectra_collection, "manifest", None
2924            ) or getattr(
2925                getattr(self.mass_spectra_collection, "collection_parser", None),
2926                "manifest",
2927                None,
2928            )
2929            if isinstance(manifest, DataFrame):
2930                manifest_df = manifest
2931            elif isinstance(manifest, dict) and manifest:
2932                try:
2933                    # Collection manifests are sample -> attrs; transpose to rows
2934                    manifest_df = pd.DataFrame(manifest).T
2935                except ValueError:
2936                    manifest_df = DataFrame(
2937                        [{"manifest_json": self._convert_manifest_to_json()}]
2938                    )
2939            else:
2940                manifest_df = None
2941
2942        if manifest_df is not None and not manifest_df.empty:
2943            _write(manifest_df.reset_index(drop=False), "manifest")
2944
2945        # Cluster assignments / mass features table
2946        mf_df = getattr(self.mass_spectra_collection, "mass_features_dataframe", None)
2947        if mf_df is not None and not mf_df.empty:
2948            _write(mf_df.reset_index(drop=False), "mass_features")
2949            if "cluster" in mf_df.columns:
2950                cluster_df = mf_df[["cluster"]].copy().reset_index(drop=False)
2951                _write(cluster_df, "cluster_assignments")
2952
2953        # RT alignments as long-format table
2954        if getattr(self.mass_spectra_collection, "rt_aligned", False) and getattr(
2955            self.mass_spectra_collection, "rt_alignments", None
2956        ):
2957            frames = []
2958            for (
2959                sample_idx,
2960                alignment_data,
2961            ) in self.mass_spectra_collection.rt_alignments.items():
2962                arr = np.asarray(alignment_data)
2963                if arr.ndim == 1:
2964                    frames.append(
2965                        DataFrame(
2966                            {
2967                                "sample_idx": sample_idx,
2968                                "point": np.arange(len(arr)),
2969                                "value": arr,
2970                            }
2971                        )
2972                    )
2973                elif arr.ndim == 2 and arr.shape[1] >= 2:
2974                    frames.append(
2975                        DataFrame(
2976                            {
2977                                "sample_idx": sample_idx,
2978                                "rt_original": arr[:, 0],
2979                                "rt_aligned": arr[:, 1],
2980                            }
2981                        )
2982                    )
2983                else:
2984                    frames.append(
2985                        DataFrame(
2986                            {
2987                                "sample_idx": [sample_idx],
2988                                "alignment_json": [json.dumps(arr.tolist())],
2989                            }
2990                        )
2991                    )
2992            if frames:
2993                _write(pd.concat(frames, ignore_index=True), "rt_alignments")
2994
2995        if save_parameters:
2996            if parameter_format not in ["json", "toml"]:
2997                raise ValueError("parameter_format must be 'json' or 'toml'")
2998            if parameter_format == "json":
2999                dump_lcms_collection_settings_json(
3000                    filename=self.out_file_path.with_suffix(".json"),
3001                    lcms_collection=self.mass_spectra_collection,
3002                )
3003            elif parameter_format == "toml":
3004                dump_lcms_collection_settings_toml(
3005                    filename=self.out_file_path.with_suffix(".toml"),
3006                    lcms_collection=self.mass_spectra_collection,
3007                )
3008
3009    def _save_rt_alignments_to_hdf5(self, hdf_handle, overwrite):
3010        """Save retention time alignments to HDF5 file."""
3011        # If no rt_alignments, return early
3012        if not self.mass_spectra_collection.rt_aligned:
3013            return
3014
3015        # If rt_alignments exist, save them
3016        if self.mass_spectra_collection.rt_aligned:
3017            group_name = "rt_alignments"
3018            # grab dictionary of rt_alignments
3019            rt_alignments = self.mass_spectra_collection.rt_alignments
3020
3021        if rt_alignments:
3022            # Check if group exists and handle overwrite logic
3023            if group_name in hdf_handle:
3024                if not overwrite:
3025                    return
3026                del hdf_handle[group_name]
3027
3028            grp = hdf_handle.create_group(group_name)
3029
3030            # Save each alignment as a dataset
3031            for sample_idx, alignment_data in rt_alignments.items():
3032                grp.create_dataset(str(sample_idx), data=alignment_data)
3033
3034    def _convert_manifest_to_json(self):
3035        """Clean the manifest for export to HDF5."""
3036        manifest = self.mass_spectra_collection.collection_parser.manifest
3037
3038        # Process the manifest to convert numpy.bool_ or bool values for the 'use_rt_alignment' key
3039        def convert_bool_values(data):
3040            if isinstance(data, dict):
3041                # Process each key-value pair recursively
3042                return {
3043                    k: (
3044                        int(v)
3045                        if k == "use_rt_alignment" and isinstance(v, (bool, np.bool_))
3046                        else convert_bool_values(v)
3047                    )
3048                    for k, v in data.items()
3049                }
3050            elif isinstance(data, list):
3051                # Recursively process lists
3052                return [convert_bool_values(item) for item in data]
3053            else:
3054                # Return non-dict/list types unchanged
3055                return data
3056
3057        # Clean the whole manifest
3058        cleaned_manifest = convert_bool_values(manifest)
3059
3060        # Serialize the cleaned manifest into JSON format
3061        json_manifest = json.dumps(cleaned_manifest)
3062        return json_manifest
3063
3064    def _save_cluster_assignments_to_hdf5(self, hdf_handle, overwrite):
3065        """Save cluster assignments to HDF5 file."""
3066        # Check if column "cluster" is present in self.mass_features_dataframe
3067        if "cluster" in self.mass_spectra_collection.mass_features_dataframe.columns:
3068            group_name = "cluster_assignments"
3069            cluster_assignments = self.mass_spectra_collection.mass_features_dataframe[
3070                ["cluster"]
3071            ].copy()
3072
3073            # Check if group exists and handle overwrite logic
3074            if group_name in hdf_handle:
3075                if not overwrite:
3076                    return
3077                del hdf_handle[group_name]
3078
3079            grp = hdf_handle.create_group(group_name)
3080
3081            # Save the index, converting strings to bytes.
3082            # Avoid Index.astype(str).values under pandas 3 string/CoW semantics;
3083            # build a plain numpy bytes array instead.
3084            index_bytes = np.asarray(
3085                [str(x).encode("utf-8") for x in cluster_assignments.index],
3086                dtype="S",
3087            )
3088            grp.create_dataset("index", data=index_bytes)
3089
3090            # Save the "cluster" column
3091            grp.create_dataset(
3092                "cluster", data=cluster_assignments["cluster"].to_numpy()
3093            )
3094
3095    def _save_feature_group_labels_to_hdf5(self, hdf_handle, overwrite):
3096        """Save cluster-indexed feature-group labels to the collection HDF5."""
3097        from corems.mass_spectra.calc.feature_grouping import GROUP_COLUMNS
3098
3099        labels = getattr(self.mass_spectra_collection, "feature_group_dataframe", None)
3100        if labels is None or len(labels) == 0:
3101            return
3102
3103        group_name = "feature_group_labels"
3104        if group_name in hdf_handle:
3105            if not overwrite:
3106                return
3107            del hdf_handle[group_name]
3108
3109        grp = hdf_handle.create_group(group_name)
3110        index_vals = np.asarray(
3111            [int(x) for x in labels.index],
3112            dtype=np.int64,
3113        )
3114        grp.create_dataset("cluster", data=index_vals)
3115
3116        for col in GROUP_COLUMNS:
3117            if col not in labels.columns:
3118                continue
3119            series = labels[col]
3120            if col in ("feature_group_id", "mono_cluster_id"):
3121                # Nullable ints → float with NaN for missing
3122                data = series.astype("Float64").to_numpy(dtype=float)
3123                grp.create_dataset(col, data=data)
3124            else:
3125                # Object / string columns
3126                encoded = np.asarray(
3127                    [
3128                        (
3129                            b""
3130                            if v is None
3131                            or (isinstance(v, float) and np.isnan(v))
3132                            or (hasattr(pd, "isna") and pd.isna(v))
3133                            else str(v).encode("utf-8")
3134                        )
3135                        for v in series.tolist()
3136                    ],
3137                    dtype="S",
3138                )
3139                grp.create_dataset(col, data=encoded)
3140
3141    def _build_cluster_mf_map(self):
3142        """Build a mapping of which mass features should be saved for each sample.
3143
3144        This uses the same logic as process_consensus_features to determine which
3145        mass features were loaded and should be updated in HDF5 files.
3146
3147        Returns
3148        -------
3149        dict
3150            Dictionary mapping sample_id to list of tuples (mf_id, cluster_id).
3151            Only includes samples that have loaded representative features.
3152            Returns empty dict if no clusters exist.
3153
3154        Notes
3155        -----
3156        This follows the DRY principle by using the same get_sample_mf_map_for_representatives
3157        method used by process_consensus_features and ReadSavedLCMSCollection.
3158        """
3159        # Check if clusters exist
3160        if (
3161            "cluster"
3162            not in self.mass_spectra_collection.mass_features_dataframe.columns
3163        ):
3164            return {}
3165
3166        # Check if cluster_summary_dataframe exists (needed by get_sample_mf_map_for_representatives)
3167        if (
3168            not hasattr(self.mass_spectra_collection, "cluster_summary_dataframe")
3169            or self.mass_spectra_collection.cluster_summary_dataframe is None
3170        ):
3171            return {}
3172
3173        # Use the same DRY helper method that process_consensus_features uses
3174        # This ensures consistency across the codebase
3175        cluster_mf_map = (
3176            self.mass_spectra_collection.get_sample_mf_map_for_representatives(
3177                include_cluster_id=True
3178            )
3179        )
3180
3181        return cluster_mf_map
3182
3183    def _update_raw_file_locations_in_hdf5(self):
3184        """Update raw file locations in each LCMS object's HDF5 file.
3185
3186        This method updates the 'original_file_location' attribute in each LCMS object's
3187        HDF5 file to reflect the new raw file location after files have been relocated.
3188        """
3189        for lcms_obj in self.mass_spectra_collection:
3190            # Get the HDF5 file path for this LCMS object
3191            hdf5_path = lcms_obj.file_location.with_suffix(".hdf5")
3192
3193            if hdf5_path.exists():
3194                with h5py.File(hdf5_path, "a") as hdf_handle:
3195                    # Update the original_file_location attribute
3196                    if "original_file_location" in hdf_handle.attrs:
3197                        hdf_handle.attrs["original_file_location"] = str(
3198                            lcms_obj.raw_file_location
3199                        )
3200                    # If the attribute does not exist, create it
3201                    else:
3202                        hdf_handle.attrs.create(
3203                            "original_file_location", str(lcms_obj.raw_file_location)
3204                        )
3205
3206    def _save_induced_mass_features_to_hdf5(self, overwrite):
3207        """Save induced mass features to the collection HDF5 file.
3208
3209        Induced mass features are gap-filled features that only exist at the collection level.
3210        They are saved with full detail (all attributes and datasets) in the collection HDF5 file
3211        and distributed to individual LCMS objects when the collection is loaded.
3212
3213        The induced mass features are stored in the collection's induced_mass_features_dataframe
3214        and are regenerated as LCMSMassFeature objects for saving.
3215
3216        Parameters
3217        ----------
3218        overwrite : bool
3219            If True, overwrites existing induced mass features group. If False, skips if group exists.
3220        """
3221        # Check if we have any induced mass features to save
3222        if (
3223            self.mass_spectra_collection.induced_mass_features_dataframe is None
3224            or self.mass_spectra_collection.induced_mass_features_dataframe.empty
3225        ):
3226            return
3227
3228        # Open the collection HDF5 file to save induced mass features
3229        with h5py.File(self.out_file_path.with_suffix(".hdf5"), "a") as hdf_handle:
3230            group_name = "induced_mass_features"
3231
3232            # Check if group exists and handle overwrite logic
3233            if group_name in hdf_handle:
3234                if not overwrite:
3235                    return
3236                del hdf_handle[group_name]
3237
3238            # Create top-level group for induced mass features
3239            imf_group = hdf_handle.create_group(group_name)
3240
3241            # Get the induced mass features dataframe
3242            induced_df = self.mass_spectra_collection.induced_mass_features_dataframe
3243
3244            # Get unique sample IDs from the dataframe
3245            sample_ids = induced_df["sample_id"].unique()
3246
3247            # Iterate through each sample and save its induced mass features
3248            for sample_id in sample_ids:
3249                # Filter dataframe to this sample
3250                sample_df = induced_df[induced_df["sample_id"] == sample_id].copy()
3251
3252                if sample_df.empty:
3253                    continue
3254
3255                # Regenerate mass features from the dataframe
3256                regenerated_features = self._regenerate_mass_features_from_sample_df(
3257                    sample_df, sample_id
3258                )
3259
3260                if not regenerated_features:
3261                    continue
3262
3263                # Create a subgroup for this sample's induced mass features
3264                sample_group = imf_group.create_group(str(sample_id))
3265
3266                # Use the static helper method from LCMSExport to save the mass features
3267                LCMSExport._save_mass_features_dict_to_hdf5(
3268                    regenerated_features, sample_group, overwrite=overwrite
3269                )
3270
3271    def _save_induced_eics_to_hdf5(self, overwrite):
3272        """Save EICs for induced mass features to the collection HDF5 file.
3273
3274        Induced mass features are gap-filled features created during process_consensus_features.
3275        Their associated EICs need to be saved at the collection level so they can be reloaded.
3276
3277        The induced mass features are identified from the collection's induced_mass_features_dataframe,
3278        and their EICs are retrieved from the individual LCMS objects.
3279
3280        Parameters
3281        ----------
3282        overwrite : bool
3283            If True, overwrites existing induced EICs group. If False, skips if group exists.
3284        """
3285        # Check if we have any induced mass features to save
3286        if (
3287            self.mass_spectra_collection.induced_mass_features_dataframe is None
3288            or self.mass_spectra_collection.induced_mass_features_dataframe.empty
3289        ):
3290            return
3291
3292        # Open the collection HDF5 file to save induced EICs
3293        with h5py.File(self.out_file_path.with_suffix(".hdf5"), "a") as hdf_handle:
3294            group_name = "induced_eics"
3295
3296            # Check if group exists and handle overwrite logic
3297            if group_name in hdf_handle:
3298                if not overwrite:
3299                    return
3300                del hdf_handle[group_name]
3301
3302            # Create top-level group for induced EICs
3303            induced_eics_group = hdf_handle.create_group(group_name)
3304
3305            # Get the induced mass features dataframe
3306            induced_df = self.mass_spectra_collection.induced_mass_features_dataframe
3307
3308            # Get unique sample IDs from the dataframe
3309            sample_ids = induced_df["sample_id"].unique()
3310
3311            # Iterate through each sample and save EICs for its induced mass features
3312            for sample_id in sample_ids:
3313                lcms_obj = self.mass_spectra_collection[sample_id]
3314
3315                # Filter dataframe to this sample
3316                sample_df = induced_df[induced_df["sample_id"] == sample_id].copy()
3317
3318                if sample_df.empty:
3319                    continue
3320
3321                # Collect EICs for induced mass features using _eic_mz from dataframe
3322                induced_eics = {}
3323                for _, row in sample_df.iterrows():
3324                    # Get the EIC m/z from the dataframe
3325                    eic_mz = row.get("_eic_mz")
3326
3327                    if eic_mz is not None and pd.notna(eic_mz):
3328                        # Try to get the EIC from the LCMS object
3329                        if (
3330                            hasattr(lcms_obj, "eics")
3331                            and lcms_obj.eics
3332                            and eic_mz in lcms_obj.eics
3333                        ):
3334                            induced_eics[eic_mz] = lcms_obj.eics[eic_mz]
3335
3336                if not induced_eics:
3337                    continue
3338
3339                # Create a subgroup for this sample's induced EICs
3340                sample_group = induced_eics_group.create_group(str(sample_id))
3341
3342                # Use the static helper method from LCMSExport to save the EICs
3343                LCMSExport._save_eics_dict_to_hdf5(
3344                    induced_eics, sample_group, overwrite
3345                )
3346
3347    def _regenerate_mass_features_from_sample_df(self, sample_df, sample_id):
3348        """Regenerate induced mass features from a sample-specific dataframe.
3349
3350        This method creates LCMSMassFeature objects from rows in the induced_mass_features_dataframe
3351        for a specific sample. The regenerated features are used for saving to HDF5.
3352
3353        Parameters
3354        ----------
3355        sample_df : pd.DataFrame
3356            DataFrame containing induced mass features for a specific sample.
3357        sample_id : int
3358            The sample ID (index in the collection).
3359
3360        Returns
3361        -------
3362        dict
3363            Dictionary of regenerated LCMSMassFeature objects keyed by feature ID.
3364        """
3365        from corems.chroma_peak.factory.chroma_peak_classes import LCMSMassFeature
3366
3367        if sample_df.empty:
3368            return {}
3369
3370        # Get the corresponding LCMS object for proper parent reference
3371        lcms_obj = self.mass_spectra_collection[sample_id]
3372
3373        # Regenerate mass features from the dataframe
3374        regenerated_features = {}
3375
3376        for _, row in sample_df.iterrows():
3377            # Extract the original ID from mf_id (format: c{cluster}_{index}_i)
3378            # This is the ID used in lcms_obj.induced_mass_features dict
3379            original_id = row["mf_id"]
3380
3381            # Create a new LCMSMassFeature with proper parent reference
3382            # Note: dataframe uses 'scan_time' but __init__ parameter is 'retention_time'
3383            mass_feature = LCMSMassFeature(
3384                lcms_parent=lcms_obj,
3385                mz=row["mz"],
3386                retention_time=row["scan_time"],  # Column is 'scan_time' in dataframe
3387                intensity=row["intensity"],
3388                apex_scan=int(row["apex_scan"]),
3389                persistence=row.get("persistence", None)
3390                if "persistence" in row
3391                else None,
3392                id=original_id,  # Use the original string ID from gap-filling
3393            )
3394
3395            # Set additional attributes dynamically from dataframe columns
3396            # Skip columns already handled in __init__ or structural metadata
3397            skip_cols = {
3398                "sample_id",
3399                "mf_id",
3400                "mz",
3401                "scan_time",
3402                "scan_time_aligned",
3403                "intensity",
3404                "apex_scan",
3405                "persistence",
3406            }
3407
3408            # Iterate through all columns and set via property setters
3409            for col_name in row.index:
3410                if col_name in skip_cols:
3411                    continue
3412                value = row[col_name]
3413                try:
3414                    if pd.isna(value):
3415                        continue
3416                except (TypeError, ValueError):
3417                    pass  # value is array-like; not NA, proceed
3418
3419                # Set via property (public interface handles private attributes)
3420                # Don't save empty lists
3421                if isinstance(value, list) and len(value) == 0:
3422                    continue
3423                try:
3424                    setattr(mass_feature, col_name, value)
3425                except (AttributeError, TypeError):
3426                    pass  # Skip attributes that don't exist or can't be set
3427
3428            # Set cluster_index if present
3429            if "cluster" in row and pd.notna(row["cluster"]):
3430                mass_feature.cluster_index = int(row["cluster"])
3431
3432            regenerated_features[mass_feature.id] = mass_feature
3433
3434        return regenerated_features
3435
3436    def _save_lcms_objects_to_hdf5(self, cluster_mf_map, overwrite):
3437        """Save updated mass features for each LCMS object.
3438
3439        This method implements a "selective update" strategy for mass features:
3440        - For mass features specified in cluster_mf_map (loaded representatives), we selectively
3441          update them by deleting their old entries and re-saving with new attributes.
3442        - Non-cluster features (not loaded) are never touched/overwritten.
3443
3444        Note: EICs are NOT saved here. Induced feature EICs are saved at the collection level.
3445
3446        Parameters
3447        ----------
3448        cluster_mf_map : dict
3449            Dictionary mapping sample_id to list of tuples (mf_id, cluster_id).
3450            This explicitly defines which mass features should be updated.
3451        overwrite : bool
3452            If True, allows overwriting of existing data. If False, skips if data exists.
3453        """
3454        for sample_id, lcms_obj in enumerate(self.mass_spectra_collection):
3455            hdf5_path = lcms_obj.file_location.with_suffix(".hdf5")
3456
3457            if not hdf5_path.exists():
3458                # If HDF5 doesn't exist, we can't do selective update, raise error
3459                raise FileNotFoundError(
3460                    f"HDF5 file for LCMS object {lcms_obj.sample_name} not found at {hdf5_path}"
3461                )
3462
3463            # Check if this sample has any loaded features in the map
3464            if sample_id not in cluster_mf_map or not cluster_mf_map[sample_id]:
3465                # Nothing loaded for this sample, nothing to update
3466                continue
3467
3468            # Extract mf_ids from the map (cluster_mf_map contains tuples of (mf_id, cluster_id))
3469            mf_ids_to_update = [
3470                mf_id for mf_id, cluster_id in cluster_mf_map[sample_id]
3471            ]
3472
3473            # Perform selective update of mass features
3474            self._selective_update_mass_features(
3475                lcms_obj, hdf5_path, mf_ids_to_update, overwrite
3476            )
3477
3478            # Save any new mass spectra that were added during processing
3479            self._save_new_mass_spectra(lcms_obj, hdf5_path, overwrite)
3480
3481    def _save_new_mass_spectra(self, lcms_obj, hdf5_path, overwrite):
3482        """Save new mass spectra that were added during processing.
3483
3484        This method checks what mass spectra are in lcms_obj._ms and saves any
3485        that aren't already in the HDF5 file's mass_spectra group. Uses the
3486        existing add_mass_spectrum_to_hdf5 method for consistency with original
3487        export logic.
3488
3489        Parameters
3490        ----------
3491        lcms_obj : LCMSBase
3492            The LCMS object with potentially new mass spectra.
3493        hdf5_path : Path
3494            Path to the HDF5 file.
3495        overwrite : bool
3496            If True, allows overwriting existing spectra.
3497        """
3498        # Check if there are any mass spectra to save
3499        if not hasattr(lcms_obj, "_ms") or not lcms_obj._ms:
3500            return
3501
3502        # Create an LCMS exporter instance for this LCMS object
3503        # This gives us access to add_mass_spectrum_to_hdf5 method inherited from HighResMassSpecExport
3504        # Turn hdf5_path into str without suffix for LCMSExport
3505        hdf5_path_str = str(hdf5_path.with_suffix(""))
3506        exporter = LCMSExport(out_file_path=hdf5_path_str, mass_spectra=lcms_obj)
3507
3508        # Open HDF5 file and check existing mass spectra
3509        with h5py.File(hdf5_path, "a") as hdf_handle:
3510            # Create mass_spectra group if it doesn't exist
3511            if "mass_spectra" not in hdf_handle:
3512                ms_group = hdf_handle.create_group("mass_spectra")
3513                existing_scan_numbers = set()
3514            else:
3515                ms_group = hdf_handle["mass_spectra"]
3516                existing_scan_numbers = set(int(k) for k in ms_group.keys())
3517
3518            # Find new mass spectra (in _ms but not in HDF5)
3519            new_scan_numbers = set(lcms_obj._ms.keys()) - existing_scan_numbers
3520
3521            if not new_scan_numbers:
3522                return
3523
3524            # Save new mass spectra using existing add_mass_spectrum_to_hdf5 method
3525            export_profile = lcms_obj.parameters.lc_ms.export_profile_spectra
3526            for scan_number in new_scan_numbers:
3527                mass_spec = lcms_obj._ms[scan_number]
3528                scan_group_name = str(scan_number)
3529
3530                # Delete existing group if overwrite is True
3531                if scan_group_name in ms_group and overwrite:
3532                    del ms_group[scan_group_name]
3533                elif scan_group_name in ms_group:
3534                    continue
3535
3536                # Use the existing method from HighResMassSpecExport
3537                exporter.add_mass_spectrum_to_hdf5(
3538                    hdf_handle=hdf_handle,
3539                    mass_spectrum=mass_spec,
3540                    group_key=scan_group_name,
3541                    mass_spectra_group=ms_group,
3542                    export_raw=export_profile,
3543                )
3544
3545    def _selective_update_mass_features(
3546        self, lcms_obj, hdf5_path, mf_ids_to_update, overwrite
3547    ):
3548        """Selectively update mass features in HDF5 file.
3549
3550        This method deletes only the mass features specified in mf_ids_to_update,
3551        then re-saves them with their potentially updated attributes. Non-cluster features
3552        in the HDF5 file are left untouched.
3553
3554        Parameters
3555        ----------
3556        lcms_obj : LCMSBase
3557            The LCMS object with mass features to update.
3558        hdf5_path : Path
3559            Path to the HDF5 file.
3560        mf_ids_to_update : list of int
3561            List of mass feature IDs that should be updated. This explicitly defines
3562            which features were loaded and should be saved.
3563        overwrite : bool
3564            If True, allows overwriting. If False, skips if group exists.
3565        """
3566        if not mf_ids_to_update:
3567            return
3568
3569        # Open HDF5 file and delete specified feature IDs, then re-save
3570        with h5py.File(hdf5_path, "a") as hdf_handle:
3571            if "mass_features" not in hdf_handle:
3572                return
3573
3574            mf_group = hdf_handle["mass_features"]
3575
3576            # Delete features that are being updated
3577            for feature_id in mf_ids_to_update:
3578                feature_id_str = str(feature_id)
3579                if feature_id_str in mf_group:
3580                    del mf_group[feature_id_str]
3581
3582            # Re-save updated features (only those that exist in mass_features dict)
3583            updated_features = {
3584                mf.id: mf
3585                for mf in lcms_obj.mass_features.values()
3586                if mf.id in mf_ids_to_update
3587            }
3588
3589            if updated_features:
3590                LCMSExport._save_mass_features_dict_to_hdf5(
3591                    updated_features, mf_group, overwrite=overwrite
3592                )

A class to export an LCMS collection to HDF5 or Parquet format.

This class provides methods to export collection-level data from multi-sample LC-MS experiments to HDF5 or Parquet files. It handles the export of metadata, retention time alignments, cluster assignments, and induced mass features (gap-filled features) across the collection.

The exporter is designed to work with LCMSCollection objects and complements the individual LCMSExport class by focusing on collection-wide data rather than individual sample data.

Parameters
  • out_file_path (str | Path): The output file path, do not include the file extension. The .hdf5 / .parquet extensions are added automatically as needed.
  • mass_spectra_collection (LCMSCollection): The LCMS collection object containing multiple LCMS samples with processed mass features, alignments, and clustering information.
Attributes
  • out_file_path (Path): The output file path as a Path object.
  • mass_spectra_collection (LCMSCollection): The LCMS collection object to be exported.
Methods

export_to_hdf5(overwrite=False) Export the LCMS collection to an HDF5 file with collection-level data. export_to_parquet(overwrite=False) Export collection-level tabular datasets to Parquet files.

Notes

This class exports collection-level data including:

  • Sample manifest (metadata about all samples in the collection)
  • Retention time alignment data (if RT alignment has been performed)
  • Cluster assignments (consensus mass feature groupings across samples)
  • Induced mass features (gap-filled features saved to individual LCMS object HDF5 files)

Individual sample data (mass spectra, mass features, EICs, etc.) should be exported separately using the LCMSExport class for each LCMS object in the collection.

Examples

Export a collection after clustering and gap-filling:

>>> from corems.mass_spectra.output.export import LCMSCollectionExporter
>>> exporter = LCMSCollectionExporter("my_collection", lcms_collection)
>>> exporter.export_to_hdf5(overwrite=True)

The resulting HDF5 file will contain collection-level metadata and can be used to reconstruct the collection state for further analysis.

See Also

LCMSExport: Export individual LCMS objects to HDF5
LCMSCollection: The collection object being exported

2772        This method saves the collection-level data to an HDF5 file, including:
2773        - Basic metadata (date, folder location, gap-filling status)
2774        - Sample manifest
2775        - Retention time alignments (if available)
2776        - Cluster assignments (if available)
2777        - Induced mass features for each LCMS object (if gap-filling was performed)

2780        Use LCMSExport for exporting individual LCMS objects.

2785            If True, overwrites the output file if it already exists and replaces

2793        update_lcms_objects : bool, optional

2796
2797        Notes
2798        -----
2799        The HDF5 file structure includes:
2800        - Attributes: date_utc, lcms_objects_folder, missing_mass_features_searched, manifest
2801        - Groups: rt_alignments, cluster_assignments (if available)
2802
2803        Induced mass features are saved to the individual LCMS object HDF5 files
2804        within the .corems folder structure, not in the collection-level HDF5 file.
2805
2806        Examples
2807        --------
2808        >>> exporter = LCMSCollectionExporter("my_collection", lcms_collection)
2809        >>> exporter.export_to_hdf5(overwrite=True)
2810        """
2811        if overwrite:
2812            if self.out_file_path.with_suffix(".hdf5").exists():
2813                self.out_file_path.with_suffix(".hdf5").unlink()
2814
2815        with h5py.File(self.out_file_path.with_suffix(".hdf5"), "a") as hdf_handle:
2816            # Add basic attributes to the HDF5 file, always overwrite these
2817            timenow = str(datetime.now(timezone.utc).strftime("%d/%m/%Y %H:%M:%S %Z"))
2818            hdf_handle.attrs["date_utc"] = timenow
2819            hdf_handle.attrs["lcms_objects_folder"] = str(
2820                self.mass_spectra_collection.collection_parser.folder_location
2821            )
2822            hdf_handle.attrs["missing_mass_features_searched"] = (
2823                self.mass_spectra_collection.missing_mass_features_searched
2824            )
2825            hdf_handle.attrs["rt_aligned"] = self.mass_spectra_collection.rt_aligned
2826            hdf_handle.attrs["rt_alignment_attempted"] = (
2827                self.mass_spectra_collection.rt_alignment_attempted
2828            )
2829
2830            # Add the manifest to the HDF5 file, always overwrite this
2831            hdf_handle.attrs["manifest"] = self._convert_manifest_to_json()
2832
2833            # Save retention time alignments if they exist, only overwrite if specified
2834            self._save_rt_alignments_to_hdf5(hdf_handle, overwrite)
2835
2836            # Save cluster assignments if they exist, only overwrite if specified
2837            self._save_cluster_assignments_to_hdf5(hdf_handle, overwrite)
2838
2839            # Save consensus feature-group labels if present
2840            self._save_feature_group_labels_to_hdf5(hdf_handle, overwrite)
2841
2842        # Save new raw file locations to each LCMS object's HDF5 file if needed
2843        if (
2844            hasattr(self.mass_spectra_collection, "raw_files_relocated")
2845            and self.mass_spectra_collection.raw_files_relocated
2846        ):
2847            self._update_raw_file_locations_in_hdf5()
2848
2849        # Save induced mass features to the collection with associations to each individual, only if lcms_collection.missing_mass_features_searched is True
2850        if self.mass_spectra_collection.missing_mass_features_searched:

Export the LCMS collection to an HDF5 file.

This method saves the collection-level data to an HDF5 file, including:

  • Basic metadata (date, folder location, gap-filling status)
  • Sample manifest
  • Retention time alignments (if available)
  • Cluster assignments (if available)
  • Induced mass features for each LCMS object (if gap-filling was performed)

Individual LCMS objects in the collection are not exported by this method. Use LCMSExport for exporting individual LCMS objects.

Parameters
  • overwrite (bool, optional): If True, overwrites the output file if it already exists and replaces existing groups within the HDF5 file. If False, appends new data to existing file without overwriting existing groups. Default is False.
  • save_parameters (bool, optional): If True, saves the collection-level parameters to a separate file in the specified format. Default is True.
  • parameter_format (str, optional): The format for saving parameters, either "json" or "toml". Default is "toml".
  • update_lcms_objects (bool, optional): If True, updates the individual LCMS object HDF5 files with new raw file locations and any additional information produced during the processing of the collection (e.g. cluster mass feature associations). Default is True.
Notes

The HDF5 file structure includes:

  • Attributes: date_utc, lcms_objects_folder, missing_mass_features_searched, manifest
  • Groups: rt_alignments, cluster_assignments (if available)

Induced mass features are saved to the individual LCMS object HDF5 files within the .corems folder structure, not in the collection-level HDF5 file.

Examples
>>> exporter = LCMSCollectionExporter("my_collection", lcms_collection)
>>> exporter.export_to_hdf5(overwrite=True)
def export_to_parquet(self, overwrite=False, save_parameters=True, parameter_format='toml'): 
2881    def export_to_parquet(
2882        self, overwrite=False, save_parameters=True, parameter_format="toml"
2883    ):
2884        """Export collection-level LC-MS datasets to Parquet files.
2885
2886        Writes next to ``out_file_path`` (same stem as the HDF5 export):
2887
2888        - ``{stem}_manifest.parquet`` — sample manifest
2889        - ``{stem}_cluster_assignments.parquet`` — cluster labels (if present)
2890        - ``{stem}_mass_features.parquet`` — collection mass-features table (if present)
2891        - ``{stem}_rt_alignments.parquet`` — RT alignment curves (if aligned)
2892        - parameters as JSON or TOML when ``save_parameters`` is True
2893
2894        Parameters
2895        ----------
2896        overwrite : bool, optional
2897            Whether to overwrite existing Parquet files. Default is False.
2898        save_parameters : bool, optional
2899            Whether to save collection parameters. Default is True.
2900        parameter_format : str, optional
2901            Parameter file format, ``'json'`` or ``'toml'``. Default is ``'toml'``.
2902
2903        Notes
2904        -----
2905        Requires ``pyarrow`` (or ``fastparquet``) for pandas Parquet I/O.
2906        This is a tabular companion to ``export_to_hdf5``; it does not replace
2907        per-sample HDF5 archives or gap-fill side effects on individual LCMS files.
2908        """
2909        stem = self.out_file_path
2910
2911        def _write(df, suffix):
2912            if df is None or df.empty:
2913                return
2914            out_path = Path(f"{stem}_{suffix}").with_suffix(".parquet")
2915            if out_path.exists() and not overwrite:
2916                return
2917            LCMSExport._prepare_df_for_parquet(df).to_parquet(out_path, index=False)
2918
2919        # Manifest — prefer the tidy samples-as-rows dataframe
2920        manifest_df = getattr(self.mass_spectra_collection, "manifest_dataframe", None)
2921        if manifest_df is None or getattr(manifest_df, "empty", True):
2922            manifest = getattr(
2923                self.mass_spectra_collection, "manifest", None
2924            ) or getattr(
2925                getattr(self.mass_spectra_collection, "collection_parser", None),
2926                "manifest",
2927                None,
2928            )
2929            if isinstance(manifest, DataFrame):
2930                manifest_df = manifest
2931            elif isinstance(manifest, dict) and manifest:
2932                try:
2933                    # Collection manifests are sample -> attrs; transpose to rows
2934                    manifest_df = pd.DataFrame(manifest).T
2935                except ValueError:
2936                    manifest_df = DataFrame(
2937                        [{"manifest_json": self._convert_manifest_to_json()}]
2938                    )
2939            else:
2940                manifest_df = None
2941
2942        if manifest_df is not None and not manifest_df.empty:
2943            _write(manifest_df.reset_index(drop=False), "manifest")
2944
2945        # Cluster assignments / mass features table
2946        mf_df = getattr(self.mass_spectra_collection, "mass_features_dataframe", None)
2947        if mf_df is not None and not mf_df.empty:
2948            _write(mf_df.reset_index(drop=False), "mass_features")
2949            if "cluster" in mf_df.columns:
2950                cluster_df = mf_df[["cluster"]].copy().reset_index(drop=False)
2951                _write(cluster_df, "cluster_assignments")
2952
2953        # RT alignments as long-format table
2954        if getattr(self.mass_spectra_collection, "rt_aligned", False) and getattr(
2955            self.mass_spectra_collection, "rt_alignments", None
2956        ):
2957            frames = []
2958            for (
2959                sample_idx,
2960                alignment_data,
2961            ) in self.mass_spectra_collection.rt_alignments.items():
2962                arr = np.asarray(alignment_data)
2963                if arr.ndim == 1:
2964                    frames.append(
2965                        DataFrame(
2966                            {
2967                                "sample_idx": sample_idx,
2968                                "point": np.arange(len(arr)),
2969                                "value": arr,
2970                            }
2971                        )
2972                    )
2973                elif arr.ndim == 2 and arr.shape[1] >= 2:
2974                    frames.append(
2975                        DataFrame(
2976                            {
2977                                "sample_idx": sample_idx,
2978                                "rt_original": arr[:, 0],
2979                                "rt_aligned": arr[:, 1],
2980                            }
2981                        )
2982                    )
2983                else:
2984                    frames.append(
2985                        DataFrame(
2986                            {
2987                                "sample_idx": [sample_idx],
2988                                "alignment_json": [json.dumps(arr.tolist())],
2989                            }
2990                        )
2991                    )
2992            if frames:
2993                _write(pd.concat(frames, ignore_index=True), "rt_alignments")
2994
2995        if save_parameters:
2996            if parameter_format not in ["json", "toml"]:
2997                raise ValueError("parameter_format must be 'json' or 'toml'")
2998            if parameter_format == "json":
2999                dump_lcms_collection_settings_json(
3000                    filename=self.out_file_path.with_suffix(".json"),
3001                    lcms_collection=self.mass_spectra_collection,
3002                )
3003            elif parameter_format == "toml":
3004                dump_lcms_collection_settings_toml(
3005                    filename=self.out_file_path.with_suffix(".toml"),
3006                    lcms_collection=self.mass_spectra_collection,
3007                )

Export collection-level LC-MS datasets to Parquet files.

Writes next to out_file_path (same stem as the HDF5 export):

  • {stem}_manifest.parquet — sample manifest
  • {stem}_cluster_assignments.parquet — cluster labels (if present)
  • {stem}_mass_features.parquet — collection mass-features table (if present)
  • {stem}_rt_alignments.parquet — RT alignment curves (if aligned)
  • parameters as JSON or TOML when save_parameters is True
Parameters
  • overwrite (bool, optional): Whether to overwrite existing Parquet files. Default is False.
  • save_parameters (bool, optional): Whether to save collection parameters. Default is True.
  • parameter_format (str, optional): Parameter file format, 'json' or 'toml'. Default is 'toml'.
Notes

Requires pyarrow (or fastparquet) for pandas Parquet I/O. This is a tabular companion to export_to_hdf5; it does not replace per-sample HDF5 archives or gap-fill side effects on individual LCMS files.
